    <scene_description>She turns to him , icepick in hand , smiles .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>For my book.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She turns back to the ice , works on it with the pick . She raises her arm , plunges it . Raises it , plunges it . He watches her .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( wary . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What kind of questions?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She puts the icepick down , pours herself a drink , turns to him .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>How does it feel to kill someone?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He looks at her a long beat .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( finally . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You tell me.</dialogue>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't know. But you do.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Their eyes are on each other .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( finally . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It was an accident. They got in the line of fire.</dialogue>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Four shootings in five years. All accidents.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a long beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>They were drug buys. I was a vice cop.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A long beat , as they look at each other .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Tell me about Professor Goldstein.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BEAT .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>There's a name from the past.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>You want a name from the present? How about Hazel Dobkins?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She looks at him a long beat , sips her drink , never takes her eyes off him .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Noah was my counselor in my freshman year.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( she smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That's probably where I got the idea for the icepick. For my book. Funny how the subconscious works.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hazel is my friend.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>She wiped out her whole family.</dialogue>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. She's helped me understand homicidal impulse.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Did n't you study it in school?</dialogue>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Only in theory.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( she smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You know all about homicidal impulse, do n't you, shooter? Not in theory - in practice.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He stares at her a long beat .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <parenthetical>( quietly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What happened, Nick? Did you get sucked into it? Did you like it too much?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He stares at her , almost horrified .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <parenthetical>( quietly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Tell me about the coke, Nick. The day you shot those two tourists - how much coke did you do?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She steps closer to him .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Tell me, Nick.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She puts her hand softly on his cheek , He grabs her hand roughly , holds it .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>I did n't.</dialogue>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, you did. They never tested you, did they? But Internal Affairs knew.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They are face to face . He is still holding her roughly by the hand .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>Your wife knew, did n't she? She knew what was going on. Nicky got too close to the flame. Nicky liked it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He twists her arm back behind her - their bodies are pressed against each other - their eyes digging into each other .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <parenthetical>( in a whisper . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That's why she killed herself?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He is twisting her arm , staring at her , pulling her against him . We hear the DOOR behind them . A beat , and he lets her go , turns away from her . Roxy stands there , staring at them . Her hair is up . She wears a black motorcycle jacket , a black T - shirt , and black jeans and cowboy boots .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <parenthetical>( brightly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hiya, hon. You two have met, have n't you?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Roxy looks at Nick . Catherine goes to her , kisses her briefly on the lips , stands there with her arm around her - both of them looking at Nick . He walks by them , opens the door to go , his face a mask .</scene_description>
    <character>CATHERINE</character>
    <dialogue>You're going to make a terrific character, Nick.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He does n't look at her ; he 's gone .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BETH GARDNER'S OFFICE - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He comes in . He looks like he 's going to kill someone . A RECEPTIONIST sits there .</scene_description>
    <character>RECEPTIONIST</character>
    <dialogue>She's on the phone - she'll be right with you, detective - He sweeps by her into Beth's inner office. She hangs up when she sees the look on his face.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Who has access to my file?</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>What are you talking about, Nick - what's wrong with you?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Who's got access to my goddamn file?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She gets up - he goes closer to her ; she backs away from him .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>Nobody.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He goes closer to her ; she backs away .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>It's a confidential psychiatric record, it'd be illegal - She backs into a wall. She looks very scared. He comes very close to her - puts an arm behind her to the wall.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't, Beth. Do n't lie to me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She says nothing , looks scared .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( suddenly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's Internal Affairs, is n't it?</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>No, Nick, please -</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( loud , hard . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Who?</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( blurts it . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Nilsen.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE INTERNAL AFFAIRS DIVISION - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He storms into the big room . He sees MARTY NILSEN . He is sitting behind his desk in his glass - enclosed office inside this big room . About a dozen plainclothes policemen are in the big room . He goes by them into Nilsen 's office .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. MARTIN NILSEN'S OFFICE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He closes the door . Nilsen sees the look on his face , backs his chair away towards the wall .</scene_description>
    <character>NILSEN</character>
    <dialogue>What do you want, Curran?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He goes to him , picks him up by his lapels , slams him against the wall .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( out of control . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You sold her the file, did n't you?</dialogue>
    <character>NILSEN</character>
    <parenthetical>( scared . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What are you talking about?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( out of control . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What'd she pay you?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He slams him against the wall again . The glass EXPLODES behind them - a chair comes into the room . Nick is frozen , holding Nilsen by the throat against the wall .</scene_description>
    <character>ONE OF THE I.A. GUYS</character>
    <dialogue>Let him go, Curran. Nice and easy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He looks back , sees two Internal Affairs men with their guns drawn , pointed at him . A beat , and he lets Nilsen go . He turns calmly and starts to walk out .</scene_description>
    <character>NILSEN</character>
    <dialogue>You're on sick leave, Shooter. As of right now. Pending the outcome of a psychiatric evaluation.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE POLICE PARKING LOT - DUSK</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He gets into his old Porsche . He STARTS the car up . Gus Moran comes up to the window . They look at each other a</scene_description>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>What's goin' down, son?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Nothin'.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'll be okay, pop.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They look at each other a long beat .</scene_description>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>No, sir. You wo n't. There's smoke off yonder on the horizon. They're gon na want your badge.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a long beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I got tired of being played with.</dialogue>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You sure got real conclusive ways of demonstrating that.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They almost smile at each other , then -</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( almost to himself . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She knows where I live and breathe. She's coming after me.</dialogue>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a long beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What is it you got between you?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat ; to himself . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I do n't know.</dialogue>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>Somethin', though.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A beat , and then Nick looks at him .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Somethin'.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. HIS APARTMENT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He sits in front of the TV , watching a lame sitcom . A bottle of Jack Daniels is half - empty in front of him . He is smoking a cigarette .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( behind him . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I still have my key.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He looks at her , looks away at the sitcom .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't want to see you, Beth.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He keeps watching the sitcom . A long beat .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( suddenly angry . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Damnit! Do n't shut me out! You owe me more than that?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He goes to the TV , shuts it off .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't owe you anything ; you do n't owe me anything.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( he looks at her . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>We went to bed - what was it? - ten or fifteen times?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( he smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It was n't memorable enough to carry any obligations.</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a long beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sometimes I really hate you.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yeah? Well why do n't you find some friendly therapist and work some of that hostility out.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But take my advice. Put a little more life into it than you usually do.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A beat , and she suddenly hurls herself at him in absolute fury , trying to claw at his face . He grabs her , blocks her . They look at each other a long beat and then he lets her go . The emotion of the moment is gone now - they turn away from each other .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( finally . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm sorry. I do n't usually. act like that.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Nick looks at her a beat .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>How could you let him have my file, Beth?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A long beat , then -</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( not looking at him . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>He was going to recommend your discharge a behavioral disability. I made a deal with him. He could review the session notes himself. It was the only way I could keep you on the force.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She looks at him . He looks away from her .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>You did it for me.</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. I care about you. I did it for you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns away from her .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( quietly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Get out of here, Beth.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Please?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He goes to the Jack Daniel 's , pours some more . She looks at him pour it and turns to go .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. HIS APARTMENT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He is asleep on the couch - the TV is on to a blank screen . The Jack Daniel 's is mostly gone . The phone on the coffee table RINGS . It RINGS again . He wakes , picks it up , listens .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Okay.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He hangs it up . He sits there a long beat , staring . He looks disturbed .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE ALLEY BEHIND THE TEN-FOUR BAR - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He walks down the alley . There are lots of police cars , flashing lights , uniformed men , coroner 's men . As he walks down the alley , he sees Lt. Walker , Gus , and several of the Internal Affairs men we saw earlier in Nilsen 's office . They are standing around a Lincoln Town Car . They look at him as he comes closer to them - then move aside . He can see into the car now . Martin Nilsen lies against the front seat . He has been shot in the head . Nick stares .</scene_description>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>One shot. Close range. Probably a.38 caliber revolver.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Nick stares at Nilsen 's body . They watch him .</scene_description>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <dialogue>Give me your gun, Nick.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A beat , and then Nick gives him his gun . Walker smells it , shakes his head , gives it to one of the Internal Affairs men .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( to Walker . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You think I -</dialogue>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't son, but I got the minority opinion.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. POLICE INTERROGATION ROOM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He sits in the same room that Catherine sat in - surrounded by four or five Internal Affairs men , Lt. Walker , Gus , and Captain Talcott . Lt. Walker and Gus sort of sit back - I.A. is running the investigation . The same police stenographer - the same plain young woman - is sitting in the room who was there with Catherine .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Okay. I went after him. I lost my temper.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Do you have any evidence that he showed your psychiatric file to anyone?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Beth Gardner comes into the room . They look at her .</scene_description>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>We'll speak to you afterwards, Dr. Gardner.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Nick gives her a look .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>I'd like to sit - in if you do n't mind.</dialogue>
    <character>THE I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>I'd really rather -</dialogue>
    <character>TALCOTT</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't see anything wrong with Dr. Gardner sitting - in if Detective Curran does n't object.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Nick looks at her , shrugs .</scene_description>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Where were you tonight?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Home. Watching TV.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>All night?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Were you drinking?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He looks at Beth .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah, I was drinking.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>When did you start drinking again?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A couple days ago.</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>I saw Detective Curran at his apartment around ten o'clock. He was sober and lucid. I asked him in my capacity as his departmental therapist about his altercation with Lt. Nilsen. He expressed regret and displayed no hostility.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( to Beth . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How long were you at his apartment?</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>About fifteen minutes. I saw there was no reason for my concern and left.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She and Nick look at each other . He looks away and lights a cigarette .</scene_description>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>There's no smoking in this building.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What are you gon na do - charge me with smoking?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>It is the exact line that Catherine used . A long beat .</scene_description>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <dialogue>I'll ask you once, Nick - for the record did you kill him?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>No.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They look at him a beat .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Come on - I'm going to storm into his office in front of everybody in the afternoon and then that night I'm going to kill him? I'd have to be really dumb to do that.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Going after him before gets you off the hook for killing him that's your alibi.</dialogue>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <dialogue>Like writing a book about killing a guy gets you off the hook for killing him.</dialogue>
    <character>AN I.A. MAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( to Walker . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I do n't understand. What are you talking about? What book?</dialogue>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <parenthetical>( to Nick . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Private joke.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't think it's funny.</dialogue>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <parenthetical>( grins . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Well, hell, son, it's got a certain ring to it, I'll say that.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. POLICE DEPARTMENT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He is by the elevators with Gus and Lt. Andrews . He spots Beth going for the stairway .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( to Lt. Andrews . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'll get my stuff tomorrow.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE STAIRWAY</stage_direction>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Beth.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She stops . He catches up to her . They walk down the flights together . They speak quietly .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She looks at him , smiles . They keep walking down the steps .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>It's the least I could do. considering I got you into this mess with those reports.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No. I mean it, thank you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She looks at him , smiles .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>How do you know Catherine Tramell saw my reports?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>She knows stuff about me that only you know.</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She must really be something.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( she smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>From a clinical point of view.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>What was she like in school?</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>I hardly knew her. She gave me the creeps, though. I do n't know why.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE BUILDING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They get outside . Beth kisses him quickly , softly on the cheek .</scene_description>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <dialogue>Get some rest. Promise?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He nods . She starts walking toward her car .</scene_description>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Beth. I did n't mean what I said. About -</dialogue>
    <character>BETH</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes you did. I'm a big girl. I can handle it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She goes to her car .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE DETECTIVE BUREAU - NEXT DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He is cleaning his desk out , putting things into a duffel bag . Only Andrews is in the room . We see Lt. Walker sitting in his glass - enclosed office . He closes the duffel bag , looks at the place a long beat . Andrews is watching him . He goes up to Andrews</scene_description>
    <character>ANDREWS</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Take care, you hear?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Did you find out about her parents?</dialogue>
    <character>ANDREWS</character>
    <dialogue>You're on leave, man.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You're on psycho leave. I'm talking to a possible whacko here.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>You know I'm whacko, Sam, what'd you find?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A beat , and Andrews opens the file .</scene_description>
    <character>ANDREWS</character>
    <dialogue>The boat blew. There was a leak in the gas line. There were two previous repairs. There was a five - mil policy on both of'em. A real heavy investigation. Zilch. Goose - egg. It was an accident.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thanks.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He sees Lt. Walker looking at him . He goes into Walker 's office .</scene_description>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <dialogue>I.A.'s going to talk to you more about Nilsen. They're handling the investigation, we're not. Stay in touch with Dr. Gardner, it'll help on the evaluation.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <parenthetical>( after a beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She killed him.</dialogue>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <dialogue>Beth? Now you've got Beth killing people?</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>Catherine Tramell. It's part of her game.</dialogue>
    <character>LT. WALKER</character>
    <dialogue>First you've got her buying your file. Now you've got her killing Nilsen. Forget her, willya? Go someplace. Sit in the sun. Get away from this goddamn fog. Get her out of your system.</dialogue>
    <character>NICK</character>
    <dialogue>You do n't but it, do you? She knew nobody would but it.</dialogue>

    "summary":"In San Francisco, homicide detective Nick Curran investigates the murder of retired rock star Johnny Boz, who has been brutally stabbed to death with an ice pick during sex with a mysterious blonde woman. Nick's only suspect is Boz's bisexual girlfriend, crime novelist Catherine Tramell, who has written a novel that mirrors the crime. It is concluded that either Catherine is the murderer or someone is attempting to frame her. Catherine is uncooperative and taunting during the investigation, smoking and exposing herself during her interrogation. She has an alibi and passes a lie detector test. Nick discovers Catherine has a history of befriending murderers, including her girlfriend Roxy, who killed her two younger brothers, on impulse, when she was 16, and Hazel Dobkins, who killed her husband and children for no apparent reason. Nick, who accidentally shot two tourists while high on cocaine during an undercover assignment, attends counseling sessions with police psychologist Dr. Beth Garner, with whom he has an on and off affair. Nick discovers that Catherine is basing the protagonist of her latest book on him, wherein his character is murdered after falling for the wrong woman. Nick also learns Catherine has bribed Lt. Marty Nielsen of Internal Affairs for information from Nick's psychiatric file and that Beth had previously given it to Nielsen after he threatened to recommend Nick's termination. Nick assaults Nielsen in his office, and later becomes a prime suspect when Nielsen is killed. Nick suspects Catherine, and when his behavior deteriorates, he is put on leave. Nick and Catherine begin a torrid affair with the air of a cat-and-mouse game. Nick arrives at a club and witnesses Catherine doing coke with Roxy and another man. Nick and Catherine dance and make out, and are later observed having violent sex in Catherine’s bed by Roxy. Catherine ties Nick to the headboard with a white silk scarf, just as Boz was by the mystery blonde, but does not kill him. Roxy, jealous of Nick, attempts to run him over with Catherine's car, but dies when the car crashes. Catherine grieves over Roxy's death and tells Nick about a previous lesbian encounter at college that went awry. She claims the girl became obsessed with her, causing Nick to believe that Catherine may not have killed Boz. Nick identifies the girl as Beth, who acknowledges the encounter, but she claims it was Catherine who became obsessed. Additionally, Nick discovers that Beth and Catherine's college professor was also killed with an ice pick in an unsolved homicide, and that the events inspired one of Catherine's early novels. Nick comes across the final pages of Catherine's book in which the fictional detective finds his partner's body in an elevator. Catherine then breaks off their affair, causing Nick to become upset and suspicious. Nick later meets his partner Gus Moran, who has arranged to meet with Catherine's college roommate at an office building, hoping to find out what really went on between Catherine and Beth. As Nick waits in the car, Gus is stabbed to death with an ice pick in the elevator. Recalling the last pages of Catherine’s book, Nick runs into the building, only to find Gus' body in a manner similar to the scene described. Beth turns up as if out of nowhere and explains that she received a message to meet Gus. Nick suspects Beth has murdered Gus and, believing she is reaching for a gun, shoots her, but discovers that Beth was only fingering an ornament on her key chain. Evidence collected in Beth's apartment points to her as the killer of Boz, Nielsen, Moran, and her own husband, along with collections of photos and newspaper clippings of Catherine that imply an obsession with her. Nick is left confused and dejected. He returns to his apartment where Catherine meets him. She explains her reluctance to commit to him and the two have sex. As they discuss their future, an ice pick is revealed to be under the bed."

    <scene_description>As her bandmates CHANT the coda ("Stroke! Stroke!"), Ricki makes her way back to the stage. She triumphantly thrusts her fist into the air and falls to her knees. Her shoulders heave. She gave it her all. A smattering of tepid applause. Actually, one person goes crazy; the bartender, DANIEL, a young Latino man. He shrieks from his post across the room.</scene_description>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>Go Ricki! You're an icon!</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks, everyone. Gracias, my sweet Daniel.</dialogue>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>You're my queen!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>If there's an element of camp at play, Ricki doesn't acknowledge it. She her job very seriously.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Hello, Tarzana. That was Billy Squier's "The Stroke," a very truthful and brave song about the corrupt record business.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki's facial expression indicates that this might be a sore subject.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I'm Ricki Rendazzo, and I'd like to take a moment to introduce my band, the Flash. We've been the house band here at the Salt Well since...</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(to Greg)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>When did we get together? 2008?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg nods earnestly.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah. 2008. That was the year we elected you-know-who...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She rolls her eyes, clearly not a fan.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>But that's okay. We've still got rock and roll, don't we? No offense, Billy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BILLY, the Flash's black KEYBOARD PLAYER, shakes his head.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>We joke around. Speaking of Billy, he's the man on keys. Billy Lambert, everybody.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Billy plays a MUSICAL STING on the keyboard.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>And we've got Mark "Buster" Frye on the Rickenbacker bass.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>"BUSTER," a skinny weirdo, fidgets and nods.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Joe Scaduto on drums. Newly single, ladies.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Balding JOE smiles sheepishly, the pain of the recent breakup evident in his eyes.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>And finally, my right-hand man, Greg Sandoval on the Gibson SG.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg grins at Ricki and leans into his microphone.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <parenthetical>(on mic)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You know, people say band mates shouldn't date, but I don't think it's hurting our sound.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Well, we're not really dating, Greg.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg chuckles to save face, but he's clearly stung.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki smiles tightly: let's discuss this later.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Is that not the terminology anymore? Are we, uh, "hooking up" like my kid says?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The other band members exchange uncomfortable glances.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>We've been spending some time together.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>I "spend time" with Buster. I think you and I are a little different.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Buster drags on a glowing-blue electronic cigarette and exhales a cloud of vapor.</scene_description>
    <character>BUSTER</character>
    <dialogue>Shit, I hope so, man.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Let's not have this conversation onstage.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She turns back toward the mic, back in "on" mode.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>So. We've learned a new tune since our last gig here at the Salt Well. You asked for more of today's hits and, well...we aim to please.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Though she tries to sound enthusiastic about this, her tone is resigned. She nods to Greg to prompt him. Greg begins to strum a familiar pop riff. Ricki gamely launches into her best Katy Perry whisper.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(singing)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You think I'm pretty without any makeup on...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CUT TO:</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SALT WELL (BAR AREA) - POST-GIG</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki sits down at the bar, spent and sweating. Daniel is ready with a glass of wine and plenty of praise.</scene_description>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>Chardonnay for my flawless queen.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry I couldn't talk before the gig. Vocal rest.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg takes the stool next to her, scoffing gently.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Vocal rest. She thinks this is Madison Square Garden.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I take things seriously.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>I know. I love that about you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg immediately begins to backpedal.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Not to freak you out or anything--</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Greg, I'm sorry about ...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg pauses.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>...what I said onstage. It was just some fun banter. The crowd loves that tension; it's why Fleetwood Mac worked.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <parenthetical>(dubious)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>All right.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Daniel hoists Ricki's huge, fringed BLACK PURSE over the bar.</scene_description>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>Your purse is vibrating, mama.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>If she'd move in with me, she wouldn't need that kind of thing.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Corny. Ricki rolls her eyes and retrieves her cheap cell phone from her purse.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Who on earth would be calling me?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ugh, probably my manager. He's 19. She looks at the display. It's a 630 area code.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(to herself)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Six-three-zero.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>What's that? Bufu, Egypt?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki's reply is barely audible.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Chicago suburbs.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Probably a telemarketer or something. You know, I got an Old Navy credit card like ten years ago and it haunts me to this day. Messed up my credit, got my name on some list all because I needed some swim trunks...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg drones on, but Ricki is lost in thought. She sips her Jack and ginger.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. SALT WELL - CLOSING TIME</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The Salt Well shares a parking lot with a strip mall. Ricki and Greg linger outside, cuddling. After a couple of drinks, Ricki is much more affectionate. Greg slides his jacket over her shoulders.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Brrr. When I was a kid, I thought it was always warm in California.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Aw, me too. I used to watch Gidget on TV and it looked so great. And like, Hawaii 5-0...</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Hawaii 5-0 was in Hawaii.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>You don't say, smart-ass.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He gazes into her eyes with clear intent.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I can't tonight. I have work in the morning at nine.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>You never go to sleep anyway.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I've got some things to do.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. RICKI'S APARTMENT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MUSIC UP: Fleetwood Mac's "Never Going Back Again." A small, crappy apartment in the deep Valley. Ricki cooks herself some Rice-a-Roni on an electric range. She adds the packet of radioactive-yellow "chicken" powder to the skillet. Her rock-and-roll getup is gone, replaced with a conservative beige bathrobe and slippers. Ricki transfers her dinner to a bowl and carries it ten feet to the "dining room." She sits down at a cheap dining room set, puts on her reading glasses, and begins to page through the Los Angeles Times.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. RICKI'S BATHROOM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki is removing her glittery black eye makeup with a cotton pad and cold cream. As she finishes, reveal a PILE of soiled pads-- it takes a lot to remove the rock star.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. RICKI'S BEDROOM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki's bedroom is small, with dirty beige wall-to-wall carpet and a glass vase full of found SEA SHELLS. She climbs into bed and turns on an "Ocean Waves" white noise machine-- Ricki has done her best to turn the Valley apartment into the L.A. beach house she imagined as a child. She turns off the light.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. WHOLE FOODS (TO ESTABLISH) - MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A busy Whole Foods in Los Angeles.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHOLE FOODS - SAME</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki wears a cashier's smock and rings up GROCERIES. She quickly scans item after item of overpriced organic stuff. Her latest CUSTOMER is a dude in bike shorts. Total California douchebag, buying an insane amount of expensive supplements, snacks, etc. Ricki holds up a mysterious FRUIT and examines it.</scene_description>
    <character>CUSTOMER</character>
    <dialogue>It's a star fruit.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki deftly punches in the SKU code with her long, gold acrylic nails.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Right.</dialogue>
    <character>CUSTOMER</character>
    <dialogue>I try to listen to my body, and today my body was like, "Fruit!"</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>It's funny how that works, isn't it? Okay, that comes to $447.74.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The man cringes-- jokingly-- as he pulls out his wallet.</scene_description>
    <character>CUSTOMER</character>
    <dialogue>Ouch. I guess there's a reason they call this place...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki wearily mouths the punch line along with him.</scene_description>
    <character>CUSTOMER</character>
    <dialogue>..."Whole Paycheck."</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Well that actually is, truly, my whole paycheck.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The man suddenly looks guilty.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>$447...yep, that's about what I make in a week.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The customer pulls out his debit card, wanting to end the interaction as soon as possible.</scene_description>
    <character>CUSTOMER</character>
    <dialogue>Heh. How about that.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Maybe if we get the Democrats out of office, the economy will improve, but until then, a lot of us are living to hand-to-mouth.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(surprised)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh. And you'd like $100 cash back.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki's manager, TROY, 19, has been observing this interaction. He walks over.</scene_description>
    <character>TROY</character>
    <dialogue>Have a great day, sir. Let me know how you like those protein cookies.</dialogue>
    <character>CUSTOMER</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki hands the man his cash and he hurries out.</scene_description>
    <character>TROY</character>
    <dialogue>You just alienated the customer.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki is apologetic.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I was making small talk. I was engaging, like you said.</dialogue>
    <character>TROY</character>
    <dialogue>Let's stick to talking about the weather. Or the inventory.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry, Troy.</dialogue>
    <character>TROY</character>
    <dialogue>Remember. "Mindfulness."</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki nods with "enthusiasm."</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHOLE FOODS (BREAK ROOM) - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki is sitting at a table, eating a sack lunch from home (tuna sandwich, Yoplait, can of soda). Her PHONE rings again. Ricki sighs, staring at the display. She finally picks up on the third ring.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Hello?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CROSS-CUT PHONE CALL</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PETE BRUMMEL'S HOME - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A suburban COUNTRY KITCHEN, sprawling, with granite counters and pristine cabinets. PETE BRUMMEL, 55, paces with a phone. He looks like what he is: an accountant on his day off. A little nerdy, a little tightly-wound, and definitely not thrilled to be speaking with Ricki.</scene_description>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Linda?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki sighs, hating the sound of her given name.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Mm-hm?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>You answered. I thought maybe you had another new number.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Is this Pete?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, this is Pete. I've been trying to call you.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Really? I'm sorry.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>I left you a voice mail. This is kind of time-sensitive matter?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I haven't figured out how to check those messages yet. You know me.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. I do.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>So what's the problem, Pete?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>It's Julie. Max left her.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Oh my goodness. Where did he go?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>He didn't go anywhere. He's divorcing her. He met someone else.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Well.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(pondering)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I suppose the heart wants what it wants...</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>What? Are you actually defending this ass who just abandoned our daughter? Wow. That is-- well, that is pretty consistent with...</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(interrupting)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm not defending him. I'm trying to be fair and balanced like always. How is Julie?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>That's why I'm calling you. Julie's not well. She's absolutely unhinged. She showed up here a few nights ago, and she's acting...I mean, she's not showering or changing her clothes... she's... I'm worried, Linda.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>How's your wife taking all this?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Maureen is in Seattle with her father. His health is failing.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Oh right, he has Alzheimers.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A.L.S.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Isn't that short for Alzheimers?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>No, it isn't.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>What can I do to help?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>You could be there for your daughter.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>This is a clearly a loaded topic. Ricki pauses.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Physically, or like in song?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A long silence on the other end.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Physically. Okay.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. LAX AIRPORT TICKETING - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki passes through the automatic doors, fully made-up and dressed to kill in tight black jeans, boots, a fringed leather jacket, and all of her rock star accessories. Her GUITAR is slung over her shoulder. She looks around, confused. She tries to walk to the ticketing counter, but a uniformed ATTENDANT stops her.</scene_description>
    <character>ATTENDANT</character>
    <dialogue>You need a boarding pass? You can get that right here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She directs Ricki to the electronic TICKETING MACHINE.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Here? This computer?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(then)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sorry. I haven't flown in a long time.</dialogue>
    <character>ATTENDANT</character>
    <dialogue>That's fine. Just put in your confirmation number.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Is that like my social?</dialogue>
    <character>ATTENDANT</character>
    <dialogue>No, ma'am.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki is fumbling in her big purse, lost. A LIPSTICK rolls onto the floor.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. LAX SECURITY CHECKPOINT - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki takes off her high-heeled boots, looking short and vulnerable. She takes off her many RINGS and BRACELETS and drops them in a plastic bin. Studs, turquoise, chains...it's a comical amount of jewelry. She steps through the detector. BEEP! A giant, ostentations BELT BUCKLE comes off. A silver TOE RING. Ricki tries again. On the other end of the conveyer belt, an exasperated TSA EMPLOYEE opens Ricki's bag.</scene_description>
    <character>TSA EMPLOYEE</character>
    <dialogue>Excuse me, Ma'am? You can't have this.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The employee holds up a GIGANTIC CAN OF HAIR SPRAY.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry.</dialogue>
    <character>TSA EMPLOYEE</character>
    <dialogue>You can't have any of this stuff.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The employee is taking out all of Ricki's "necessary" stuff-- mousse, gel, Oil of Olay, Poison perfume, a big bottle of CHEAP RED WINE. A YOUNG BUSINESS TRAVELER behind Ricki sighs.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>For heaven's sake, the wine is just a hostess gift. I'm not going to drink it on the plane.</dialogue>
    <character>TSA EMPLOYEE #2</character>
    <dialogue>Ma'am, can you step over to this area, please?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PLANE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki is stuffed into an economy class seat. She wears her READING GLASSES and reads a library copy of Tuesdays with Morrie.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. HERTZ RENT-A-CAR LOT (CHICAGO) - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It's FREEZING in Chicago. Receipt in hand, Ricki shivers and trots across a lot full of RENTAL CARS, dragging her suitcase and guitar. She clearly didn't pack any type of proper outerwear for this trip. Ricki finds her car, a white PT Cruiser, and unlocks it, rubbing her hands together.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. CHICAGO EXPRESSWAY (TO ESTABLISH) - NIGHT</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. CAR - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki is listening to the classic rock station, of course. She slows the car as her headlights illuminate the gated entrance to RUFFLED FEATHERS GOLF COMMUNITY. She pulls into the gate and is stopped by the GUARD.</scene_description>
    <character>GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>Your name, please?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Ricki.</dialogue>
    <character>GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>You're here to see...</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Peter Brummel.</dialogue>
    <character>GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>Can I see some ID?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki fishes out her license and hands it over.</scene_description>
    <character>GUARD</character>
    <parenthetical>(examining)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This says "Linda."</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>That's my given name. But Pete knows I prefer to go by Ricki, so I think he would probably...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The guard checks the log, interrupting.</scene_description>
    <character>GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>Here you are. Linda Brummel.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT. PETE BRUMMEL'S HOME - SAME</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Pete stands at the front door of his handsome brick home. He stares out into the night, impatient and nervous. There's a DRESSED-UP GOOSE STATUE on the front porch. Ricki pulls up and parks crookedly in the driveway. Pete takes a deep breath and walks out to stiffly greet his ex-wife. Ricki struggles with her suitcase and guitar.</scene_description>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Let me help you with that.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>You brought a guitar.</dialogue>
    <dialogue>RICKI Just the one.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Um, how was your flight?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They walk into the house together. Pete carries Ricki's suitcase, but the mood is awkward and businesslike.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>It was fine. Travel has really changed since we took the kids to Disney World.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah. That was 1988.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I remember when flying was a treat.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>People got a little dressed up, even. Now I see these young girls in exercise pants.</scene_description>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I can see you're still putting in the effort.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki's not sure if this is a compliment. Matter of fact, it definitely isn't. Still, she remains cordial.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Gee, thanks, Pete. Wow, this is some house. This is like a mansion.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks, yeah. We got this, uh, double- height entry, and Maureen had to have those Palladian windows.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Very classical.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, I feel like Jefferson at Monticello.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Silence. Ricki and Pete are out of small talk.</scene_description>
    <character>PETE (CONT'D)</character>
    <dialogue>I'll tell Julie you're here.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. KITCHEN - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki enters the huge kitchen. She looks very out of place amongst all the stainless-steel luxury. The decor is very crafty and "country". Lots of farm and chicken motifs. A handpainted sign that says "THIS IS NOT BURGER KING-- WE DO THINGS MY WAY." Another that says "HUG A NURSE." A hum as the space-age dishwasher begins to cycle. Ricki walks over. There's a cute little SIGN hanging from the dishwasher that says DIRTY. Ricki turns it over. It says CLEAN. There are some "classic"-looking paneled doors against the wall. Ricki pulls at them curiously, then reacts with surprise-- it's a REFRIGERATOR.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Oh.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She opens the freezer side. Alongside the ice cream and frozen veggies, we see a few BAGGIES full of glistening, green MARIJUANA. Ricki raises her eyebrows, surprised.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Peter.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As if on cue, Pete enters the kitchen. Ricki closes the freezer quickly.</scene_description>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>So, Julie is pretty tired. She's glad you're here though and she's looking forward to having a conversation in the morning...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A thunder of FOOTSTEPS. Angry, bloodshot EYES appear over Pete's shoulder in the doorway.</scene_description>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Julie is not glad you're here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Julie's fucking pissed. JULIE emerges in a rage. She's in her late 20s, beautiful, but unstable and disheveled. She wears an old Slayer T-shirt and red flannel pajama pants and looks like she hasn't showered in a week.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Hi Ju-jee!</dialogue>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Oh my God. Look who it is. Joanfucking- Jett has graced us with her presence.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Who would I marry then?</dialogue>

    <dialogue>That was my cover story when I was in college. Ten years ago. I'm sorry you didn't stay updated on my sexual identity. But then, you didn't stay updated on much.</dialogue>

    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Don't twist my words. That is not fair, Adam. I am not homophobic. I have a wonderful little friend named Daniel who is a gay bartender.</dialogue>

    <parenthetical>(to no one in particular)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She costumes herself as this "edgy" rocker who's cooler than all the PTA moms. When in fact, she voted for George W. Bush twice.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>I can't help being gay!</dialogue>

    <character>ADAM</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Julie)</parenthetical>

Don't forget that. Let's try to put some of this crap behind us and just appreciate the proximity, OK? Right now, the Brummels are proximal. That's-- that's special in itself.</dialogue>

  <scene>

  <scene>

    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Julie?</dialogue>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. MASTER SUITE - SAME</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki walks in and looks around. It's a huge MASTER SUITE, immaculately maintained, with shining wood floors. It couldn't be more different than Ricki's cramped bedroom with the dirty apartment carpet. Ricki crosses the room and opens another door. A huge BATHROOM with a gigantic, free-standing SOAKING TUB.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(to herself)</parenthetical>

On the other side of the closet. Pete's BUSINESS SUITS are hanging. His shirts are organized by color. Near the back of the closet, Ricki sees a WHITE SPA-STYLE BATHROBE hanging on a hook. It looks like it doesn't get a lot of use. She reaches for it.</scene_description>

Scrolling through the menu, she clicks on "Movies." Ricki selects Life of Pi. A message flashes on the TV asking Ricki to confirm the $6.99 purchase. Ricki glances around the room. She selects "OK." She puts her feet up and begins to watch the movie.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PETE BRUMMELL'S HOME (KITCHEN) - AFTERNOON</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Julie sits at the counter wearing the same Slayer T-shirt and PJ pants. She still hasn't washed her hair and looks like a greasy mess. The clock on the stove reads 1:00 PM. Ricki enters. Julie barely glances up from her bowl of cereal.</scene_description>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>You're still here? Don't you have to go to work?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I gave all of this weekend's shifts to my coworker, Florence.</dialogue>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Florence must be P.O.'d.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>No, she was happy to pick up the hours. Most people need money.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>It's implied that Julie, lounging in her dad's 500 square foot kitchen, is not one of those people.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>What are you eating?</dialogue>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Whole-grain fart flakes. I'm done.</dialogue>

    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Whoops.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Last night, why did you announce that Josh and Emily got engaged?</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Because I thought you had a right to know. And because I'm kind of a shit- disturber.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>It was a little embarrassing. And then your brother started in on me...</dialogue>
    <character>JULIE</character>

    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>What--</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(realizing)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You think he was defending me?</dialogue>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah. He always does.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(then)</parenthetical>

    <dialogue>Don't be silly. It's just that when you have a child...that's a lasting bond.</dialogue>

    <parenthetical>(duh)</parenthetical>

    <dialogue>How do you think he paid for this ten-of-a-kind architectural statement?</dialogue>

    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Never...</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Exactly. We can go to the old neighborhood, maybe do some of the things we used to do...</dialogue>

    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Or just, you know, old times sake.</dialogue>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PETE BRUMMELL'S HOME (KITCHEN) - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Pete is in the kitchen, home from work. His BRIEFCASE sits on the kitchen island. Julie and Ricki enter. Ricki has a look of satisfaction on her face.</scene_description>

    <dialogue>Hi, Dad.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Hey, I'm sorry if I was a bit of an asshole yesterday afternoon. Things have been a little stressful at the company.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Well, you work very hard. And I admire that.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>You do? You used to call me an uptight workaholic.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>I "used to" a lot of things. But I've changed, Pete. I have.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>I can see that.</dialogue>
