    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <parenthetical>(reading)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>"In lieu of a gift, please make a donation to one of the following children's charities."</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(aghast)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ha! Oh my God, who gets married and doesn't want a bunch of stuff?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>My son.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>On stage, Buster speaks into the mic.</scene_description>
    <character>BUSTER</character>
    <dialogue>Testes, one-two.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Daniel hands the invite back to Ricki.</scene_description>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>Flower seeds. That is some bougie shit. How much do you think those invites cost per person?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I have no idea. I just thought you'd get a kick out of it.</dialogue>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>So are you excited about the wedding, then?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I'm not going.</dialogue>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>You have to! It won't be sexy without you. Buy something at Dress Barn, take your man, and go see your baby get married.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I don't have any money. I discussed it with Greg and we simply don't have it. But it's fine. I don't think I'm necessarily wanted there.</dialogue>
    <character>DANIEL</character>
    <dialogue>Well, you're always wanted here.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you, sweetie.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki pats Daniel's hand as she gets up and heads for the stage. She hops on to scattered applause.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Good evening, Tarzana! Happy Valentine's weekend to all you lovers out there. Any Janis fans out there? Janis Joplin?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>No response, except CLAPPING from Daniel.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI (CONT'D)</character>
    <dialogue>Good, because we're gonna start things off with a song that's very special to me...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She glances at Greg, who is wearing a DIFFERENT GUITAR than usual. It's not his beautiful sunburst Gibson SG. It's a cheaper YELLOW ELECTRIC GUITAR, '80s model.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI (CONT'D)</character>
    <dialogue>Where's your guitar?</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>This is my guitar.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>No, your guitar.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(disbelief)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Your '68 SG Standard that you've been besotted with since the day I met you?</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>I felt like playing this one tonight.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>This idea is so absurd that Ricki laughs.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah, right. The "Wet Banana"? What's going on?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Billy, Buster and Joe exchange glances.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>I sold it.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Why?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Greg just looks at her. Over on bass, Buster shakes his head and takes a drag off his blue e-cigarette.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, Greg.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. AIRPORT (SECURITY CHECKPOINT) - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki and Greg are the TSA's worst nightmare. Greg pulls off a GIANT BELT BUCKLE and unlaces a pair of 18-hole boots. Ricki is removing her usual array of accessories.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>How do we know that scanner isn't some form of mind-control?</dialogue>
    <character>TSA AGENT</character>
    <dialogue>Sir, you cannot take this through.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>An AGENT, digging through Greg's carry-on, holds up a bottle of CABO WABO TEQUILA.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Come on, man, that's Sammy Hagar's tequila!</dialogue>
    <character>TSA AGENT #2</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Ricki)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ma'am, I need you to remove the toe ring.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PLANE - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki and Greg READ on the plane. Ricki is reading a library copy of The Celestine Prophecy. Greg enthusiastically flips through the Skymall catalog.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Look at this. It cooks the hot dog and toasts the bun at the same time.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>That's useful.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Right?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>This book is very enlightening.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <parenthetical>(musing)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I don't eat hot dogs much anymore.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki pats Greg's arm affectionately.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DRESS BARN (TO ESTABLISH) - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A strip mall in the Chicago suburbs.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DRESS BARN - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki is in one of the "dressing rooms"-- a BOOTH hidden behind a curtain. Greg is sitting on a chair waiting for her to emerge.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Come out, babe.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>I look absurd.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>I'm sure you look gorgeous.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>I look like my mother.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>No way. Your mother's dead.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki comes out wearing a CONSERVATIVE, UN-RICKI-LIKE PALE BLUE DRESS with the tags hanging off it. It looks very odd with her pleather boots.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>You look beautiful. That is like, the most amazing blue. Reminds me of Roger Daltrey's eyes in Tommy.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(sincere)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thank you.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Did the invitation say you had to be fancy?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>It said "Dress to Impress." Ricki rolls her eyes at the affected wording.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I'm impressed.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I haven't seen a lot of these people in years. Pete got "custody" of all our friends and most of the family. They're gonna see me and there's gonna say "Wow, there's Linda. I guess things didn't work out for her in Hollywood."</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Um, are any of those "nosy rosies" in Tarzana's number one party band?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki has to laugh at that.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah. I'd say things worked out pretty fucking well!</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Ha. I'll just tell them I'm collaborating with Greg Sandoval. That'll shut them up.</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>Collaborating? You're doing him. You're the luckiest woman alive.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The SALES LADY walks over.</scene_description>
    <character>SALES LADY</character>
    <dialogue>Can I show you some other styles?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Do you have anything black?</dialogue>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <dialogue>She'll take this one.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. MORTON ARBORETUM (TO ESTABLISH) - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It's a beautiful spring day at the OUTDOOR WEDDING VENUE, a tree-filled nature preserve.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. MORTON ARBORETUM - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A HARPIST plays as GUESTS filter into the WEDDING CEREMONY. HIP-LOOKING WAITERS and WAITRESSES hold trays of signature COCKTAILS. The wedding looks perfectly rustic in a very expensive way. Ricki enters the area with trepidation, wearing her new blue dress. A PERKY WAITRESS immediately solicits her.</scene_description>
    <character>WAITRESS</character>
    <dialogue>Would you like a cocktail before the ceremony?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Sure. What is this?</dialogue>
    <character>WAITRESS</character>
    <parenthetical>(gesturing)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This one is called "The Josh." It's ginger beer and small-batch whiskey with candied lemon peel. This is "The Emily"; it's kind of a playful take on a Kir Royale.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki looks at the girl like she's speaking Cantonese.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Which one do you recommend?</dialogue>
    <character>WAITRESS</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry, I'm in recovery.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Me too.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki scoots away from the cocktails, wrinkling her nose. She wanders self-consciously through the sea of assembled GUESTS. Suddenly, a WIZENED HAND grips her arm.</scene_description>
    <character>OMA (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Linda.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Linda turns to see a VERY OLD WOMAN of about 90.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Hi, Oma. How are you?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Oma appears to be senile.</scene_description>
    <character>OMA</character>
    <dialogue>I like you. You know? Even though you ran off on my son.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I always liked you too.</dialogue>
    <character>OMA</character>
    <dialogue>How is Las Vegas?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Um...</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(realizing)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Los Angeles. It's very nice. Warm.</dialogue>
    <character>OMA</character>
    <dialogue>I don't like Peter's new wife one bit. Don't trust her.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Peter and Maureen seem happy.</dialogue>
    <character>OMA</character>
    <dialogue>Maybe now, but it's only been a few weeks.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(gently)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's been many years.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A YOUNG, MALE RELATIVE rushes to retrieve poor, confused Oma.</scene_description>
    <character>MALE RELATIVE</character>
    <dialogue>Oma, there you are! Come on. Let's have a seat.</dialogue>
    <character>MALE RELATIVE</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Ricki, flat)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh. Hi.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Oma is ushered away. Ricki looks at the COCKTAIL WAITRESS.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I'll take "the Emily."</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. MORTON ARBORETUM (CEREMONY AREA) - DAY</stage_direction>
    <character>OFFICIANT (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Everyone, please take your seats.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The ceremony is about to start. The ceremony area consists of about 100 chairs in a clearing. Everything is festooned with wildflowers. Ricki is seated alone on an aisle seat near the back, reading the wedding program. The "better" seats are rapidly filling up. As PEOPLE walk by and sit down, we hear a snippet of GOSSIP in hushes tones: Is that?...It is. Wow...Not even sitting with family... Ricki continues to look down at her program.</scene_description>
    <character>OFFICIANT</character>
    <dialogue>All rise.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Everyone complies. Ricki looks ahead and sees that JOSH and ADAM, the best man, have appeared at the altar in suits. A CLASSICAL GUITARIST begins to play near the altar as the wedding procession begins. A BRIDESMAID in a long dress walks down the aisle, escorted by a GROOMSMAN. Another PAIR follows. The bridesmaids wear elegant vintage dresses and carry "green" bouquets. Then, Julie appears, looking radiant (and almost unrecognizable) with her hair and makeup done. She's so beautiful that there's a murmur through the crowd as she emerges on the arm of a GROOMSMAN Julie sees Ricki and pauses. Ricki smiles at Julie. Julie looks at the assembled crowd, remembering her last trip down the aisle. She looks frozen, disturbed. Ricki realizes what's bothering Julie. As the GROOMSMAN tries to nudge Julie down the aisle, Ricki leans over and whispers at her daughter.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Don't run away.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Julie looks back at her mother.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Just keep walking.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She nods encouragingly. Julie looks ahead, squares her shoulders, continues to WALK. As Ricki regards Julie's departing form, she notices with surprise-- and love-- that her daughter wears COMBAT BOOTS with her dress. Finally, EMILY appears, escorted by both her MOTHER and FATHER. All three look rich, elegant and happy. Shutters click as everybody oohs and ahhs over the bride. Ricki looks at Josh: he wipes a tear away from his eye as he gazes at his soon-to-be wife. Ricki looks at the bride and her parents as they stride past her: a perfect, intact TRIAD, seemingly untouched by dysfunction or pain. From the front row, PETE and MAUREEN beam at their soon-to- be daughter-in-law. Pete's arm is around Maureen. He rubs her arm happily as the bride swishes past. Ricki glances across the aisle at a LITTLE BOY who seems to be having an awful time. He pouts and kicks the chair in front of him. He meets Ricki's gaze. She WINKS.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. RECEPTION - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ricki makes her way through the RECEIVING LINE, where Josh and Emily greet their GUESTS. Josh hugs Ricki warmly, overwhelmed by his big day.</scene_description>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>Mom. I'm so glad you're here. I didn't know if you would make it out.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>My boyfriend pawned his Gibson SG.</dialogue>
    <character>EMILY</character>
    <dialogue>Oh!</dialogue>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>Well, we got your RSVP so late that we couldn't really move things around with the hall so...</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(awkward)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I hope you don't mind eating with some of Emily's cousins and like, our harpist...</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Not at all. I'd love to learn about harp theory. Well. I'll see you guys in there.</dialogue>
    <character>EMILY</character>
    <dialogue>Great.</dialogue>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>Really great to see you, Mom.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki heads into the reception area and sees ADAM with his date, a GOOD-LOOKING ASIAN GUY. She waves in their direction.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Adam!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She trots toward them and holds her arms out expectantly. Adam puts on a brave face. So does Ricki.</scene_description>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>Hi, Mom. Um, Desmond, this is my mother, Linda.</dialogue>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <dialogue>What a pleasure. I see where Adam gets his cheekbones.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>You're Adam's friend?</dialogue>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <parenthetical>(quickly)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes. We're friends.</dialogue>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>We're seeing each other.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>That's wonderful. Adam, I'm so glad you've met someone. Particularly someone so handsome! You may be too young for this, but have you ever heard of Bruce Lee?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Adam looks like he wants to die.</scene_description>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <dialogue>Of course I've heard of Bruce Lee; he's the man!</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>You look a lot like him.</dialogue>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>Not at all. Not even a little.</dialogue>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks! I've been growing my hair out lately, and I think I'm serving up some "Bruce realness."</dialogue>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>You're not even Chinese.</dialogue>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <dialogue>Neither was Bruce; he was born in San Francisco.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(to Ricki)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I did a research paper on him in college.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Where did you go to school?</dialogue>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <dialogue>Harvard.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <parenthetical>(enjoying herself)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Wow! Adam always dreamed of going to Harvard, but to no avail...</dialogue>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks, Mom.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki stops and looks Adam in the eyes.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>No. You're brilliant. If you'd had more support from me, you could have done it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Adam seems to respect Ricki's willingness to "own" this.</scene_description>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Desmond's eyes dart from Ricki to Adam. Awkward.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Well. I just think you two are a beautiful couple and I hope you have a nice time and enjoy your vegan dinner.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She pronounces it vedge-in, like vegetable.</scene_description>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <dialogue>Vegan.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I don't know what it is.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She smiles and walks off. Adam's got that stun-gun look.</scene_description>
    <character>ADAM</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Desmond)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>OK, she must be heavily medicated.</dialogue>
    <character>DESMOND</character>
    <dialogue>I like her.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. RECEPTION - EVENING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The dinner portion of the RECEPTION is in full swing. Everything is lovely, quirky, and just-so. Guests drink wine out of mason jars. A JAZZ COMBO plays dinner music onstage. Near the front of the room, the BRIDAL PARTY holds court at the customary LONG TABLE. Pete is sitting there, chatting with the newlyweds. The seat next to him is empty; Maureen is circulating and saying hello to various people. The perfect hostess. Ricki watches her, as usual, with envy. Near the back of the room, Ricki is sitting at a round table with SEVEN OTHER PEOPLE, none of whom she knows. A GIRL sitting across from her tries to strike up a conversation</scene_description>
    <character>GIRL AT TABLE</character>
    <dialogue>So, how did you meet Josh?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Caesarean section.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Before the confused girl can reply. Ricki glances at her watch nervously.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I have to go.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She gets up and crosses the room to the bridal party's table. She walks up to Pete.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Pete. I think it's time.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Pete seems surprised.</scene_description>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Already?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>It's nearly the end of dinner.</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>That's right, that's what you said.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Julie overhears this conversation and reacts with alarm.</scene_description>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>You're leaving, aren't you?</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Julie...</dialogue>
    <character>JULIE</character>
    <dialogue>Big surprise. You've been here for a hot minute. How about waiting until the ink dries in the guest book?</dialogue>
    <character>PETE</character>
    <dialogue>Calm down, honey. You don't know what this is about.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki has already picked up a CHAMPAGNE GLASS. She begins hitting it with a fork: ding ding ding. She nods at the JAZZ COMBO, who hurriedly finish up their song. A SERVER appears and hands RICKI a microphone. Ricki accepts it nervously. The entire crowd turns to face her.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Hello everyone. Remember me?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Awkward chuckles from the crowd.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>If you don't, I'm Linda Brummel, mother of the groom. I remember a lot of you, from years ago. It's nice to see your faces again.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Many of those FACES stare back at her. Blinking.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I wasn't really sure what to give Josh and Emily as a gift.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Not just because I don't have any money, but because there were too many possibilities. There's so much out there that I haven't given them. Where to begin? How to decide what to give my son, who deserves so much and has gotten so little?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Josh and Emily have nervous smiles on their faces.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I was never a traditional mom. And I won't be a traditional mother-in-law-- I hope.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>More laughter, this time more genuine.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>But I realized that the only thing I have to give Josh and Emily is the only thing I've ever had to give anyone. I'm not much of a housekeeper, a cook, or a nurse...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>On Maureen, watching Ricki intently...</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI (CONT'D)</character>
    <dialogue>But I am a musician. That's what I have to give. That's what I am. That's all. And so I'd like to sing a song for my son and his beautiful wife right now.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(then)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh. I want to thank my children's "other mother" for helping me to arrange this surprise.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>From across the room, Maureen nods at Ricki respectfully. Josh mouths What is she doing? to Maureen; Mo waves him off.</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI (CONT'D)</character>
    <dialogue>Guys? You can come in.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Ricki gestures toward the back of the room. GREG, BUSTER, JOE and BILLY appear. Greg has the Wet Banana, Buster carries his bass; Joe has his sticks. They wear cheap SUITS. (Buster actually has a "tuxedo" T-shirt on.) They head toward the stage as the crowd murmurs.</scene_description>
    <character>EMILY</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Josh)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Who are they?</dialogue>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>I think that's the Flash.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The regular BAND steps aside, making room for Ricki and the Flash. They've discussed all of this in advance. Greg plugs in his yellow guitar. Ricki adjusts her mic.</scene_description>
    <character>GREG</character>
    <parenthetical>(into mic)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I usually have a way better guitar.</dialogue>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>Josh and Emily, here's some sage advice from .38 Special. I love you both very much.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Joe counts off with his sticks.</scene_description>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>One-two-three-four!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Flash launch into "HOLD ON LOOSELY."</scene_description>
    <character>RICKI</character>
    <dialogue>I see it all around me. Good lovin' gone bad. And usually it's too late when you Realize what you had...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>On Emily's PAINED FACE...her reception has been hijacked. Plus she hadn't planned on .38 Special at her perfect quirky/indie wedding. Josh looks a little sheepish. But when he sees the expression on his bride's face, he realizes he has to embrace the situation to keep it from ruining the day. Josh takes Emily's hand and leads her out into the middle of the floor.</scene_description>
    <character>EMILY</character>
    <dialogue>Josh! What about our first dance?</dialogue>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>I guess this is it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He gives Ricki the thumbs up as he begins to SPIN and TWIRL Emily, who knows the steps well...</scene_description>
    <character>EMILY</character>
    <dialogue>What about our choreography?</dialogue>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>Just do what we rehearsed</dialogue>
    <character>EMILY</character>
    <dialogue>But it's not the right song!</dialogue>
    <character>JOSH</character>
    <dialogue>Just do it faster.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Emily can't help but laugh as Josh whips her around. The crowd begins to WHOOP and CHEER and Emily softens.</scene_description>
    <character>EMILY</character>

    <parenthetical>( PAUSE )</parenthetical>

    <character />
    <parenthetical>( PAUSE )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What is this?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>I believe you poetry under- graduate types call it...'' a slough of despond.''</dialogue>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>If you do n't get up and play a game with me I wo n't come back here again. Ever.</dialogue>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. CROQUET LAWN -</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JANE AIMS , STRIKES , hits a FEEBLE SHOT .</scene_description>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>My turn.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>STEPHEN AIMS , HITS his BALL through the FIRST HOOP , then walks , as best he can , off toward his BALL , using his MALLET as a WALKING STICK . With his second shot he hits her BALL . He then picks up his BALL , places it beside hers so that it touches , puts his foot on his ball , then smacks his BALL HARD with his MALLET , blasting her ball down to the next hoop . He proceeds to play a MASTER GAME that will not allow JANE another shot , enlisting her ball to advance his own from HOOP to HOOP , until - - he knocks his ball and hits the finishing peg . JANE has been watching all this , her eyes FLOODING WITH TEARS , until she can bear it no longer , and walks up to him and picks up his ball , stopping the game . They stare into each others eyes , until he can bear it no longer and he walks off ( as best he can ) back to his room . She watches him , then follows determinedly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. STEPHEN'S DORM ROOM/CAMBRIDGE UNI - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He enters ANGRILY , SLAMS the door behind him , then tries to break a CHAIR by throwing it against the wall - just as JANE enters .</scene_description>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>Go away.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>More knocks .</scene_description>

    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>STEPHEN? Let me in. Please. Please let me in.</dialogue>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. HALLWAY/STEPHEN'S DORM/CAMBRIDGE UNI - DAY</stage_direction>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Go away!</dialogue>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>Are you going to talk about this or not?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Silence .</scene_description>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>There's nothing to say -- just... ( go )</dialogue>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>Is that what you want?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>That's what I want. I have n't got time for you. So - if you care about me at all - go.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JANE moves closer and closer to STEPHEN during this whole interchange - almost trapping STEPHEN , who is gallantly trying to resist being taken into her life .</scene_description>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>I ca n't.</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>I've got two years. I need to work.</dialogue>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>I ca n't.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>His eyes widen . He ca n't believe his ears . He looks at her .</scene_description>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I think -- I've fallen in love with you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He ca n't speak now . This STUNS him .</scene_description>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I know. Strange. Inexplicable.</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>You've -- you've leapt to -- a false conclusion...</dialogue>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>My chances are probably -</dialogue>
    <character />
    <parenthetical>( SHRUGS )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>- well, some `` integer of zero'', but I think we can make a go of this. I want us to be together, for as long as we've got. And if that's not very long then - well, that's just how it is. It will have to do.</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>You do n't realise what's coming. It'll affect everything.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She advances , and kisses him on the lips . He is still speechless . She stares into his eyes , with love --</scene_description>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>Your glasses are always dirty.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She takes them off , cleans them on her dress . His heart is exploding with joy and hope . She slips his GLASSES gently back on his nose .</scene_description>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>There. That's better. Is n't it?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <parenthetical>( POWERFULLY MOVED )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes. It is.</dialogue>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SEMINAR ROOM,TRINITY HALL,CAMBRIDGE - DAY</stage_direction>

    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>Come in Stephen.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>STEPHEN makes his way slowly , laboriously , to stand in front of the three examiners .</scene_description>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How are you?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <parenthetical>( his speech has worsened )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Fine.</dialogue>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>Would you like to sit down?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>No thankyou.</dialogue>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>So. Chapters One -- full of holes and lacks mathematical support.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to KIP THORNE )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Professor Thorne?</dialogue>
    <character>KIP THORNE</character>
    <dialogue>Chapter Two -- not really original -- uses a lot of Roger's ideas.</dialogue>
    <character>PENROSE</character>
    <dialogue>Well at least you run with them. Chapter Three? Too many unanswered questions.</dialogue>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>But Four?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Silence . STEPHEN waits , as the PANEL turn the pages of his thesis . STEPHEN grows WORRIED .</scene_description>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A black hole at the beginning of Time.</dialogue>
    <character>KIP THORNE</character>
    <dialogue>A spacetime singularity?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SCIAMA and PENROSE and KIP THORNE look at each other . STEPHEN ca n't breath for the tension .</scene_description>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>Brilliant. It's brilliant Stephen. So all that remains to be said is... well done. Or should I say, well done Doctor. And extraordinary theory.</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>Thankyou.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>STEPHEN sighs with RELIEF , and smiles .</scene_description>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>So, what now?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>Prove it. Prove... with a single equation, that Time has a beginning. Would n't that be nice Professor? One single elegant equation to explain everything?</dialogue>
    <character>SCIAMA</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. It would. It would indeed.</dialogue>

  <scene>

    <dialogue>TO DOCTOR-</dialogue>
    <character>BRIAN</character>
    <dialogue>-Who?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Over laughter -</scene_description>

    <scene_description>BRIAN holds forth on a funny story about him and Stephen , as he uncorks a bottle of wine -</scene_description>
    <character>BRIAN</character>
    <dialogue>What's astonishing is that for Stephen and I, `` work'' was the worst four-letter word, the worst.</dialogue>

    <parenthetical>( LAUGHTER )</parenthetical>

    <character>JANE</character>

    <dialogue>I'm sorry.</dialogue>

Hearing something , he looks up - The TWO YEAR-OLD ROBERT has woken , and stands in his pajamas at the BABY-GATE at the top of the stairs , looking down at his father .</scene_description>

    <scene_description>JANE and STEPHEN sip tea . Holding a cup is extremely difficult for him . A new tension exists between them . She watches him .   <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DINING ROOM,LITTLE ST MARY'S LANE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The NEW BABY 'S CRIES carry ( from UPSTAIRS ) as JANE helps STEPHEN on with his PYJAMA TOP . She struggles to pull it down over his head when the BABY 's cries grow too urgent .</scene_description>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>Go Jane.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>One second.</dialogue>

    <scene_description>CUT TO :</scene_description>
    <scene_description>INSIDE HIS PYJAMA . It 's dark . STEPHEN , helpless . His eyes are wide open , looking through the grain in the fabric at the OPEN FIRE , burning in the FIREPLACE .</scene_description>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <dialogue>JANE?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Silence . He waits ... The pin points of fire-light through the fabric , SLOWLY MORPH into STARS and a NIGHT SKY . This is what STEPHEN is visualizing . We see what he sees -- The LIFE OF THE UNIVERSE IN REVERSE ... STARS being pulled back together , toward a single POINT , a SINGULARITY . As the SINGULARITY takes SHAPE , a DARK CIRCLE FORMS AROUND IT , rimmed by a GLOWING CIRCULAR HORIZON . FINALLY - A BLACK HOLE has FORMED . A POINT IN SPACE , GOBBLING STARS , ILLUMINATED ONLY AT ITS EDGES ( EVENT HORIZON ) BY AN AMBIENT GLOW - A RING of LIGHT . The REVERIE ends as JANE eases the PYJAMA down over his head , returning STEPHEN back into the real world . He stares at his wife , AWESTRUCK .</scene_description>
    <character>JANE</character>
    <dialogue>Are you alright?</dialogue>
    <character>STEPHEN</character>
    <parenthetical>( breathless , stunned )</parenthetical>

    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D )</parenthetical>

    "summary":"University of Cambridge astrophysics student Stephen Hawking begins a relationship with literature student Jane Wilde. Although Stephen is intelligent, his friends and professors are concerned about his lack of a thesis topic. After he and his professor Dennis Sciama attend a lecture on black holes, Stephen speculates that black holes may have been part of the creation of the universe, and decides to write his thesis on them. However, Stephen's muscles begin to fail, giving him decreasing coordination with his body. He learns he has motor neuron disease, which will eventually leave him unable to move, swallow, and even breathe. There are no treatments, and he has approximately two years to live. The doctor assures Stephen that his brain will not be affected, so his thoughts and intelligence will remain intact, but eventually, he will be unable to communicate them. As Stephen becomes reclusive, focusing on his work, Jane confesses she loves him. She tells his father she intends to stay with Stephen even as his condition worsens. They marry and have their first son, Robert. Stephen presents his thesis to the examination board, arguing that a black hole created the universe in a Big Bang, that it will emit heat, and end in a Big Crunch. He begins using a wheelchair after his walking ability deteriorates. After the Hawkings have their daughter Lucy, Stephen develops a theory about the visibility of black holes and becomes a world-renowned physicist. Jane, focusing on the children as well as Stephen's health and increasing fame, is unable to work on her own thesis and becomes frustrated. Stephen tells her he will understand if she needs help. She joins a church choir, where she meets widower Jonathan and they become close friends. She employs him as a piano teacher for Robert, and Jonathan befriends the entire family, helping Stephen with his illness, supporting Jane, and playing with the children. When Jane gives birth to another son, Timothy, Stephen's mother asks Jane if the baby is Jonathan's, which she denies. Jonathan is appalled, but when he and Jane are alone, they admit their feelings for one another. He distances himself from the family, but Stephen tells him Jane needs him. While attending an opera performance in Bordeaux, Stephen is taken ill and rushed to a hospital. The doctor informs Jane that he has pneumonia, and that he needs a tracheotomy to survive, but it will leave him mute. She agrees to the surgery. Stephen learns to use a spelling board, and uses it to communicate with Elaine, his new nurse. He receives a computer with a built-in voice synthesizer, and uses it to write a book, A Brief History of Time (1988), which becomes an international best-seller. Stephen tells Jane he has been invited to the United States to accept an award and will be taking Elaine with him. Jane faces the realization that the marriage has not been working, telling him she "did her best", and they agree to divorce. Stephen goes to the lecture with Elaine, the two have fallen in love, and Jane and Jonathan reunite. At the lecture, Stephen sees a student drop a pen; he imagines getting up to return it, almost crying at the reminder of how his disease has affected him. He goes on to give a speech telling audiences to pursue their ambitions despite the harsh reality of life: "While there's life, there is hope". Stephen invites Jane to meet Queen Elizabeth II with him when being made a member of the Order of the Companions of Honour; they share a happy day together with their grandchildren. An extended closing series comprises select moments from the film; shown in reverse, back to the moment Stephen first saw Jane; the reversal is reminiscent of Stephen's research methodology of reversing time to understand the beginning of the universe. Later, Jane and Jonathan marry, and she completes her Doctor of Philosophy. She and Stephen remain close friends. Stephen declines a knighthood from the Queen and continues his research, with no plans to retire in the near future."

    "summary":"Peter Gibbons is a frustrated and unmotivated programmer who works at a company called Initech. His co-workers include fellow programmers Samir Nagheenanajar and Michael Bolton, as well as Milton Waddams, a meek collator who is mostly ignored by the rest of the office. The staff constantly suffer under callous management, especially Initech's smarmy vice president Bill Lumbergh, whom Peter loathes. Peter's girlfriend Anne persuades him to attend a hypnotherapy session. Dr. Swanson, the therapist, dies of a heart attack while hypnotizing Peter. A newly-relaxed and self-confident Peter acts on the impulse to skip the next workday, and he ignores phone calls from Lumbergh and Anne, who angrily breaks up with him and admits she was cheating on him. Peter soon asks and takes Joanna, a restaurant waitress, out for a date. Meanwhile, a pair of business consultants, Bob Slydell and Bob Porter (colloquially known as the Bobs), are brought in to help the company downsize. Peter finally shows up at work and casually disregards office protocol, including violating Initech's dress code, taking Lumbergh's reserved parking spot, refusing to follow Lumbergh's directions, and removing a cubicle wall that blocks his view out the window. The Bobs are impressed by his frank insights into the office problems, and they decide to promote him against Lumbergh's will and support. Michael and Samir, however, are fired. Milton is also expected to be eliminated, but it is learned that Milton's contract had been terminated five years prior, of which Milton and the accounting department were not informed. To avoid confrontation and riding on the hope that the issue will resolve itself naturally, the Bobs and Lumbergh inform only the accounting department and cease Milton's salary payments. Peter, Michael, and Samir decide to take revenge by infecting Initech's accounting system with a computer virus designed to divert fractions of pennies into a bank account. They believe that such transactions are small enough to avoid detection but will result in the accrual of a substantial amount of money over time. On Michael and Samir's last day at Initech, Peter steals a frequently malfunctioning printer, which the three take to a field and smash to pieces to vent their frustration. Peter then discovers that a bug in Michael's code has caused their virus to steal over $300,000 in only a few days, which is far more conspicuous. Peter plans to accept full responsibility for the crime and writes out a confession, which he slips under Lumbergh's office door late at night, along with traveler's checks for the stolen money. The next morning, Milton enters Lumbergh's office to reclaim a stolen red Swingline stapler, but instead finds and claims the letter and traveler's checks. He then makes good on an oft-repeated threat and ignites the building, which destroys all evidence against Peter. Samir and Michael begin new jobs at Initech's rival Initrode, while Peter lands a dream job as a construction worker with his neighbor Lawrence. Milton uses the money from the traveler's checks to vacation in Mexico."

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. GOOGLEPLEX - TEAM LYLE BULLPEN - THE NEXT MORNING</stage_direction>

    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Nap pod.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>-- and continues off. Lyle examines his phone. On screen some code-looking stuff ending in "fuuuuuuukkkkk uuuuuuu".</scene_description>
    <character>LYLE</character>
    <dialogue>What is this?</dialogue>

    <dialogue>What if Google was your friend?</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Hmm?</dialogue>

    <dialogue>What if your Droid wouldn't let you text or email after 2am unless you'd correctly answered a question?</dialogue>

    <character>JOE</character>

    <dialogue>In life fifteen minutes. Maybe get some breakfast first.</dialogue>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. NAP POD ROOM - SAME</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ollie tiptoes in. Settles into a pod, placing a cold blindfold over his eyes. Exhales a little too loudly. Shifts around. Clears his throat. All this noise awakens DANA, who lies in a pod nearby. She opens one eye. Sees that it's him, not pleased.</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(points to sign)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This is a "shhh" zone.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>(happy to see her)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh, hey. Sorry about that.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(a quiet moment, then)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You seem stressed. What's wrong?</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>I'm pretty sure it's the combination of trying to take a nap and you.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>C'mon. Tell me what's bothering you?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(genuine)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I actually want to know. To be honest, it's a surprise to me.</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(sits up)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm leaving.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>No, wait. You were here. I'll go.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(about to get up)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But before I do, I'll tell you why you're stressed.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(she shakes her head)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's because you spend your whole life at the office. Admittedly, it's an office with dog runs and hovercars and nap pods which I'm sure are normally very relaxing, but it's still an office. And one day, maybe not tomorrow but soon, you're going to wake up and wonder what happened to the everything else part.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(rises)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Take it from the 40-year-old with nothing else.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He pads for the door, when --</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(in spite of herself)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I already feel that way.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns back, pleasantly surprised he's gotten through.</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(this is hard for her)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ever since I turned 30, I can't go on Facebook because it's all babies. Old friends' kids getting food on their faces and wearing socks that look like tiny sneakers and they're so fucking adorable and I hate them.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>(sits)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>They're the absolute worst.</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>I want what those friends have. I want a little piece of "everything else". Only you're right -- my 20s was nothing but work. Which means I'm ten years behind. Those women already did their dozens of bad dates and the long-term relationship with that guy with the body hair shoulder-pads--</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(Ollie winces)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>--and then, finally, found the person to procreate with. And I'm--</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Back at the beginning of something and that's scary.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She nods. Surprised he understands.</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>God, it felt good to say that out loud.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah?</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(exhales)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yeah.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She shuts her eyes. He considers for a moment, then truly opens up --</scene_description>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>This has been hard for me, too. Starting over. But it's also been good. To know it's not too late to try new things.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Like video hangouts or an actual grown-up conversation with someone I'm attracted to.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(then)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It does feel good to say that out loud, huh?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns to her to see...she's asleep. Makes a little snoring noise. He sighs. A beat, then... She smiles --</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(eyes still closed)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm just fucking with you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He throws a pillow at her. She throws one back.</scene_description>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Can I make a couple suggestions? One, you need to get the hell out of this building. And, two, I'm such a mountain of mistakes that a date with me will be like ten years of bad experience in one shot. So let me take you out to dinner.</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>You realize that's a total red paddle.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>There's your first mistake right there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Off her smile, we CUT TO -- AN IPOD snapped into a DOCK. A finger touches through the screens to bring up a PLAYLIST: get-psyched mix DIGITAL EDITION! MUSIC: A modern getting psyched selection, ie David Guetta.</scene_description>
  </scene>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. BALLFIELD - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MUSIC: Dramatic NFL Films-style war march. Steam rises off the field. Our warriors march in...with broomsticks between their legs. Graham's team wears perfect matching Harry Potter striped outfits, goggles and capes. Our team dons a hodgepodge of mismatched workout junk.</scene_description>

    <dialogue>Cliffs Notes the rules for us again?</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Right. The Beaters toss the Bludgers at the Chasers before they can get the Quaffle through the--</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Use your Muggle words.</dialogue>
    <character>LYLE</character>
    <dialogue>You have to peg them with the kickballs before they throw the volleyballs through the hoop and they're meanwhile trying to stop your volleyballs with their kickballs. And then the tennis ball--</dialogue>

Each competitor holds a broom between their legs at all times, forcing them both to look ridiculous and to grab the balls with one hand. Joe and Ollie may be better athletes but they have a tenuous grasp on the rules...</scene_description>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <parenthetical>(re: kickball)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Should I take the Beater?</dialogue>
    <character>STUART</character>
    <dialogue>You're the Beater. That's the Bludger.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Graham easily scores a hoop. Then another. Dodges our guys' throws. Joe grabs a volleyball and attempts to score but gets beaned by a few Bludgers. Our boys are getting their asses handed to them. Graham dunks a ball, Joe falling to the turf.</scene_description>
    <character>GRAHAM</character>
    <dialogue>May as well throw in the Snitch. You boys are dead.</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Time out! Are there time outs? Broom break!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Moments Later: A HUDDLE with our team.</scene_description>
    <character>YO-YO</character>
    <dialogue>Graham's right. It's over.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>(winded)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hold on a second. Maybe the problem is we're too focused on scoring more points than them.</dialogue>
    <character>LYLE</character>
    <dialogue>That's how you win. I thought you guys knew sports.</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <parenthetical>(catching his breath)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>We do, Lyle. Like the old Detroit Pistons -- this is back when you were all still in short pants chasing the Good Humor truck -- they couldn't outskill Michael Jordan's Bulls, right? So they out physical'd 'em. A Bull drove, they ended up on the hardwood. Laimbeer gave them a reason to think twice before coming into the paint next time down the court. You follow me?</dialogue>
    <character>ALL</character>
    <dialogue>Nope. / Not at all. / That's the Hanes guy, right? / The black man with the Hitler moustache?</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Just follow our lead.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Moments Later: Gameplay resumes. Graham drives for a hoop. Joe grabs Graham's broom and yanks it into his balls, sending him flying into the hoop pole. Computer Guy lifts a --</scene_description>
    <character>COMPUTER GUY</character>
    <dialogue>Yellow wand!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>That's a foul. Graham's going to feel that in the morning. Joe nods to his teammates, touching a finger to his nose as he heads to the PENALTY BOX.     <character>GRAHAM</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Chubby Kid)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Great tenacity, Augustus Gloop.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Computer Guy blows a whistle --</scene_description>
    <character>COMPUTER GUY</character>
    <dialogue>Score's tied. Next Quaffle wins!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A final run to the balls. Graham is the only member of his team who refuses to stand down. Makes a final push alone, head to head with Joe --</scene_description>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Looks like we're not so dead after all. Turns out we were just chilling at a train station in wizard heaven and now we're back to finish your ass.</dialogue>
    <character>GRAHAM</character>
    <dialogue>Never!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Graham grabs a volleyball and scrambles off. Joe and Ollie share a look -- that was dramatic. Joe wails a throw, connecting with a Bludger to Graham's head. Stuart snatches a volleyball, runs up to the opposing team's hoop (it's the height of a kids' basket) and DUNKS the ball, hanging on the rim.     "summary":"University of Cambridge astrophysics student Stephen Hawking begins a relationship with literature student Jane Wilde. Although Stephen is intelligent, his friends and professors are concerned about his lack of a thesis topic. After he and his professor Dennis Sciama attend a lecture on black holes, Stephen speculates that black holes may have been part of the creation of the universe, and decides to write his thesis on them. However, Stephen's muscles begin to fail, giving him decreasing coordination with his body. He learns he has motor neuron disease, which will eventually leave him unable to move, swallow, and even breathe. There are no treatments, and he has approximately two years to live. The doctor assures Stephen that his brain will not be affected, so his thoughts and intelligence will remain intact, but eventually, he will be unable to communicate them. As Stephen becomes reclusive, focusing on his work, Jane confesses she loves him. She tells his father she intends to stay with Stephen even as his condition worsens. They marry and have their first son, Robert. Stephen presents his thesis to the examination board, arguing that a black hole created the universe in a Big Bang, that it will emit heat, and end in a Big Crunch. He begins using a wheelchair after his walking ability deteriorates. After the Hawkings have their daughter Lucy, Stephen develops a theory about the visibility of black holes and becomes a world-renowned physicist. Jane, focusing on the children as well as Stephen's health and increasing fame, is unable to work on her own thesis and becomes frustrated. Stephen tells her he will understand if she needs help. She joins a church choir, where she meets widower Jonathan and they become close friends. She employs him as a piano teacher for Robert, and Jonathan befriends the entire family, helping Stephen with his illness, supporting Jane, and playing with the children. When Jane gives birth to another son, Timothy, Stephen's mother asks Jane if the baby is Jonathan's, which she denies. Jonathan is appalled, but when he and Jane are alone, they admit their feelings for one another. He distances himself from the family, but Stephen tells him Jane needs him. While attending an opera performance in Bordeaux, Stephen is taken ill and rushed to a hospital. The doctor informs Jane that he has pneumonia, and that he needs a tracheotomy to survive, but it will leave him mute. She agrees to the surgery. Stephen learns to use a spelling board, and uses it to communicate with Elaine, his new nurse. He receives a computer with a built-in voice synthesizer, and uses it to write a book, A Brief History of Time (1988), which becomes an international best-seller. Stephen tells Jane he has been invited to the United States to accept an award and will be taking Elaine with him. Jane faces the realization that the marriage has not been working, telling him she "did her best", and they agree to divorce. Stephen goes to the lecture with Elaine, the two have fallen in love, and Jane and Jonathan reunite. At the lecture, Stephen sees a student drop a pen; he imagines getting up to return it, almost crying at the reminder of how his disease has affected him. He goes on to give a speech telling audiences to pursue their ambitions despite the harsh reality of life: "While there's life, there is hope". Stephen invites Jane to meet Queen Elizabeth II with him when being made a member of the Order of the Companions of Honour; they share a happy day together with their grandchildren. An extended closing series comprises select moments from the film; shown in reverse, back to the moment Stephen first saw Jane; the reversal is reminiscent of Stephen's research methodology of reversing time to understand the beginning of the universe. Later, Jane and Jonathan marry, and she completes her Doctor of Philosophy. She and Stephen remain close friends. Stephen declines a knighthood from the Queen and continues his research, with no plans to retire in the near future."

    "summary":"Peter Gibbons is a frustrated and unmotivated programmer who works at a company called Initech. His co-workers include fellow programmers Samir Nagheenanajar and Michael Bolton, as well as Milton Waddams, a meek collator who is mostly ignored by the rest of the office. The staff constantly suffer under callous management, especially Initech's smarmy vice president Bill Lumbergh, whom Peter loathes. Peter's girlfriend Anne persuades him to attend a hypnotherapy session. Dr. Swanson, the therapist, dies of a heart attack while hypnotizing Peter. A newly-relaxed and self-confident Peter acts on the impulse to skip the next workday, and he ignores phone calls from Lumbergh and Anne, who angrily breaks up with him and admits she was cheating on him. Peter soon asks and takes Joanna, a restaurant waitress, out for a date. Meanwhile, a pair of business consultants, Bob Slydell and Bob Porter (colloquially known as the Bobs), are brought in to help the company downsize. Peter finally shows up at work and casually disregards office protocol, including violating Initech's dress code, taking Lumbergh's reserved parking spot, refusing to follow Lumbergh's directions, and removing a cubicle wall that blocks his view out the window. The Bobs are impressed by his frank insights into the office problems, and they decide to promote him against Lumbergh's will and support. Michael and Samir, however, are fired. Milton is also expected to be eliminated, but it is learned that Milton's contract had been terminated five years prior, of which Milton and the accounting department were not informed. To avoid confrontation and riding on the hope that the issue will resolve itself naturally, the Bobs and Lumbergh inform only the accounting department and cease Milton's salary payments. Peter, Michael, and Samir decide to take revenge by infecting Initech's accounting system with a computer virus designed to divert fractions of pennies into a bank account. They believe that such transactions are small enough to avoid detection but will result in the accrual of a substantial amount of money over time. On Michael and Samir's last day at Initech, Peter steals a frequently malfunctioning printer, which the three take to a field and smash to pieces to vent their frustration. Peter then discovers that a bug in Michael's code has caused their virus to steal over $300,000 in only a few days, which is far more conspicuous. Peter plans to accept full responsibility for the crime and writes out a confession, which he slips under Lumbergh's office door late at night, along with traveler's checks for the stolen money. The next morning, Milton enters Lumbergh's office to reclaim a stolen red Swingline stapler, but instead finds and claims the letter and traveler's checks. He then makes good on an oft-repeated threat and ignites the building, which destroys all evidence against Peter. Samir and Michael begin new jobs at Initech's rival Initrode, while Peter lands a dream job as a construction worker with his neighbor Lawrence. Milton uses the money from the traveler's checks to vacation in Mexico."

    <stage_direction>INT. NAP POD ROOM - SAME</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ollie tiptoes in. Settles into a pod, placing a cold blindfold over his eyes. Exhales a little too loudly. Shifts around. Clears his throat. All this noise awakens DANA, who lies in a pod nearby. She opens one eye. Sees that it's him, not pleased.</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(points to sign)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This is a "shhh" zone.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>(happy to see her)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh, hey. Sorry about that.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(a quiet moment, then)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You seem stressed. What's wrong?</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>I'm pretty sure it's the combination of trying to take a nap and you.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>C'mon. Tell me what's bothering you?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(genuine)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I actually want to know. To be honest, it's a surprise to me.</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(sits up)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm leaving.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>No, wait. You were here. I'll go.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(about to get up)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But before I do, I'll tell you why you're stressed.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(she shakes her head)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's because you spend your whole life at the office. Admittedly, it's an office with dog runs and hovercars and nap pods which I'm sure are normally very relaxing, but it's still an office. And one day, maybe not tomorrow but soon, you're going to wake up and wonder what happened to the everything else part.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(rises)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Take it from the 40-year-old with nothing else.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He pads for the door, when --</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(in spite of herself)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I already feel that way.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns back, pleasantly surprised he's gotten through.</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(this is hard for her)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ever since I turned 30, I can't go on Facebook because it's all babies. Old friends' kids getting food on their faces and wearing socks that look like tiny sneakers and they're so fucking adorable and I hate them.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>(sits)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>They're the absolute worst.</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>I want what those friends have. I want a little piece of "everything else". Only you're right -- my 20s was nothing but work. Which means I'm ten years behind. Those women already did their dozens of bad dates and the long-term relationship with that guy with the body hair shoulder-pads--</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(Ollie winces)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>--and then, finally, found the person to procreate with. And I'm--</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Back at the beginning of something and that's scary.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She nods. Surprised he understands.</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>God, it felt good to say that out loud.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah?</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(exhales)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yeah.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She shuts her eyes. He considers for a moment, then truly opens up --</scene_description>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>This has been hard for me, too. Starting over. But it's also been good. To know it's not too late to try new things.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Like video hangouts or an actual grown-up conversation with someone I'm attracted to.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>(then)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It does feel good to say that out loud, huh?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns to her to see...she's asleep. Makes a little snoring noise. He sighs. A beat, then... She smiles --</scene_description>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <parenthetical>(eyes still closed)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm just fucking with you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He throws a pillow at her. She throws one back.</scene_description>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Can I make a couple suggestions? One, you need to get the hell out of this building. And, two, I'm such a mountain of mistakes that a date with me will be like ten years of bad experience in one shot. So let me take you out to dinner.</dialogue>
    <character>DANA</character>
    <dialogue>You realize that's a total red paddle.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <dialogue>There's your first mistake right there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Off her smile, we CUT TO -- AN IPOD snapped into a DOCK. A finger touches through the screens to bring up a PLAYLIST: get-psyched mix DIGITAL EDITION! MUSIC: A modern getting psyched selection, ie David Guetta.</scene_description>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. BALLFIELD - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MUSIC: Dramatic NFL Films-style war march. Steam rises off the field. Our warriors march in...with broomsticks between their legs. Graham's team wears perfect matching Harry Potter striped outfits, goggles and capes. Our team dons a hodgepodge of mismatched workout junk.</scene_description>

    <dialogue>Use your Muggle words.</dialogue>

Each competitor holds a broom between their legs at all times, forcing them both to look ridiculous and to grab the balls with one hand. Joe and Ollie may be better athletes but they have a tenuous grasp on the rules...</scene_description>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <parenthetical>(re: kickball)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Should I take the Beater?</dialogue>
    <character>STUART</character>
    <dialogue>You're the Beater. That's the Bludger.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Graham easily scores a hoop. Then another. Dodges our guys' throws. Joe grabs a volleyball and attempts to score but gets beaned by a few Bludgers. Our boys are getting their asses handed to them. Graham dunks a ball, Joe falling to the turf.</scene_description>
    <character>GRAHAM</character>
    <dialogue>May as well throw in the Snitch. You boys are dead.</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Time out! Are there time outs? Broom break!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Moments Later: A HUDDLE with our team.</scene_description>
    <character>YO-YO</character>
    <dialogue>Graham's right. It's over.</dialogue>
    <character>OLLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>(winded)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hold on a second. Maybe the problem is we're too focused on scoring more points than them.</dialogue>
    <character>LYLE</character>
    <dialogue>That's how you win. I thought you guys knew sports.</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <parenthetical>(catching his breath)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>We do, Lyle. Like the old Detroit Pistons -- this is back when you were all still in short pants chasing the Good Humor truck -- they couldn't outskill Michael Jordan's Bulls, right? So they out physical'd 'em. A Bull drove, they ended up on the hardwood. Laimbeer gave them a reason to think twice before coming into the paint next time down the court. You follow me?</dialogue>
    <character>ALL</character>
    <dialogue>Nope. / Not at all. / That's the Hanes guy, right? / The black man with the Hitler moustache?</dialogue>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Just follow our lead.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Moments Later: Gameplay resumes. Graham drives for a hoop. Joe grabs Graham's broom and yanks it into his balls, sending him flying into the hoop pole. Computer Guy lifts a --</scene_description>
    <character>COMPUTER GUY</character>
    <dialogue>Yellow wand!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>That's a foul. Graham's going to feel that in the morning. Joe nods to his teammates, touching a finger to his nose as he heads to the PENALTY BOX. Quick Shots: Joe, Ollie, and four formerly passive geeks are the Bad Boys of intramural Quidditch. Leg sweeps. Cape pulls. Broom trips. Yo-Yo gives the "not-in-my-house" finger wag. The intimidation is working -- Chubby Kid has no interest in driving the lane. Tosses the ball over to the other side. Our team scores.</scene_description>
    <character>GRAHAM</character>
    <parenthetical>(to Chubby Kid)</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Great tenacity, Augustus Gloop.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Computer Guy blows a whistle --</scene_description>
    <character>COMPUTER GUY</character>
    <dialogue>Score's tied. Next Quaffle wins!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A final run to the balls. Graham is the only member of his team who refuses to stand down. Makes a final push alone, head to head with Joe --</scene_description>
    <character>JOE</character>
    <dialogue>Looks like we're not so dead after all. Turns out we were just chilling at a train station in wizard heaven and now we're back to finish your ass.</dialogue>
    <character>GRAHAM</character>
    <dialogue>Never!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Graham grabs a volleyball and scrambles off. Joe and Ollie share a look -- that was dramatic. Joe wails a throw, connecting with a Bludger to Graham's head. Stuart snatches a volleyball, runs up to the opposing team's hoop (it's the height of a kids' basket) and DUNKS the ball, hanging on the rim.     "summary":"After salesmen Billy McMahon and Nick Campbell's employer goes out of business, Billy applies for Google internships for them both. They are accepted due to their unorthodox interview answers, despite a lack of relevant experience and not being of traditional collegiate age. They will spend the summer competing in teams against other interns in a variety of tasks, with only members of the winning team guaranteed jobs with Google. Billy and Nick's team is led by Lyle, who constantly tries to act hip to hide his insecurities, and its other members are seen as rejects: the smartphone-addicted Stuart, the tiger-parented Filipino Yo-Yo, and Indian American nerd-related kink enthusiast Neha.
