    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD (GAGE'S POV)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A big tanker truck - silver body , ORINCO written on the side in blue letters - blasts by .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE, BY THE CAT CARRIER</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The windlash if the passing truck blows GAGE 'S hair back from his forehead . We should be scared here - not by the truck , but by GAGE 'S lack of fear . He 's smiling , happy .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Druck!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts down the driveway toward the road .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, RACHEL, ELLIE (AT THE SWING)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ELLIE has been disentangled from the swing . She 's sitting by the wreckage at the end of the driveway , weeping hysterically -LRB- as much from tiredness as from pain , I think -RRB- as LOUIS and RACHEL examine her scraped knee . The wound does n't look too serious .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( to RACHEL . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Would you get the first aid kit?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( screaming . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Not the stingy stuff! I do n't want the stingy stuff, daddy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL suddenly looks around toward :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE FRONT OF THE WAGON (RACHEL'S POV)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>No one there .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, ELLIE, LOUIS, BY THE SWING</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Gage's gone!</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Jesus, the road!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They get up together .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE, AT THE EDGE OF THE ROAD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A truck is coming . A great big one .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ANGLE ON THE TRUCK, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The grille looks like a tombstone that 's learned how to snarl .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He takes a step into the road . and then big , gnarled hands grab him . GAGE looks rather surprised at this , but not worried - this kid is used to being picked up and treated humanely . To GAGE strangers are as interesting as . well , as interesting as Orinco trucks .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE AND JUD CRANDALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The fellow who has picked GAGE up is a man of about eighty in old blue jeans , a faded Bruce Springsteen t - shirt . Over this he wears a faded khaki vest with bright silver buttons . His face is deeply wrinkled and kindly .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD CRANDALL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to GAGE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No you do n't, my friend - not in that road.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But he softens this with a grin . GAGE grins back at him .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Drucks!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( low . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No shit, Sherlock.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD carries him up the driveway to the station wagon . Here he 's joined by LOUIS and RACHEL , out of breath and really scared . ELLIE brings up the rear . She 's still sniffling .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Gage!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( hands him to her . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>He was headed for the road, looked like. I corralled him for you, missus.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you. Thank you so much.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes - thanks. I'm Louis Creed.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He sticks out his hand and JUD shakes it . LOUIS takes it easy - no crushing JayCees grip , or anything like that - the old guy looks as if he might have arthritis .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Jud Crandall. I live just across the road.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>I'm Rachel. Thanks again for saving the wandering minstrel boy, here.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No harm, no foul. But you want to watch out for that road. Those damn trucks go back and forth all day and most of the night.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He leans over toward ELLIE .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Who might you be, little Miss?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>I'm Ellen Creed and I live at 642 Alden Lane, Dearborn, Michigan.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>At least, I used to.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>And now you live on Route 9 in Ludlow, and your dad's gon na be the new doctor up to the college, I hear, and I think you're going to be just as happy as a clam here, Ellen Creed.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to LOUIS . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Are clams really happy?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They all laugh - even GAGE .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Excuse me, Mr. Crandall - I've got to change this kid. It's nice to meet you.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Same here. Come over and visit when you get the chance.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As RACHEL , carrying GAGE , moves away :</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( worries . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Daddy, do I really have to have the stingy stuff?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>No - I guess not.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yayyy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She goes belting off .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( amused . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I guess your daughter there ai n't going to die after all.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( also amused . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I guess not.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>House has stood empty for too long. It's damn good to see people in it again.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : A truck engine , gearing down .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  A MOVING VAN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It blinks and comes lumbering into the Creed 's driveway .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Hey - they actually found the place!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Movin' in's mighty thirsty work. I usually sit out on my porch of an evening and pour a couple of beers over m ` dinner. Come on over and join me, if you want.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well, maybe I -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Louis, what's this?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL AND GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>GAGE has been changed , and RACHEL is following him as he explores the nearest edges of the new homestead . They are fairly close to the wreckage of the tire swing , and here is the head of the path ELLIE has already glimpsed .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They cross to the van . The FIRST and SECOND MOVERS are just climbing out of the van .</scene_description>
    <character>FIRST MOVER</character>
    <dialogue>You Mr. Creed?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. Just a second.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL AND GAGE, AT THE HEAD OF THE PATH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's holding GAGE on her hip now , and both of them are looking at that strange -LRB- and oddly enticing -RRB- path which disappears into the deepening twilight . LOUIS and JUD join them .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>The movers -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Yes - I know. This path, Louis? Where does it go?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't have the slightest idea. When I saw the house, this field was under four feet of snow.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I bet Mr. Crandall knows!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD nods . He smiles , too , but underneath the smile we sense that he is serious .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, ayuh! I know. It's a good story, and a good walk, too. I'll take you up there sometime, and tell you the story, too - after you get settled in.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He smiles at them and they smile back - it is a look of understanding and real liking , in spite of the age difference between the CREEDS and JUD .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Crickets . Ree - ree - ree - ree . There 's one light upstairs , one downstairs . Perhaps we see the path , glimmering away into the field ? Either by virtue of it being mown , or by virtue of some gentle optical trick ? Maybe .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE LIVING ROOM  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There 's a light on in the kitchen , but it just casts a dim glow in here . The room has a fireplace and a lovely wooden floor . It 's going to be nice , but now it 's just a big bare box with movers ' cartons stacked all over the place . LOUIS is drinking a can of Pepsi , and he looks pretty damned tired - anyone who 's ever moved house and can remember the first night in the new place will understand . He finishes the last of the Pepsi and surveys the living room . He sits on one of the bigger boxes , takes cigarettes from his pocket , and lights one . He drops the spent match in the empty can , and taps into the can during the scene . SOUND : Feet coming down the stairs . The door on the far side of the room opens and RACHEL comes in , wearing a nightgown .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( crossing to LOUIS . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Kids are asleep, doc.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Great.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He hugs her . She hugs him back warmly - for a moment they are just two good people in all the big darkness of their new house .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>You're not really going over to have a beer with that old guy, are you?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I've got a million questions about the area, and -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>- and you'll end up doing a free consultation on his arthritis or urinary problems and -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Did you see his shirt?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( giggles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sure. Bruce Springsteen.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I really do have a million questions about the area. but the thing I'm really curious about is how come this octogenarian Yankee is decorating the slumped remains of his pecs with the Boss.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She laughs .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE PATH OF THE CRANDALL HOUSE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Pervasive SOUND of the crickets as LOUIS comes rather hesitantly up the crazy - paved path from the road 's edge .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That you, doc?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE SCREENED-IN PORCH OF THE CRANDALL HOUSE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We hear the SQUEAK of a rocker ; we see the dim red fitful glow of JUD 'S Pall Mall . We see by its glow that he is wearing Walkman earphones .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It's me.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE PORCH, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The Walkman is in his lap . He switches it off and puts the headphones casually around his neck , like a kid .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well, come on up and have a beer.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE PORCH, A SLIGHTLY WIDER SHOT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS comes on up . JUD has got a pail of ice beside his chair with some cans of beer in it . He opens one and hands it to LOUIS .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You need a glass?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Not at all.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Good for you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS drinks half the can at a draught .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>God, that's fine.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ai n't it just? The man who invented beer, Louis, that man was having a prime day for himself.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What were you listening to?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Allman Brothers.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>The Eat A Peach album. God, they were good before drugs and bad luck caught up with them. Listen to this, Louis.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He passes the headphones over . LOUIS puts them on . JUD presses the Walkman 's PLAY button . SOUND : Ramblin ' Man blasts us out of our seats . LOUIS winces and rakes the spidery earphones off his head .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I'm sorry. Wait.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns it down .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Try that.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS puts the earphones back on and listens for a few moments . It 's the instrumental break . Gregg and Duane Allman dueling hot Fenders . LOUIS takes the earphones off .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Nice.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I like rock and roll. No. I guess that's too mild. I love it. Since my ears started to die out on me, it's the only music I can really hear. And since my wife died. I dunno, some - times a little rock and roll fills up night. Not always, but sometimes.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>One more time - welcome to Ludlow. Hope your time here will be a happy one.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( great sincerity . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thank you, Mr. Crandall.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He drinks again - they both do . There 's a moment of companionable silence here , broken by the SOUND of a big truck . They look toward :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT/INT.  THE ROAD (THROUGH THE PORCH SCREEN)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One of those big tanker trucks goes rumbling by - now there are little amber running lights on top of it . It 's going fast , too - sweeps by in a blast of air .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE PORCH, WITH LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( wincing . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Jesus!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( lights a cigarette . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That's one mean road, all right - you remember that path your wife commented on?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>The one that goes into the woods - sure.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>That road - and those Orinco trucks - are the two main reasons it's there.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What's at the end of it?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Another day - after you get settled in a bit. Meantime, doc -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Here JUD raises his glass in a toast .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( continues . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Here's to your bones.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS clinks his glass against JUD 'S .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>And yours.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They drink .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ROUTE 9  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS crosses from the CRANDALL side to his own , and the CAMERA FOLLOWS as he walks slowly up the driveway and past the wagon . He pauses for a moment , looking thoughtfully - hopefully - at his new house . Then something - the CRY of an OWL , perhaps - draws his attention the other way . toward the path . He walks to its head and stands looking out at it - it glimmers in a wide cut swath that 's a bit ghostly in the dark . A SHAPE suddenly lurches out of the high grass at him , and LOUIS recoils with a startled , muffled cry .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The cat , sure ; who - or what - else ? We see his big green eyes in the dark as he cries his strange feline hello : Waow !</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND CHURCH, AT THE HEAD OF THE PATH</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Church! God, you scared the life out of me!</dialogue>
    <character>CHURCH</character>
    <dialogue>Waow!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS bends and picks up the cat . As he does , that truck SOUND comes again and he looks toward :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Another Orinco tanker drones by , fast .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( to the cat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I know one thing that will keep you home, good buddy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts toward the house . BLACK . And in that blackness , we see a second title card : THE DEAD SPEAK .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  A KITCHEN BLACKBOARD, CU  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Written on it is : MONDAY 1 . -RRB- CHURCH SPAYED 10 A.M. QUENTIN JOLANDER , D.V.M. And below , in even bigger letters : 2 . -RRB- ELLIE 'S FIRST DAY OF SCHOOL ! THE CAMERA PANS LEFT , showing us the kitchen . There are still a few cardboard cartons around , but the place is getting in shape . We look out the window and see the CREEDS , led by JUD CRANDALL , climbing the path toward the woods . LOUIS has got GAGE in a Gerrypak .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  AT THE TOP OF THE HILL, WITH CREEDS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They are also at the edge of the woods . JUD stops and lets them catch up .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Take a look behind you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They turn around , and their faces express their wonder .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>My God!</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>It's beautiful!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE VIEW</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is indeed beautiful . The CREED house is in the f.g. , Route 9 just behind it -LRB- with one of the ever - present Orinco trucks droning along -RRB- , but behind that is the great sweep of the Penobscot river valley , dozing under a fall sky of clear blue .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  AT THE TOP OF THE HILL, WITH JUD AND THE CREEDS</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You folks ready to go on?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Sure.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>But where are we going, Mr. Crandall?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You'll see soon enough, hon.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They go into the woods , still following the path .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  FOREST  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>These are old woods indeed - huge trunks with dusty sunlight shafting through them . It looks as though man has never made his mark here . THE CAMERA PANS SLOWLY DOWN to them , on the path . Here it is carpeted with pine needles , but it is just as clearly marked . JUD stops . LOUIS looks glad of the rest ; he 's sweating and there are wide dark patches under his arms where the Gerrypak 's straps are .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Who owns the woods up ahead? Paper companies?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Nope. The Micmac Indians. What's up ahead is all that's left of their tribal lands.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( giggling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Micmac, Ricmac, Kickmac, Sickmac.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ayuh, it's a funny word, ai n't it? You tired of totin' that yowwen yet, doc?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Not yet. how much further is it?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Aw, you'll be okay. Less than a mile.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts off again , fresh as a daisy . ELLIE scampers after him . LOUIS rolls his eyes at his wife and RACHEL rolls hers back . Then they press on .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ARCH READING PET SEMATARY</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AND THE CREEDS, ON THE PATH</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( stopping . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This is the place, honey.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE is of course second . Se tries to read the words on the arch but ca n't . She whips around to look at her mother .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What's it say, mommy?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A strange expression has come over RACHEL 'S face - she does n't like this . Not a bit .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>It says Pet Cemetery, hon. It's misspelled, but. that's what it says.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She runs for the arch . RACHEL starts ; looks more uneasy than ever .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Ellen -!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's almost under the arch . She looks back , questioning .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, LOUIS, JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( a bit lame . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Be careful.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She goes racing into the Pet Sematary .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, LOUIS, JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JUD lights a cigarette with a wooden match , using his thumbnail .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I told you it was a bad road, Louis - it's killed a lot of pets and made a lot of kids unhappy. But at least something good come of it. This place.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( excited voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mom! Dad! Y' oughtta see it!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE, AT THE EDGE OF THE SEMATARY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She surveys the rude markers with puzzled delight , then runs toward the center , pausing to investigate some of the markers as she goes . We clearly see the symmetrical pattern of rings .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, LOUIS, JUD</stage_direction>

    <dialogue>That's where I buried my dog Spot when he died of old age in 19 and 14. Dug it good and deep. By the time I finished, I had blisters all over my hands and a hell of a crick in my back. Soil's stony up here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE looks awed . LOUIS looks a little awed , too . JUD sweeps a hand around , indicating the whole sematary , but is still looking at ELLEN .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Do you know what this place is, Ellie? Oh, I know you know it's a boneyard, but a bone ai n't nothing and even a whole pile of'em do n't amount to much. Do you know what a graveyard really is?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Well. I guess not.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>It's a place where the dead speak, Missy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He sees her startled , uneasy expression and laughs . He ruffles her hair reassuringly .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No - not right out loud. Their stones speak. or their markers. Even if the marker ai n't nothing but a tin can someone wrote on with a Magic Marker, it speaks. Ai n't that so, Louis?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I think it is so, Ellie.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What if you ca n't read what's written on there anymore?</dialogue>

    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>And that someone cared enough about that animal to mark the spot.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>To remember.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes. To remember. This ai n't a scary place, Ellie. It's a place of rest and speaking. Can you remember that?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( a little awed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes, sir.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Rachel -!</dialogue>
