SOUND BLEEDS IN : Most of all the SOUND OF THE CRICKETS . They go to the door , and JUD is wordlessly elected as the prime honcho . He knocks . No answer . Again . No answer . SOUND : Crazy laughter .</scene_description>
    <character>BILL BATERMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>

    <dialogue>Oh holy Jesus lookit that.</dialogue>

    <character>BILL</character>
    <dialogue>You men get out of here!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I heard your boy was killed down Georgia.</dialogue>
    <character>BILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( agitated . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That was a mistake!</dialogue>
    <character>HANNIBAL</character>
    <dialogue>Was it?</dialogue>
    <character>BILL</character>
    <dialogue>You see him standing there, do n't you? Now get out! Get the Christ off my land!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now TIMMY turns around and comes shambling forward .</scene_description>
    <character>TIMMY</character>
    <parenthetical>( laughing . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ge ow! Ge Cwise off eye an!</dialogue>
    <character>GEORGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( revolted . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh Jesus, Jud! He's dead! I can smell him!</dialogue>
    <character>BILL</character>
    <dialogue>He ai n't dead! Give him a day or two and he'll be fine! Do n't you say that!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Bill, this ai n't right - you can see that yourself -</dialogue>
    <character>BILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( screaming . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>GET OUT! YOU HEAR? GET OUT!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  TIMMY BATERMAN/SEPIA</stage_direction>

    <parenthetical>( laughing . )</parenthetical>

    <scene_description>Abruptly he reaches up with both hands and scratches down his cheeks , goring deep grooves in his flesh . Blood flows sluggishly out . Very weird blood .</scene_description>

    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ENTIRE GROUP/SEPIA</stage_direction>

    <character>BILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( over his shoulder . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You want to get out of here before I get my shotgun! You boys are trespassing!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE FOUR MEN/SEPIA</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>God help you, Bill.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  BILL AND TIMMY BATERMAN/SEPIA</stage_direction>
    <character>BILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( snarls . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>God never helped me. I helped myself.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  TIMMY BATERMAN, CU/SEPIA</stage_direction>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>

    <parenthetical>( v.o . )</parenthetical>

    <scene_description>ELLIE is in the window - seat , asleep . RACHEL is holding a paperback but not reading it . Her eyes are red . She 's looking into space . CAMERA DRIFTS TO ELLIE . Her sleep is not easy . Her head turns from side to side , as if in negation . She becomes steadily more upset . She 's starting to mutter . Suddenly her eyes flare open and she screams .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JETLINER, SLIGHTLY WIDER</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We can see the GOLDMANS in the seats behind the CREEDS . They are startled . So are other passengers . A stewardess comes running .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Paxcow says it's almost too late!</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Ellie. Ellie. what.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Paxcow says it's almost too late! We have to go back! Paxcow says it's almost too late!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LUDLOW CEMETARY  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The CREED wagon turns in and drives up one of the lanes . It stops and LOUIS gets out .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He walks to a fresh grave on which the first flowers are already starting to wilt . He sits down and takes a flower . He plucks it , looking at the grave steadily . He says nothing for a long time .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It's wrong.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What happened to you is wrong.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE, IN THE FIELD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He runs toward THE CAMERA , happy and laughing , in SLOW MOTION .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY GAGE'S GRAVE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS is now weeping , but he seems calm just the same .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Remember, doc.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS looks at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  A TOMB, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PASCOW , bloody and mutilated , is standing by it .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>The barrier was not meant to be crossed. The ground is sour.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY GAGE'S GRAVE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He is not put out of countenance in the slightest by PASCOW 'S appearance ; he probably knows PASCOW is just a figment of his conscience or imagination , and so do we .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I'll tell you where the ground is sour - the ground in my heart is sour. Let me tell you something else, Vic - baby : Wrong is wrong.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  PASCOW</stage_direction>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>Timmy Baterman. That was wrong.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY GAGE'S GRAVE</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't talk like an asshole even if you are just a bit of underdone potato or a blot of mustard.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  PASCOW, BY THE TOMB</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He stands mute , just looking .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( weeping . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>He was my son! He was n't even two and he was run down in the fucking road and he was almost in pieces, and if you do n't think I'm going to try.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE TOMB, SANS PASCOW</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>VIC has put on his boogie shoes .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY GAGE'S GRAVE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's crying harder . Abruptly he reaches out at the floral tributes and knocks a bunch of them over .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>If it does n't work - if he comes back like Timmy Baterman - I'll put him to sleep. But I'm going to try.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>And if it does n't work. they do n't ever need to know.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GOLDMAN HOUSE IN LAKE FOREST, ILLINOIS  NIGHT</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  UPSTAIRS HALL  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA MOVES LEISURELY along this hallway , which is lined with pictures of RACHEL , ELLIE . and GAGE -LRB- there may even be a couple in which LOUIS is featured , but damned few -RRB- . Near the end of the hall a door is open and light spills out .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Honey, you just had a bad dream. You know that, do n't you?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It was n't a dream. It was Paxcow.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA GOES THROUGH THE DOOR and into the room where ELLIE is staying . She 's in bed , still badly upset . RACHEL is sitting on the bed beside her . There 's a single lamp on the bedside table .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Paxcow says Daddy's going to do something really bad. He -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Who is this Paxcow? Is he like the boogeyman?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>He's a ghost. But he's a good ghost.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL turns off the bed - lamp .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>There are no ghosts, Ellie. I want you to go to sleep and forget all this nonsense.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Will you at least call and make sure daddy's okay?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Of course I will.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She kisses ELLIE .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Now will you try to go to sleep?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( turns over on her side . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes, Mom.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL gets up and leaves the room .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE UPSTAIRS HALLWAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PASCOW is here , halfway down the hall to the stairs , bloody as ever . RACHEL does n't see him . She looks perplexed , a woman trying to think of something . She stops very near him .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to herself . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Paxcow, why do I know that name?</dialogue>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>Pascow.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL suddenly straightens . She looks startled and afraid .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Pascow? Was she saying Pascow?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She suddenly heads for the stairs , fast .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOME IN LUDLOW  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND : A car starting up . The station wagon backs out and heads down the driveway . As it passes THE CAMERA , we see LOUIS driving . The wagon turns onto Route 9 and heads off . CAMERA HOLDS ON THE HOUSE . A beat of silence . Then : the telephone starts ringing .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN LIVING ROOM  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>IRWIN and DORY are watching RACHEL with some anxiety . RACHEL is holding the phone to her ear . We can hear the FILTERED SOUND of one ring after another . She hangs up .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>He's not home.</dialogue>
    <character>DORY</character>
    <dialogue>Why, he probably went out for a hamburger or a chicken dinner, dear. You know how men are when they're alone.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Good old IRWIN 'S face says that maybe LOUIS went out for a couple of grams of coke and a whore in Nazi SS boots . RACHEL is dialing another number .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CRANDALL HOUSE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Phone starts to ring .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CRANDALL KITCHEN, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He shuffles to the telephone . His Walkman ` phones are around his neck . He 's got a bottle of beer in one hand .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( picks up . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hello - you got Judson.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN LIVING ROOM, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>It's Rachel Creed, Jud. I'm calling from Chicago.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( surprised voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Chicago! Is Louis with you?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>No. we're going to be here awhile, and he wanted a few days to wind up our affairs there. I just wondered if he was with you.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CRANDALL KITCHEN, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>His face says this is very serious .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No - but if he drops by, I'll tell him to call you.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN LIVING ROOM</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Jud, do you remember the name of the student that died on Louis's first day at work? The one that was hit by a car?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I do n't -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Was it Pascow?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CRANDALL KITCHEN, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ayuh, I think't was. If I see Louis come home before I go to bed, I'll tell him to -</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN LIVING ROOM, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't bother. I'm coming home.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( alarmed voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Rachel!</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you, Jud. Goodbye.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She hangs up .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CRANDALL KITCHEN, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No! Rachel! Do n't do that! Rachel -!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The buzz of an open line . Connection broken . JUD slowly replaces the receiver . The man looks very grim .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE FRONT HALL OF THE GOLDMAN HOUSE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL comes down the stairs , dressed for travelling . She 's carrying a suitcase in one hand . Her parents meet her at the foot of the stairs .</scene_description>
    <character>DORY</character>
    <dialogue>Rachel. darling. you're upset. a night's sleep.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>I have to go. The connections are tight, and I have to be at O'Hare in forty minutes. Will you drive me, daddy?</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <dialogue>You know something's wrong, do n't you? You know. And Ellie does, too.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Yes.</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <dialogue>I'll drive you.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mommy?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They all turn to :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  ELLIE, ON THE STAIRS</stage_direction>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Please hurry.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL AND THE GOLDMANS</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>I will. Come and kiss me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE races into her arms .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LUDLOW CEMETERY  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND Of a car engine , THROBBING AND LOW . It cuts off . CAMERA MOVES IN on the low stone wall between the cemetery and the road . Beyond it we can see the roof of the CREED station wagon . LOUIS appears , dressed in dark clothes . He looks both ways , then tosses a big duffle bag over the wall . Stuff clanks inside . LOUIS climbs over the wall , grabs his bag , and checks out the scene .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LUDLOW CEMETERY, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A quiet city of the dead . Spooky . SOUND of crickets : Ree - ree - ree .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He heads for GAGE 'S grave .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN CAR, WITH RACHEL AND IRWIN</stage_direction>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <dialogue>I'll come with you if you want, honey.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shakes her head . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I've got three planes to catch and I got the last seats on two of them. It's like God saved them for me.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  O'HARE UNITED AIRLINES TERMINAL, WITH IRWIN'S CAR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>IRWIN 'S car heads for it .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GRAVE OF GAGE CREED</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS approaches it slowly and sets down his bag of grave - robbing equipment . He sets aside the remaining floral tributes and then opens the bag and takes out the spade . He looks down at the grave for a long second .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( low . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gon na bust you out, son.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts to shovel .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE SHOVEL, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Digging . throwing . digging again . Already the shape of the excavation is beginning to show . The work is easy ; this earth is new and fresh .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JETLINER, IN A LINE-UP OF JETLINERS</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JETLINER, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Everyone looks impatient , but RACHEL looks half crazy .</scene_description>
    <character>PILOT</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This is the Captain speaking. I'm sorry about this delay, folks, but we've got a real low ceiling tonight and air traffic control's playing it safe. Looks like it's going to be about half an hour before we get on a roll, so I'm turning off the NO SMOKING sign.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Bing ! There 's a general groan . CAMERA MOVES IN ON RACHEL , who has closed her eyes . I think she 's praying .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE'S GRAVE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Now it 's pretty deep . Four feet , maybe . LOUIS is standing in it . We see his feet as the shovel goes up and down , up and down .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's sweating and dirt - streaked . He 's tossing dirt on a big pile . Suddenly , as he takes another shovelful , we hear a SCRAPING SOUND . He tosses the shovel aside and squats .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  IN THE GRAVE, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There 's a white streak on the bottom of the grave - the top of GAGE 'S coffin . LOUIS swipes his hand through the loose dirt , uncovering more , and then he begins to sweep off the top of the coffin with his hands .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CRANDALL PORCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JUD comes out . He 's wearing a light jacket . His Walkman ` phones are around his neck . He 's got a six - pack . He looks at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE, JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's dark .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CRANDALL PORCH, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He sits down .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You done it, you stupid old man. now you got to undo it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He puts his earphones on . Cracks a beer . Lights a cigarette . Pushes the PLAY button on the deck . Faint SOUNDS of The Clash buzz - sawing `` Rock The Casbah . '' JUD begins to watch .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He climbs out of the grave and opens his duffle bag . He starts to pull out the pick . SOUND of an approaching car . LOUIS freezes .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD OUTSIDE OF THE CEMETERY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A police car comes cruising slowly along . The spotlight on the driver 's side comes on and runs along the graveyard 's stone wall .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Watching . Waiting . Hardly breathing .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE POLICE CAR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It reaches the end of the wall . Everything looks jake . The spotlight goes out and the police car speeds up .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He relaxes perceptibly . He gets the pick and drops back into the grave .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE TOP OF THE COFFIN, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS inserts the tip of the pick in the flange of the coffin and levers it . CRACKING SOUND . Again . More CRACKING . Again . And the lock breaks . The coffin lid comes up a little , dirt gritting in the hinges .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Here 's a man on the thinnest edge between sanity and madness .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JETLINER LIFTING OFF FROM O'HARE</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL AND HER SEATMATE</stage_direction>
    <character>SEATMATE</character>
    <dialogue>Think you'll make your connection in Boston?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>I have to.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY GAGE'S GRAVE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's lying on his stomach , reaching in . We hear the SOUND of dirt grating in hinges again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We 're looking up into his face . If GAGE had a POV , this would be it . LOUIS 'S face fills with a terrible grief .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, Gage - oh, honey.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD CRANDALL, ON HIS PORCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>His chin slips to his chest , even though we hear Creedence on his ` phones and to him the sound must be at blastoff levels . There 's a long round ash on his cigarette in the tray . A couple of empty beer cans on the table beside him . A truck blasts by , startling him out of his doze . He jerks his head up suddenly . and slaps himself . He 's okay . for now .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GRAVEYARD, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He is sitting on the edge of the grave , holding his dead son in his arms , rocking him . GAGE is back to us . We see only a small limp figure in a dark suit . Hair flops limply .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It's going to be all right. I swear it's going to be all right.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The canvas tarp has been spread open to the right . LOUIS begins to lay his son down on it .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GROUND BESIDE THE TARP, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's littered with flower petals . One limp hand appears among them .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He closes the tarp over GAGE , making a roll . He then produces rope from the duffle bag . He cuts the rope and begins to tie one piece around one end of the canvas roll containing the corpse of his son .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JETLINER IN THE NIGHT SKY</stage_direction>
    <character>PILOT</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Good evening again, ladies and gentlemen.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE JETLINER, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Her seatmate is knitting something . Across the aisle sits VICTOR PASCOW , bloody but serene , hands clasped in his lap , looking straight ahead . RACHEL looks around tensely .</scene_description>
    <character>PILOT</character>
    <parenthetical>( continues . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm delighted to tell you that we've got a strong tail - wind tonight and we expect to arrive at Boston's Logan Airport almost on time.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW clenches his fist in a `` That 's one for our side ! '' gesture .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( softly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thank God.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Her SEATMATE looks at her a bit strangely .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GRAVEYARD, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's got the bundle containing his son and the duffle - bag with the tools . He runs bent over . He reaches the wall and there 's the SOUND of another motor . He crouches at the base of the wall .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Here comes that same police car . The spotlight runs along the wall .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Crouching against his side of the wall and sweating .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE POLICE CAR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It stops . The COP gets out . He walks slowly toward the wall .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Crouched . Now we see the COP looking over the top . If he looks down . but he does n't . Instead he turns around so we see his back . LOUIS looks up , miserably scared , pouring sweat . Silence . Then : SOUND of the cop taking a whiz .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE COP</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ah ! Relief . SOUND of his fly being zipped . He looks back at the cemetery for a moment .</scene_description>
    <character>COP</character>
    <dialogue>I ai n't afraid of no ghost.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He walks back to his cruiser , gets in , and hauls ass .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BEHIND THE WALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He collapses with relief . Then he gets up and looks cautiously over the wall . Nothing there but his car , parked a little way down on the other side of the road .     <stage_direction>INT./EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE, WITH THE STATION WAGON, JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BEDROOM, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He turns slowly and walks toward the bed .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Gage? Come on out.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He reaches in his pocket and brings out a pocket - knife . He unfolds the blade .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I want to show you something.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Miaow !</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE DOORWAY, WITH CHURCH, JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD, BY THE BED</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( to the cat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How did you -?!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A small hand holding a scalpel shoots out from beneath the skirt of the coverlet and slashes JUD 'S calf ,</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He screams with pain and staggers backward .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The other hand shoots out . GAGE grabs one of JUD 'S ankles and pulls .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>With a startled yell , he falls .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD AND GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>This one 's got ta be pretty rough . George will know what to do . We finally see GAGE , but it should be clear to us that it 's not really GAGE at all . Some daemonic presence is riding inside the mouldering , disfigured shell of GAGE . There is a struggle . JUD is repeatedly slashed with the scalpel . Perhaps he gets GAGE a time or two with the pocketknife . GAGE screams and gibbers - nothing intelligible here ; only sounds . JUD expires . GAGE sits on top of him . and then bites into his throat .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ROUTE 9, BETWEEN THE CRANDALL AND CREED HOUSES</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Headlights . RACHEL 'S truck has arrived . It pulls up . RACHEL opens the passenger door , which is on JUD 'S side .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ANGLE ON THE CAB</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We can see PASCOW sitting in the passenger seat where RACHEL just was .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you so much.</dialogue>
    <character>TRUCKER</character>
    <dialogue>I did n't get a ticket, so you're welcome, lady.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( And , more seriously . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Whatever your problems are, I hope they work out.</dialogue>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>It's the end of the line for me, too - I'm not allowed any further.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to the trucker . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm sure things will be fine.</dialogue>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>I'm not.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She closes the door and steps down . The truck starts off with a HISS OF RELEASED AIRBRAKES . As it pulls past her , RACHEL starts across the road , when :</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( soft voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She stops , startled . Her face wears a `` did I hear that ? '' expression . She looks back toward JUD 'S house .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( soft voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL walks halfway up JUD 'S paved walk and looks at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD'S HOUSE, RACHEL'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The one place in the whole world we do not want RACHEL to go .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She goes . Up the steps to the porch . All through this she 's been travelling with two bags : her handbag and a light tote with her initials on it . Now she sets the tote down on the top step and opens the porch door . She looks very uncertain . This is the wee hours of the morning , and someone else 's house . But . that voice .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy, I need you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL looks stunned - rocked . She steps onto the porch .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Who -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The door to the house swings open . After a moment CHURCH comes into the doorway and sits down .</scene_description>
    <character>CHURCH</character>
    <dialogue>Miaow!</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Church!</dialogue>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy, I need you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She crosses to the open door .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Gage? Gage?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>No answer . RACHEL steps in .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  MORNING</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED BEDROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's restless , having a very bad dream , from the look . He rolls back and forth . Closer and closer to the edge . Finally , with a wild yell , he goes over onto the floor .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, ON THE FLOOR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He comes awake . Sits up . Ouch ! He 's aches from top to bottom and side to side . but his back is worst . His hands go to it .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Jesus!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts to get up very slowly , and this his eyes fix on :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  GAGE'S TRACKS ON THE BEDROOM FLOOR, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They enter the house , go to the closet , then leave again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Gage -?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He scrambles for the closet , his aches and pains forgotten . He stares in wildly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE DOCTOR-BAG</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's open .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He pulls the doctor - bag out . His original hope is now tempered with the first signs of fear . He begins to go through the doctor - bag . Suddenly he brings out a case and opens it . The case is empty , but the indented shape is clear . There was a scalpel in this case . but not anymore .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Oh my God.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gage!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE HALL, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Gage!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS stands there , tensely listening , for a moment or two , but there 's only silence . He rushes down the hallway and opens the door to GAGE 'S room .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  GAGE'S ROOM, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Empty .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, ON THE STAIRS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He goes downstairs , yelling GAGE 'S name .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Nothing . The phone RINGS . LOUIS almost jumps out of his skin reaching for it .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Hello!</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hello, Louis - it's Irwin. I just wanted to be sure Rachel got back all right.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As IRWIN says this , LOUIS 'S eyes fix upon something .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE FLOOR, WITH TWO SETS OF GAGE-TRACKS, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One set comes in from the shed - garage and heads for the parlor and upstairs . The other comes out of the parlor and crosses to the kitchen door giving directly on the outside .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In his eyes we suddenly see that he understands everything . or almost everything .</scene_description>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Louis. are you there?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( slowly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes - I'm here.</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Did she get there all right?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, she's fine.</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Well, put her on at that end and I'll put Ellie on at this one. Ellie's very worried about her mother.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She's almost in hysterics.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>She. Rachel's asleep.</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( an edge in his voice now . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Then I suggest you wake her up. Ellie. I think she had a dream that her mother was dead.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I'll call you right back.</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Louis -!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But LOUIS , whose last few responses have been almost trancelike , hangs up . He looks at the tracks , then goes into the parlor .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CRANDALL LIVING ROOM, WITH THE PHONE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Tiny bloody hands lift it off the cradle . A tiny bloody finger dials .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED KITCHEN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The phone starts to ring . After two or three ringy - dingys , LOUIS , looking extremely upset , comes out of the parlor and picks it up .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Irwin, you'll just have to -</dialogue>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm at Jud's, daddy. Will you come over and play with me?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS is dumbfounded . slack - mouthed with terror .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( a bare whisper . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gage?</dialogue>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mommy already came. We played, daddy. First I played with Jud and then mommy came and I played with mommy. We had an awful good time. Now I want to play with you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>GAGE begins to giggle . a really awful sound .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What did you do? What did you -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CLICK ! The GAGE - THING hangs up , still giggling .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED BED, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He puts the doctor - bag down on the bed and roots through it . He comes up with three syringes , still wrapped in paper , and puts them aside . Then he roots around some more and comes up with several ampoules . He holds one up for inspection and we can read the word MORPHINE on it very clearly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BEDROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He carries the syringes and ampoules of morphine over to the window . His hair has gone partially white . He fills all three syringes with morphine -LRB- using two ampoules for each syringe - i.e. , enough to kill a polar bear -RRB- and puts them in the left breast pocket of his shirt . He puts the spare ampoules in the right breast pocket of his shirt . LOUIS is slowly going insane . What remains of his rationality is like a rapidly fraying rope .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What you buy is what you own, and sooner or later what you own comes home to you. Was n't that what you said, Jud? Was n't that pretty much it?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He leaves the room .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE FRONT DOOR OF THE CREED HOUSE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS comes out the door . In one hand he 's got a raw pork chop . In the other he is carrying a pair of Playtex rubber gloves . He walks to the soft shoulder and waits for an Orinco truck to pass . Then he crosses .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CRANDALL WALK, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He walks most of the way to the house , then stops .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH, LOUIS"S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He gets up , humping his back warily .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Hi, Church. Want some grub?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He tosses the pork chop onto the grass .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He hurries down the steps , goes to the chop , sniffs it , and starts to chow up . He looks up at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He is pulling on the rubber gloves .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't mind me. Eat it while you can. Eat all you want.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He starts worrying the chop again . Smack - smack - smack .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ANGLE ON LOUIS AND CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Eat all you can. all you want. that's right. today's Thanksgiving day for cats, but only if they came back from the dead.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He finishes with the gloves , gets one of the loaded syringes out of his breast pocket , holds it up , squirts a drop out of the tip , then moves toward CHURCH . CHURCH looks up . LOUIS stops moving . CHURCH starts eating again , and LOUIS starts moving again as soon as he does . All the time he talks to the cat in that soothing voice . He bends down . and grabs him . CHURCH begins to squall and fight . LOUIS holds onto him . He tries to get the syringe into the cat and CHURCH almost gets away .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>No, you do n't!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The syringe plunges into his haunch .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH AND LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The needle is still dangling out of CHURCH 'S haunch . The cat looks dazed . It tries to walk and falls over on its side . It tries to get up . and then falls over again .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Go on. Lie down. Play dead. Be dead.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He walks to the porch steps and picks up the tote - bag .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE TOTE-BAG, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Any doubt he might have allowed himself the luxury of having is erased by the initials - R.C. , same as the cola .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Twang ! One of the few remaining strands of sanity has now parted . He looks back at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  CHURCH, ON THE PATH, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Dead .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He climbs the steps and goes onto the porch .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. LOUIS, ON THE PORCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He strips off the rubber gloves . He tosses them onto the table beside JUD 'S beer - cans as he goes inside .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE FOYER OF THE CRANDALL HOME, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's dark in here , and spooky .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Rachel?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Jud?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Longer pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gage?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>No answer . He looks down and sees :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  A SHOE, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One of RACHEL 'S shoes . It lies by the foot of the stairs .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He goes over and picks up the shoe . It 's a three - quarter heel , and it 's pretty badly scuffed . RACHEL , after all , did some pretty hard travelling to get here . There 's a spot of blood on it . SOUND : A low giggle . LOUIS looks up :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE STAIRS, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Mighty dark . Mighty shadowy . SOUND : Another giggle .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, AT THE FOOT OF THE STAIRS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Gage?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE STAIRS</stage_direction>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Let's play, daddy! Let's play hide and go seek!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He takes one of the loaded syringes from his pocket .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>All right, Gage. let's.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He begins to climb the stairs .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  UPSTAIRS, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS arrives on the landing . We begin the nerve - wracking business of checking rooms . First , the bathroom . and the shower curtain is of course pulled . LOUIS yanks it back . Nothing . He checks the linen closet . Nothing . Goes back to the hall . Looks down it . He walks slowly along it . He checks one room . It 's a guest room . Shadowy and empty . Down the hall . A closet door . A bag falls off the top shelf , and a bunch of ceramics inside it SHATTER LOUDLY . LOUIS flinches back . Down the hall . Now he 's at JUD 'S room . He goes in .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S ROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He checks the closet . No go . He steps around the bed and sees :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE FLOOR, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A bloodstain .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He gets down on his hands and knees and examines the bloodstain . He sees the skirt on the bedspread . He lifts it . He is nose to nose with JUD , who is dead with his eyes open , an expression of incredible horror on his face . The DOOR SLAMS . LOUIS bolts to his feet as GIGGLES fade down the hall . Slowly , he kneels down and speaks to the skirt of the spread , which has mercifully fallen back into place .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I'm sorry, Jud. I'm so sorry. I'm -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>There 's a SQUEAKING , SQUEALING SOUND . LOUIS turns around . He gets up again . He starts for the door . Then he turns back and speaks to JUD again .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I'm going to set things back in order. I. I know just what to do.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He goes out .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE HALLWAY, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He takes one of the two remaining loaded syringes from his breast pocket .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Gage?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Another SQUEAKING SOUND . And another GIGGLE . LOUIS starts slowly forward . He gets about halfway down the hall - and our nerves are tuned to the breaking point - when there is a SQUEALING CREAK and a GRATING THUMP from overhead .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  CEILING TRAPDOOR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>This happens fast . The trap - which presumably gives on the attic with a set of folding stairs - rises , and RACHEL 'S body plunges down through and then hangs , swinging : she has been bound around the armpits and as become a grotesque parody of MISSY DANDRIDGE . Half her face is gone . Eaten .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He SCREAMS and backs against the wall . Twang ! The last silver thread parts .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE TRAPDOOR, WITH GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He leaps down , crashes on the floor , and then picks himself up . He is waving the scalpel .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( screeching . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Allee - allee - in - free! allee - allee - in - free! Allee - allee - in - free!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS AND GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>I wo n't choreograph all the moves , but GAGE slashes his stunned father up pretty badly with the scalpel . He 's screeching the whole time . LOUIS finally begins to react . He grapples with the little critter , and tries to get the syringe into him . No good . It 's batted out of his hand just before he can do it . It breaks . LOUIS and GAGE fall to the floor . LOUIS gets the other syringe out of his pocket , but it 's also knocked out of his hand . Only consolation is this one is n't broken . It rolls off along the floor . LOUIS finally manages to get it again as the struggle goes on , and plunges it into GAGE 'S neck .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <dialogue>No fair! NO FAIR!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He gets to his feet , clawing for the needle lolling out of his neck . He 's lost all interest in his father . He goes staggering away . He 's slowing down . He goes to his knees . and falls on his face . LOUIS watches this . and then his vacant , half - catatonic gaze goes to :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She swings slowly back and forth .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE BACK YARD OF THE CRANDALL HOUSE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Time has passed . It 's late afternoon . LOUIS comes out with a sheet - wrapped form in his arms . RACHEL , of course . He sets the body down and goes back inside .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's splashing around a can of coal - oil . When he 's got the room wetted down to his satisfaction , he goes to the door , lights a match , and tosses it . Flame runs across the floor . The fire is slow at first , but then it begins to gain rapidly . LOUIS goes out .</scene_description>

    "summary":"The Creed family—Louis, Rachel, and their children Ellie and Gage—move from Chicago to rural Ludlow, Maine, after Louis is offered a job as a physician with the University of Maine. They befriend their elderly neighbor Jud Crandall, who takes them to an isolated pet cemetery (misspelled "sematary") in the forest behind the Creeds' new home. On his first day at work, Louis encounters Victor Pascow, a jogger who has been mortally injured after being hit by a truck. He warns Louis about the pet cemetery before he dies, calling Louis by name despite the fact they have not previously met. That night, Pascow comes to Louis as a ghost and leads him to the Pet Sematary, warning him not to cross the barrier because the ground beyond is "sour". Louis awakens, assuming it was a dream, but notices his feet are covered in dirt. During Thanksgiving while the family is gone, Ellie's cat, Church, is run down on the highway. Realizing that Ellie will be devastated, Jud takes Louis beyond the cemetery and deep into the woods, where they reach an ancient Miꞌkmaq burial ground. Jud instructs Louis to bury the cat and warns him not to tell anyone else about what they have done. The next day a reanimated Church returns to the house, a shell of what he was before; he stinks, moves sluggishly, and is vicious towards Louis. Jud explains that as a boy he himself revived his beloved pet dog in the Miꞌkmaq ground and that although the cat might be different, it will save Ellie the grief of losing her favorite pet. Sometime later, Gage is killed by a truck along the same highway. The family is devastated, and Jud anticipates that Louis is considering burying his son in the Miꞌkmaq ground, although Louis denies it. Jud believes that introducing Louis to the ritual ground aroused the malevolent forces present there, which caused Gage's death. He tells him the story of a local named Bill Baterman who buried his son Timmy in the Miꞌkmaq ground after he was killed in World War II. Timmy returned as a malevolent zombie, terrifying the townsfolk. A group of men including Jud tried destroying Timmy by lighting the Baterman house on fire, only for Bill to perish with his son. Jud insists that the burial ground is evil and Louis must never try to bury his son there. After the funeral, Rachel and Ellie leave for Chicago while Louis remains home. Despite Pascow and Jud's warnings, Louis exhumes his son's body and buries him at the ritual site. In Chicago, Pascow appears to Ellie in a dream and warns her that Louis is about to do something terrible. Rachel is unnerved by her daughter's dream but is only able to reach Jud when she calls, who tells her Louis is not home. She decides to return to Maine, much to Jud's alarm. That night, Gage returns home and steals a scalpel from his father's bag. He taunts Jud before slashing his Achilles tendon and his mouth horizontally through the lips, before biting his throat, killing him. Rachel returns home and is lured into Jud's house by the voice and specter of her dead sister Zelda, only to discover that she is actually seeing Gage, holding a scalpel. In shock and disbelief, Rachel reaches down to hug her son and he kills her. Waking up from his sleep, Louis notices Gage's muddy footprints in the house and discovers that his scalpel is missing. Receiving a phone call from Gage that he has "played" with Jud and Mommy, he fills three syringes with morphine and heads to Jud's house. Encountering Church, he kills the cat with an injection before entering the house. Gage taunts him further and Louis is startled by Rachel's falling corpse hanged from the attic before he is attacked by his son. After a brief battle, Louis kills Gage with the morphine injection. He then lights the house on fire, leaving it to burn as he carries Rachel's body from the fire. Pascow appears and warns Louis not to "make it worse" but grief-stricken Louis believes that because Rachel was not dead as long as Gage was, burying her "will work this time". Pascow cries out in frustration and vanishes as Louis passes through him. That night, Rachel returns to Louis and the couple embrace. Rachel takes a large knife from the counter as Louis screams."

    "summary":"In New York City in 1991, Alyssa "Ally" Craig is waiting with her mother for the subway, when they are mugged by two young men, who shoot her mother after boarding the train. Ten years later, Ally is a student at New York University (NYU), and lives with her father, Neil, a New York Police Department detective. Tyler Hawkins audits classes at NYU and works at the university bookstore. He has a strained relationship with his workaholic businessman father, Charles, because his older brother, Michael, died by suicide years before. Charles ignores his youngest child, Caroline, of whom Tyler is protective. One night, with his roommate, Aidan, Tyler gets involved in somebody else's fight, and is arrested by Neil. Aidan calls Charles to bail Tyler out, but he does not stick around to have a conversation with his father. Aidan sees Neil dropping Ally off, realizing that she is his daughter. He approaches Tyler with the idea to get back at the detective by persuading him to sleep with and dump Ally. Tyler and Ally go to dinner, kiss at the end of the night, and continue seeing one another. While at Tyler's apartment, Aidan convinces the pair to go to a party, after which Ally is very drunk, and ends up throwing up. She passes out before Tyler can get her to tell him Neil's phone number. The following day, she and her father argue. Neil slaps her, and Ally flees back to Tyler's apartment. Caroline, a budding artist, is featured in an art show, and Tyler asks his father to attend the show. When he fails to show up, Tyler confronts him in a board room filled with people, which causes his father's frustration to boil over. Neil's partner recognizes Tyler with Ally on a train, so Neil breaks into Tyler's apartment, and confronts him. Tyler provokes Neil by confessing to Aidan's plan and his initial reason for meeting Ally, which forces Tyler to confess to Ally. She leaves and returns home. Aidan visits Ally at her father's home to explain that he is to blame, and Tyler is genuinely in love with her. Caroline is bullied by classmates at a birthday party where they cut a chunk of her hair off. Ally and Aidan visit Tyler's mother's apartment, where Caroline is sobbing. Tyler accompanies his sister back to school, and when her classmates tease her for her new haircut, Tyler turns violent, and ends up in jail. Charles is impressed that Tyler stood up for his sister, and they connect. Charles asks Tyler to meet with the lawyers at his office. Tyler spends the night with Ally, and they reveal they love each other after making love. Charles takes Caroline to school. He calls Tyler to let him know this, and explains that he will be late. Tyler is happy that his father is spending time with Caroline. He tells Charles that he will wait in his office. He looks on Charles's computer, featuring a slideshow of pictures with Tyler, Michael, and Caroline when they were younger. After Charles drops Caroline off at school, she sits in her classroom, where the teacher writes the date on the blackboard as September 11, 2001. Tyler looks out the window of his father's office, which is revealed to be located on the 101st floor of the North Tower of the World Trade Center. Once the terrorist attacks begin, the rest of the family, Aidan and Ally, look at the towers before the camera pans over the rubble, showing Tyler's diary. In a voice-over of his diary, Tyler reveals to Michael that he loves him, and he forgives him for killing himself. Tyler is buried next to Michael. Some time later, Caroline and Charles seem to have a healthy father-daughter relationship. Aidan, who has since gotten a tattoo of Tyler's name on his arm, is working hard in school, and Ally gets on the subway at the same spot where her mother was killed."

    "summary":"The family of Harlan Thrombey, a wealthy mystery novelist, attends his 85th birthday party at his Massachusetts mansion. The next morning, Harlan's housekeeper, Fran, finds him dead with his throat slit. The police believe Harlan's death to be suicide, but private detective Benoit Blanc is anonymously paid to investigate. Blanc learns Harlan's relationships with his various family members were strained: on the day of his death, Harlan threatened to expose his son-in-law Richard for cheating on his daughter Linda, cut off his daughter-in-law Joni's allowance for stealing from him, fired his son Walt from his publishing company, and had an altercation with his grandson Ransom. Unknown to Blanc, Harlan's nurse, Marta Cabrera, accidentally mixed up his medications, making her think she overdosed him with morphine, and was unable to find the antidote, apparently leaving Harlan only minutes to live. Wanting to save Marta's family from scrutiny (her mother being an undocumented immigrant), Harlan gave her instructions to create a false alibi and then slit his own throat. Harlan's elderly mother saw Marta carrying out his instructions, but mistook her for Ransom. Marta cannot lie without vomiting, so she gives true but incomplete answers when questioned.
