  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Crickets . Ree - ree - ree - ree . There 's one light upstairs , one downstairs . Perhaps we see the path , glimmering away into the field ? Either by virtue of it being mown , or by virtue of some gentle optical trick ? Maybe .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE LIVING ROOM  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There 's a light on in the kitchen , but it just casts a dim glow in here . The room has a fireplace and a lovely wooden floor . It 's going to be nice , but now it 's just a big bare box with movers ' cartons stacked all over the place . LOUIS is drinking a can of Pepsi , and he looks pretty damned tired - anyone who 's ever moved house and can remember the first night in the new place will understand . He finishes the last of the Pepsi and surveys the living room . He sits on one of the bigger boxes , takes cigarettes from his pocket , and lights one . He drops the spent match in the empty can , and taps into the can during the scene . SOUND : Feet coming down the stairs . The door on the far side of the room opens and RACHEL comes in , wearing a nightgown .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( crossing to LOUIS . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Kids are asleep, doc.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Great.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He hugs her . She hugs him back warmly - for a moment they are just two good people in all the big darkness of their new house .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>You're not really going over to have a beer with that old guy, are you?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I've got a million questions about the area, and -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>- and you'll end up doing a free consultation on his arthritis or urinary problems and -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Did you see his shirt?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( giggles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sure. Bruce Springsteen.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I really do have a million questions about the area. but the thing I'm really curious about is how come this octogenarian Yankee is decorating the slumped remains of his pecs with the Boss.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She laughs .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE PATH OF THE CRANDALL HOUSE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Pervasive SOUND of the crickets as LOUIS comes rather hesitantly up the crazy - paved path from the road 's edge .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That you, doc?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE SCREENED-IN PORCH OF THE CRANDALL HOUSE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We hear the SQUEAK of a rocker ; we see the dim red fitful glow of JUD 'S Pall Mall . We see by its glow that he is wearing Walkman earphones .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It's me.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE PORCH, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The Walkman is in his lap . He switches it off and puts the headphones casually around his neck , like a kid .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well, come on up and have a beer.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE PORCH, A SLIGHTLY WIDER SHOT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS comes on up . JUD has got a pail of ice beside his chair with some cans of beer in it . He opens one and hands it to LOUIS .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You need a glass?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Not at all.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Good for you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS drinks half the can at a draught .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>God, that's fine.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ai n't it just? The man who invented beer, Louis, that man was having a prime day for himself.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What were you listening to?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Allman Brothers.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>The Eat A Peach album. God, they were good before drugs and bad luck caught up with them. Listen to this, Louis.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He passes the headphones over . LOUIS puts them on . JUD presses the Walkman 's PLAY button . SOUND : Ramblin ' Man blasts us out of our seats . LOUIS winces and rakes the spidery earphones off his head .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I'm sorry. Wait.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns it down .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Try that.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS puts the earphones back on and listens for a few moments . It 's the instrumental break . Gregg and Duane Allman dueling hot Fenders . LOUIS takes the earphones off .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Nice.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I like rock and roll. No. I guess that's too mild. I love it. Since my ears started to die out on me, it's the only music I can really hear. And since my wife died. I dunno, some - times a little rock and roll fills up night. Not always, but sometimes.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>One more time - welcome to Ludlow. Hope your time here will be a happy one.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( great sincerity . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thank you, Mr. Crandall.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He drinks again - they both do . There 's a moment of companionable silence here , broken by the SOUND of a big truck . They look toward :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT/INT.  THE ROAD (THROUGH THE PORCH SCREEN)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One of those big tanker trucks goes rumbling by - now there are little amber running lights on top of it . It 's going fast , too - sweeps by in a blast of air .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE PORCH, WITH LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( wincing . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Jesus!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( lights a cigarette . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That's one mean road, all right - you remember that path your wife commented on?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>The one that goes into the woods - sure.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>That road - and those Orinco trucks - are the two main reasons it's there.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What's at the end of it?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Another day - after you get settled in a bit. Meantime, doc -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Here JUD raises his glass in a toast .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( continues . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Here's to your bones.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS clinks his glass against JUD 'S .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>And yours.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They drink .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ROUTE 9  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS crosses from the CRANDALL side to his own , and the CAMERA FOLLOWS as he walks slowly up the driveway and past the wagon . He pauses for a moment , looking thoughtfully - hopefully - at his new house . Then something - the CRY of an OWL , perhaps - draws his attention the other way . toward the path . He walks to its head and stands looking out at it - it glimmers in a wide cut swath that 's a bit ghostly in the dark . A SHAPE suddenly lurches out of the high grass at him , and LOUIS recoils with a startled , muffled cry .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The cat , sure ; who - or what - else ? We see his big green eyes in the dark as he cries his strange feline hello : Waow !</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND CHURCH, AT THE HEAD OF THE PATH</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Church! God, you scared the life out of me!</dialogue>
    <character>CHURCH</character>
    <dialogue>Waow!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS bends and picks up the cat . As he does , that truck SOUND comes again and he looks toward :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Another Orinco tanker drones by , fast .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( to the cat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I know one thing that will keep you home, good buddy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts toward the house . BLACK . And in that blackness , we see a second title card : THE DEAD SPEAK .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  A KITCHEN BLACKBOARD, CU  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Written on it is : MONDAY 1 . -RRB- CHURCH SPAYED 10 A.M. QUENTIN JOLANDER , D.V.M. And below , in even bigger letters : 2 . -RRB- ELLIE 'S FIRST DAY OF SCHOOL ! THE CAMERA PANS LEFT , showing us the kitchen . There are still a few cardboard cartons around , but the place is getting in shape . We look out the window and see the CREEDS , led by JUD CRANDALL , climbing the path toward the woods . LOUIS has got GAGE in a Gerrypak .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  AT THE TOP OF THE HILL, WITH CREEDS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They are also at the edge of the woods . JUD stops and lets them catch up .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Take a look behind you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They turn around , and their faces express their wonder .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>My God!</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>It's beautiful!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE VIEW</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is indeed beautiful . The CREED house is in the f.g. , Route 9 just behind it -LRB- with one of the ever - present Orinco trucks droning along -RRB- , but behind that is the great sweep of the Penobscot river valley , dozing under a fall sky of clear blue .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  AT THE TOP OF THE HILL, WITH JUD AND THE CREEDS</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You folks ready to go on?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Sure.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>But where are we going, Mr. Crandall?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You'll see soon enough, hon.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They go into the woods , still following the path .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  FOREST  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>These are old woods indeed - huge trunks with dusty sunlight shafting through them . It looks as though man has never made his mark here . THE CAMERA PANS SLOWLY DOWN to them , on the path . Here it is carpeted with pine needles , but it is just as clearly marked . JUD stops . LOUIS looks glad of the rest ; he 's sweating and there are wide dark patches under his arms where the Gerrypak 's straps are .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Who owns the woods up ahead? Paper companies?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Nope. The Micmac Indians. What's up ahead is all that's left of their tribal lands.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( giggling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Micmac, Ricmac, Kickmac, Sickmac.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ayuh, it's a funny word, ai n't it? You tired of totin' that yowwen yet, doc?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Not yet. how much further is it?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Aw, you'll be okay. Less than a mile.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts off again , fresh as a daisy . ELLIE scampers after him . LOUIS rolls his eyes at his wife and RACHEL rolls hers back . Then they press on .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ARCH READING PET SEMATARY</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AND THE CREEDS, ON THE PATH</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( stopping . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>This is the place, honey.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE is of course second . Se tries to read the words on the arch but ca n't . She whips around to look at her mother .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What's it say, mommy?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A strange expression has come over RACHEL 'S face - she does n't like this . Not a bit .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>It says Pet Cemetery, hon. It's misspelled, but. that's what it says.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She runs for the arch . RACHEL starts ; looks more uneasy than ever .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Ellen -!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's almost under the arch . She looks back , questioning .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, LOUIS, JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( a bit lame . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Be careful.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She goes racing into the Pet Sematary .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, LOUIS, JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JUD lights a cigarette with a wooden match , using his thumbnail .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I told you it was a bad road, Louis - it's killed a lot of pets and made a lot of kids unhappy. But at least something good come of it. This place.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( excited voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mom! Dad! Y' oughtta see it!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE, AT THE EDGE OF THE SEMATARY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She surveys the rude markers with puzzled delight , then runs toward the center , pausing to investigate some of the markers as she goes . We clearly see the symmetrical pattern of rings .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, LOUIS, JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They are walking slowly toward that rude archway . LOUIS is extremely interested in all this , but it 's becoming clearer and clearer that RACHEL is troubled . They stop and look in .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>How can you call it a good thing? A graveyard for pets killed in the road! Built and maintained by broken - hearted children!</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well, but Missus Creed! It ai n't quite that way, deah!</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I think it's rather extraordinary.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Extraordinarily morbid, maybe.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She 's growing more and more upset . JUD looks at her curiously .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well. they have to learn about death somehow, now do n't they, Missus Creed? The little ones?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( coldly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Why?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well. well, because -</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mommy! Daddy! Look at me!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE, ON THE DEADFALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She has begun to climb it , and this looks like an extremely dangerous proposition . ELLIE , however , is having the time of her life . A branch breaks under one of her feet and she switches nimbly to the next one up .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GROWNUPS, AT THE ARCH</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( alarmed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No, honey! You do n't want to go climbing on that! Come on down!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He hurries in .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELIIE, ON THE DEADFALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She looks back at JUD .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>It's okay, Mr. Crandall -</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE'S FOOT, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The branch she 's on breaks with a dry CRRRACK . Her foot drops down suddenly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She totters backward , pinwheeling her arms , and JUD catches her as she falls . Not much of a catch because she was n't too far up . LOUIS joins JUD and ELLIE . GAGE jounces along on his back .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Have you got a death - wish, Ellen?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I thought it was safe -</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Best never to go climbing on old blowdowns like this, Ellie - sometimes they bite.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Bite?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ayuh.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, STANDING AT THE ARCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Her discomfort makes one thing very clear - she does n't want to come in .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( calls . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Is she all right, Louis?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, JUD, ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( calls back . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Fine! Come and see!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, STANDING AT THE ARCH</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( calling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I think I'll sit this one out, doc.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, JUD, ELLIE--BY THE DEADFALL</stage_direction>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>I want to look around, daddy - may I?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>For a little while.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD looks toward :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL AT THE ARCH (ELLEN IN F.G.)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL has retreated a bit . She sits on the pine needle carpet of the path , opens her purse , and draws out cigarettes .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JUD looks at LOUIS as if to say `` What 's all this about ? '' LOUIS looks away .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Dad! Daddy! Look! A goldfishie!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She runs from one tombstone to the next , cheerful as maybe only a kid could be in such a place . She looks at BIFFER 'S tombstone ; at SMUCKY 'S .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They are walking slowly toward her . LOUIS is looking at the tombstones .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I can hardly read these.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ayuh - they get older as you go toward the middle.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Points . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Pete LaVasseur's dog is buried there.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( points . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>the Stoppard boys' racing pigeon that Missus Cowley's cat got. and I think that's the cat himself right there, although it's been so many years I ca n't tell for sure.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( calling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Missy Ellen! Come over here just a minute!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLEN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She runs amid the tombstones - they have worked their way near to the center and there are quite a few of them - and joins the adults .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I see you're quite a reader for such a little girl. Can you read that?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He points again , and Ellen goes over for a look - see .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ELLEN, AT THE GRAVE MARKER</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is a small slate marker slanted to one side . ELLEN reads the words laboriously , tracing them with her finger .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLEN</character>
    <dialogue>`` Spot a good fellow we love you boy.''</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>`` Owned by Judson. Judson.'' Gee, I ca n't read the rest.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AND LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Last name's Crandall, little missy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS looks at him sharply as ELLIE rejoins them .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>That's where I buried my dog Spot when he died of old age in 19 and 14. Dug it good and deep. By the time I finished, I had blisters all over my hands and a hell of a crick in my back. Soil's stony up here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE looks awed . LOUIS looks a little awed , too . JUD sweeps a hand around , indicating the whole sematary , but is still looking at ELLEN .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Do you know what this place is, Ellie? Oh, I know you know it's a boneyard, but a bone ai n't nothing and even a whole pile of'em do n't amount to much. Do you know what a graveyard really is?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Well. I guess not.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>It's a place where the dead speak, Missy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He sees her startled , uneasy expression and laughs . He ruffles her hair reassuringly .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No - not right out loud. Their stones speak. or their markers. Even if the marker ai n't nothing but a tin can someone wrote on with a Magic Marker, it speaks. Ai n't that so, Louis?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I think it is so, Ellie.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What if you ca n't read what's written on there anymore?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well, it still says some animal got laid down here after, do n't it?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>And that someone cared enough about that animal to mark the spot.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>To remember.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes. To remember. This ai n't a scary place, Ellie. It's a place of rest and speaking. Can you remember that?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( a little awed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes, sir.</dialogue>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, OUTSIDE THE ARCH</stage_direction>

    <parenthetical>( calls . )</parenthetical>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, ELLIE, JUD</stage_direction>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL AND ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>But RACHEL is not amused . She does n't like any of this .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( soft . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Did he.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>My wife is not crazy about cemeteries of any kind. As you may have noticed.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Me neither. But I believe in knowing your enemy.</dialogue>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ARCH, A NEW ANGLE</stage_direction>

    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Did we take too long?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>

  <scene>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN TRASH CAN  NIGHT</stage_direction>

The table is covered with newspapers . On it , LOUIS is putting together a complicated model boat , using glue and tweezers . He 's wearing glasses . ELLIE comes in , wearing a nightgown . She watches him for awhile .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( not looking around . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hi, babe.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Daddy, that Pet Sematary is there because of the road, is n't it?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS looks around at her , surprised .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>That's what I think. I heard Missy Dandridge tell Mom when Church was fixed he would n't cross the road so much.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well, it's always better to take precautions - but I'm sure Church will be all right, honey.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUST OUTSIDE THE KITCHEN DOOR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL is coming along with some dirty dishes . She hears voices and stops , listening , her face troubled and afraid .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No he wo n't! Not in the end! He wo n't be all right in the end no matter how you fix ` im!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS AND ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Ellis has started to cry .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>In the end he's gon na croak, is n't he?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Lovey. Church might be still alive when you're in a high school. and that's a very long time.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>It does n't seem long to me. It seems short. I think the whole thing about pets dying s - s - sucks!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Poor kid 's bawling her eyes out now . LOUIS folds her into his arms and she hugs him tightly , wanting his comfort .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>If it was up to me I'd let Church live to be a hundred. but I do n't make up the rules.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( muffled . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Well who does? God, I suppose. But he's not God's cat! He's my cat! Let God get His own, if He wants one! Not mine! Not mine! Not -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She breaks down completely , sobbing , and LOUIS rocks her back and forth .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE HALLWAY OUTSIDE THE KITCHEN, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She is crying silently .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  ELLIE'S BEDROOM  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She is a dimly perceived hump in the darkness . An oblong shaft of light falls on her , illuminating her more clearly . She 's asleep with her teddy encircled by one arm and her thumb corked into her mouth .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE DOORWAY, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL looks at her daughter with infinite love and then quietly closes the door .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS'S AND RACHEL'S BEDROOM  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS is in his pajamas , propped up on pillows on his side of the bed . There a number of medical books scattered around him and he 's making notes from one as RACHEL comes in .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>She's finally asleep.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>She was a little over - excited, that's all. Poor kid.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>It was that place. That creepy cemetery up in the woods. Whatever disease the kids in this town have got, I do n't want Ellie to catch it.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Jesus, Rachel, what's got into you?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Do you think I did n't hear her tonight, crying as if her heart would break? Here she is thinking Church is going to die.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>It should be clear to us by now that , despite her words , RACHEL is much more upset than ELLIE was . LOUIS slowly puts his notebook aside and caps his pen .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Rachel. someday Church is going to die.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( whirls on him . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That is hardly the point! Church is not going to die today, or tomorrow - Never mind. I can see you do n't have the slightest idea what I'm talking about.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She stalks to the bathroom , which adjoins . LOUIS follows . She goes in and slams the door . He goes for the knob .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Rachel -!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : CLICK OF THE LOCK . LOUIS stares at the door , bewildered and upset .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ROUTE 9  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Here comes a big Orinco truck , droning along , headlights glaring .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS'S AND RACHEL'S BEDROOM</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The headlights of the truck illuminate the room and we see LOUIS and RACHEL asleep , each as far over to his/her own side as he/she can get , with a big empty space in the middle . Lights and TRUCK SOUNDS slowly fade .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  GAGE  MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Cheerful little clots of scrambled eggs are scattered all the way across the tray of his high - chair - it looks a little like a map of the Pacific islands done by a guy who only had a yellow crayon . Now he scoops up a handful and throws them .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN TABLE, WITH ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Splat ! Eggs on the serving plate of toast .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yee - uck! Gross!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, A WIDER SHOT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL is at the sink , doing dishes -LRB- we see the blackboard with its message near her -RRB- . LOUIS comes in , wearing a sport - coat and slacks , ready for his first day on the job . and ELLIE is in a pretty first day of school dress .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>He ca n't help it, babe. Emily Post is going to be beyond him for a few years.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  BY THE KITCHEN DOOR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Here is the cat - carrier with CHURCH inside it . He waows unhappily .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN TABLE, WITH ELLIE AND GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ELLIE gets down and goes across to the cat - carrier .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't want him to get his nuts cut, daddy! What if he dies?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL AND LOUIS, BY THE SINK</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS looks shocked and amused by ELLIE 'S colorful choice of words .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Good God! Where'd you hear that?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Missy Dandridge. And she says it's a operation!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL AND LOUIS, BY THE SINK</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS tries to kiss RACHEL 'S mouth . She turns her head slightly so he gets her cheek instead . She 's still mad . LOUIS 'S amusement dies .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Honey, Church will be fine.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  ELLIE, BY THE CAT CARRIER</stage_direction>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>But what if he dies and has to go to the Pet Sematary?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS AND RACHEL, BY THE SINK</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She gives him a look as if to say : `` There ! Now do you understand what you did ? ''</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't be silly. Church is not going to die.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>According to what Mr. Crandall says, the road's a lot more dangerous than the operation. Church will be just the same. Well - almost the same - and we wo n't have to worry about him getting turned into catburgers by one of those damn Orinco trucks.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>At this RACHEL tightens up still more in that funny way - she 's actually angered by LOUIS 'S reference to catburgers - but under the anger we sense she is deeply shocked , as a prudish woman might be shocked by a dirty joke . For RACHEL , that 's just what death is .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>That's enough of that kind of talk!</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I just said -</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>I know what you just said. Ellie, clear your place.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE goes slowly back to the table .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( sets the plate down . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm scared. What if school here is n't like in Chicago! I'm scared and I want to go h - h - home!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ELLIE bursts into loud tears and puts her hands over her face .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, A NEW ANGLE (FEATURES LOUIS AND RACHEL)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA FOLLOWS as they go to the table to comfort ELLIE .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>You'll be fine, Ellie. Now you can be excused. Go and wash your face.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>And Church will be fine.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( anxious . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Do you promise, Daddy?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well, honey. you know that.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't shilly - shally, Louis. Give the little girl her promise.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( reluctantly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Church will be fine. I promise.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Yayyyy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She runs off , cheered up . And RACHEL is cheered up , too .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you, Louis.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, you're welcome. Only if some - thing should go wrong while he's under the gas - it's a one - in - a - thousand shot, but it happens - you explain to her.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He gets up and leaves the table . She looks after him , stunned and a little frightened .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  GAGE</stage_direction>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( conversationally . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Here, Durch!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He picks up a large glob of scrambled eggs from his tray and throws it in the direction of the cat - carrier .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CAT-CARRIER</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHURCH is close to the mesh , looking out . Scrambled eggs hit the mesh , driving him back , surprised .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The school bus pulls up , red lights flashing . ELLIE runs toward it across the lawn , with her lunch - box .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, RACHEL, AND GAGE, IN THE FRONT DOORWAY</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Have a great day!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS grabs GAGE 'S hand and makes him wave it .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Bye - bye!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE BUS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ELLIE climbs aboard . The red flashers go out and the bus pulls away .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED DRIVEWAY  MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The station wagon is parked there . LOUIS comes out with a heavy briefcase in one hand and the cat - carrier in the other . He opens the wagon 's doorgate . A small car turns into the CREED driveway and parks beside LOUIS . A rather sour - looking middle - aged woman gets out and crosses the front of her car . Her color is bad . This is MISSY DANDRIDGE . She looks at the cat - carrier .</scene_description>
    <character>MISSY</character>
    <dialogue>Gon na get his -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>- nuts cut, yes. Thank you, Missy, for introducing that colorful phrase into my daughter's vocabulary.</dialogue>
    <character>MISSY</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't mention it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She opens the passenger side door of her car and we see a big neat pile of folded sheets . She reaches for them , then winces and presses her hands against her midriff for a moment , as if with an attack of indigestion .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( sees this . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How's that belly - ache of yours?</dialogue>
    <character>MISSY</character>
    <parenthetical>( gets the sheets . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No better and no worse.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>You ought to see a doctor about it.</dialogue>
    <character>MISSY</character>
    <dialogue>It'll pass. They always do.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She starts toward the house with the sheets .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE SIDE YARD  MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL hurries past MISSY , who turns to look and then goes on into the house . LOUIS has just put the cat - carrier into the back of the wagon and closed the doorgate as RACHEL reaches him .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( anxious . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Still friends, doc?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS appears to consider this seriously for a moment . and then he smiles and hugs her . They kiss .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank God. I was a little worried there. Have a great first day at school, doc. No broken bones.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiles . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Not so much as a sprain.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  VICTOR PASCOW AND FRIENDS  MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PASCOW is in a blanket that is being carried by three boys and one girl . They are all yelling at each other not to joggle him , not to drop him . A small knot of horrified college kids moves with the bearers . PASCOW 'S head is upside down to the CAMERA , which retreats ahead of the advancing students . Fixed eyes stare . Half of his head has been shattered inward . Before the catastrophe he was a husky male of about twenty . He 's dressed in a U of M muscle shirt and red jogging shorts . THE CAMERA PULLS JERKILY TO ONE SIDE , allowing the bearers to mount the steps of a brick building . The infirmary . The lookers - on break to either side . The infirmary doors open .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.. NURSE CHARLTON, AT THE DOORS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's the head nurse , a tough old babe of about fifty .</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLTON</character>
    <dialogue>Holy Jesus.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( turns . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Steve! Steve! Dr. Creed! Dr. Creed, we've got a mess here! Stat!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The bearers sweep past her and inside , leaving a red smear of blood across the midriff of MARCY CHARLTON 'S uniform .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE INFIRMARY RECEPTION AREA</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA will show us all we need to see , but its movements will seem almost random ; this is like being in the hotel kitchen after Sirhan shot Bobby . As the students bring in PASCOW , LOUIS comes running , followed by STEVE MASTERTON , his P.A. Standing to one side are two student nurses in candystriper uniforms . They 're boggled and horrified . LOUIS kneels . THE CAMERA RUSHES FORWARD , shoving between onlookers . LOUIS looks at the wound . There 's shattered bone and pulsing brain tissue beneath . There 's a scream ; the girl who was carrying one corner of the blanket is having hysterics .</scene_description>
    <character>GIRL</character>
    <dialogue>Vic! Vic! Oh Christ! Vic!</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( to CHARLTON . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Get her out. Get them all out.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CHARLTON puts her arms around the girl .</scene_description>
    <character>GIRL</character>
    <parenthetical>( struggling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No! No! He ca n't die! He ca n't die!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA MOVES BACK DOWN as LOUIS takes an opthalmascope from STEVE and shines it in PASCOW 'S bulging , fixed eyes . CHARLTON is just pushing the last of them gawkers and bearers out the door .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Steve, get the ambulance over here right now. He's got to go to EMMC.</dialogue>
    <character>STEVE</character>
    <dialogue>The ambulance is at Sonny's Sunoco downtown, getting -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>- a new muffler, oh shit -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW makes a weird gargling noise . Blood suddenly spurts out of his mouth . He begins to seizure . One of the candystripers shrieks . THE CAMERA JERKS UP TO COVER the student nurses . One turns and throws up on the wall . CHARLTON rushes over .</scene_description>
    <character>CANDYSTRIPER</character>
    <dialogue>I ca n't look at it. I ca n't stand it.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLTON</character>
    <parenthetical>( slaps her . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes you by God can. Go get the hard stretcher!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As they start away , one helping the other down the hall , and as CHARLTON starts over to where PASCOW lies dying on his blanket , THE CAMERA DROPS TO LOUIS AND STEVE .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Help me hold him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They hold PASCOW 'S spasming body .</scene_description>
    <character>STEVE</character>
    <dialogue>It would n't matter if we did have the ambulance.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It would n't matter if we had the SST.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW begins to quiet .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>He's going. Steve, go call the motor - pool. Marcy, roll out the crash wagon.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLTON</character>
    <dialogue>It wo n't -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I know it wo n't! But let's for God's sake do it by the rules!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She leaves . LOUIS is alone with PASCOW . CHARLTON has drawn the drapes , so the doctor and the dying man have complete if temporary privacy .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS AND PASCOW, A CLOSER SHOT</stage_direction>
    <character>LOIS</character>
    <dialogue>There was n't even supposed to be a sprain today, my friend - that's what I told her.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW 'S fixed eyes suddenly roll and his left hand bear - traps LOUIS 'S right wrist . The dying man pulls him slowly but relentlessly down , until their faces are only inches apart .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>Pet Sematary.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS recoils , breaking the grip of the hand . but he can not quite snap the grip of those bright dying eyes . Blood leaks from PASCOW 'S mouth .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( whispers . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>W - What did you say?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW struggles hard to speak again . At first he can only gurgle .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>It's not the real cemetery.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Long pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>The soil of a man's heart is stonier, Louis. a man grows what he can. and tends it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS leans forward again , terrified , yet needing to know .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>How do you know my name?</dialogue>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <parenthetical>( gurgling . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'll come. to you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS grabs PASCOW 'S bloody shoulder .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( low but urgent . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Dammit, how do you know my name?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  HALLWAY ENTRANCE TO RECEPTION, WITH STEVE</stage_direction>
    <character>STEVE</character>
    <dialogue>Louis, they're sending a -</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS AND PASCOW</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PASCOW begins to spasm again .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( snaps . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Help me!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW spews more blood as STEVE kneels beside LOUIS .</scene_description>
  </scene>
