  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One of the branches snaps . LOUIS 'S foot plunges . His cuff rips .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We 're looking up at a fairly steep angle as LOUIS staggers off - balance . He steps with his other foot , misses , and goes flying .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, CLOSER</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He does a half - somersault in the air and hits the deadfall on his back , the green garbage bag flying out of his hand . His flashlight also goes . Branches crack . White dust puffs out from under him .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD, AT THE BASE OF THE DEADFALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS thumps to the ground nearby . JUD kneels beside him .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Louis! You all right?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS sits up groggily . His pants are torn . His sweatshirt is torn . His ankle is bleeding .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( dazed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sure. I guess I just lost my happy thoughts for a second there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS gets slowly up and retrieves the bag , which is rather shredded now - and we can see catfur through some of the rents .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( continues . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I should n't have stopped. and it does bite.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He whaps the flashlight against his palm a time or two and the light comes on . Satisfied , he shuts it off .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No, you should n't have stopped. But you got away with it. Important thing is are you sure you're all right?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Where are we going, Jud?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You'll see before long. Let's go.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts off up the path . After a moment LOUIS follows , carrying the bag .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD, FROM THE DEADFALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Again , there should be a sense of awe and mystery as they go tolling up the path into the twilight , dwarfed by those ancient firs . SOUND OF CRICKETS , LOW at first , then UP TO LOUD : Ree - ree - ree .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD, AT THE EDGE OF LITTLE GOD SWAMP  TWILIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Lots of undergrowth here , and creeping ground - mist , too . The SOUND OF CRICKETS is now only a part of the soundtrack : BUZZ OF CICADAS , THUMP OF FROGS . Swamp - sounds . LOUIS looks frankly doubtful .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>This next bit's like the deadfall, Louis - you got to walk steady and easy. Just follow me and do n't look down.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LITTLE GOD SWAMP, LOUIS'S AND JUD'S POV  DEEP TWILIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Mysterious . awesome . scary . Dead trees poke out of the murk like twisted hands . There 's scummy water standing around tussocks covered with long grass , most of it dead . There 's a lot of choking underbrush . All of this fades away into a grim , obscuring fog .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Micmacs used to call it Little God Swamp.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Is there quicksand?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ayuh.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( nervous ; joking . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Are there ghosts?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD looks at him expressionlessly .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ayuh.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD starts off , stepping to the first tussock . After a moment , LOUIS follows .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>His face is set , strange .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>There's a lot of funny things down this way, Louis.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BEHIND JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>You're telling me.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( still walking . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>The air's heavier. more electrical. something. You might see St. Elmo's Fire. what the sailors call ` foo - lights.' It makes funny shapes, but it's nothing.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HE looks up and his eyes widen as he sees :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ANGLE ON LITTLE GOD SWAMP, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A faintly glowing , ethereal shape hangs in the branches of one of the dead trees . It looks a bit like a corpse . In fact , I think it looks quite a bit like PASCOW 'S corpse . As we watch it fades . fades . is gone .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's somewhere between being mystified and puzzled and being scared . Now a weakly glowing fireball rolls slowly across the surface of the standing water toward him . and then just fades into the thick mist .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It's funny, all right.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Just do n't stop, Louis. You do n't ever want to stop down here in Little God.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>And you do n't ever want to look behind you, whatever you hear.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AND LOUIS, LONG ANGLE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We see them moving through the mist like wraiths , JUD with his digging tools , LOUIS with his light and his Hefty - Bag coffin . The whole swamp is glowing dimly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE FAR SIDE OF LITTLE GOD SWAMP  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In the extreme f.g. we can see firm ground sloping up . Ahead is a thick white mist . And here comes JUD and LOUIS slogging through it and out of it . Both of them are wet from the knees down . They head into the woods on the far side .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  A LOW, STONY BLUFF OR STEEP HILL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In the book this is described as being almost a cliff , but a rocky hill rising out of the woods would serve just as well . We can see steps cut into the side , and two figures - LOUIS and JUD - toiling up them .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AND LOUIS, A CLOSER SHOT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JUD 'S panting and out of breath ; LOUIS is , if anything , in worse shape .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Almost there, Louis.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>You keep saying that.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>This time I mean it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He tops the last step and stands on a rocky level under the stars , the wind blowing his hair off his deeply lined brow . A few moments later LOUIS joins him and stares with undisguised wonder .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE MICMAC BURYING GROUND, LOUIS AND JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The top of this hill or bluff is rocky and bare , but there are a number of rocky piles . But for every pile of rocks we can see , there are ten littered heaps , as if the neat piles had been burst apart . There 's a shape to all of this , and it is the shape of the Pet Sematary : concentric circles . SOUND : The wind , blowing ceaselessly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD, AT THE EDGE OF THE BURYING GROUND</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( awed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What is this place?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>This was their burying ground, Louis.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Whose burying ground?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>The Micmac Indians. I brought you here to bury Ellen's cat.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Why? For God's sake, why?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I had my reasons, Louis. We'll talk later. All right?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I guess so. but.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You want to rest a bit before you start?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>No, I'm okay. Will I really be able to dig him a grave? The soil looks thin.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Soil's thin, all right. But you'll manage.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He hands him the pick and shovel .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I'm going to sit over yonder and have a smoke. I'd help you, but you've got to do it yourself. Each buries his own. That's how it was done then.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD walks away , leaving LOUIS with the digging tools in one hand and the flashlight in the other . After a minute , LOUIS walks out into the burying ground .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOOKING DOWN INTO A SHALLOW HOLE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND : The wind . It blows ceaselessly up here . The hole 's about two and a half feet deep . Stubby rocks protrude from the sides . The pick comes down , hits a rock at the bottom , and flashes fire .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He drops the pick and sticks his hurt hands in his armpits . Beside him we see a low pile of rocks and earth .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Should be deep enough.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He joins LOUIS . He 's got a lot of rocks in his arms .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>You think so?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He notices the rocks .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What are those for?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Your cairn.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE MICMAC BURYING GROUND, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Those tumbled piles of rock are very obvious .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND JUD, BY CHURCH'S GRAVE</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Does n't look like they last long.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't worry about that.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Jud, why am I doing all this?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Because it's right.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He walks off again . LOUIS looks after him for a moment , then kneels down .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY THE GARBAGE BAG</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He opens it and looks in at CHURCH 'S stiffening corpse .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Pax vobiscum, Church old buddy. You were a hell of a god cat. I doubt if you were worth all this aggravation, but you were a hell of a good cat.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He tumbles the bag containing the body into the grave , and then begins pushing the stony soil over it with the spade .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CAIRN, CU  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS 'S hands come into the frame and add a final two or three stones .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, BY THE CAIRN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He looks at it for a moment and stands up . JUD is right there .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>That's fine. You did real good.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS looks at him .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There 's a light on in the kitchen , but that 's all . There 's silence at first , and then the PHONE STARTS RINGING .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS'S FIELD  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS and JUD are coming down the path with their tools and their lights . They are both clearly fagged out . SOUND , FAINT : The telephone .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, shit! Rachel!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He drops the tools and sprints .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED'S SIDE YARD, BY THE TIRE SWING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS runs into the side yard . SOUND of the phone is louder .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE KITCHEN DOOR OF THE CREED HOUSE, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He runs to the door and inside .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE END OF THE PATH, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He stands there , eyes inscrutable .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE LIVING ROOM, WITH THE PHONE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It stops . A beat later LOUIS enters the room . He picks it up , although he already knows it 's too late . He listens to the SOUND of the dial tone and then drops it back into the cradle , disgusted . He starts to dial a number from memory .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Louis.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN/LIVING ROOM DOORWAY, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>When you talk to'em, not one word about what we done tonight.'S ` far's you know, the cat's still fine.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, BY THE PHONE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>After a moment he lowers it into the cradle .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>You'll understand. In the meantime, keep your peace. What we did, Louis, was a secret thing. Women are supposed to be the ones who are good at keeping secrets, but any woman who knows anything at all would tell you she's never seen into a man's heart. The soil of a man's heart is stonier, Louis - like the soil up there in the old Micmac burying ground. A man grows what he can. and tends it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>During this , he 's come across the room to LOUIS and dropped his hand on LOUIS 'S shoulder .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>But -</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>No buts! Accept what's done, Louis. What we done was right. Another time it might not be, but tonight it was. at least I hope to Christ it was. Now you make your call. but not a word about tonight.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUNDS : Boops and beeps of a touch - tone telephone . Ringing . Then :</scene_description>
    <character>DORY GOLDMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Goldman residence.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Hi, Dory. it's Louis -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>During this , another SOUND has been growing : an approaching truck . As JUD gains his side of the road , he looks back , and we read fear on his face - no matter what he said to LOUIS , he 's sorry for tonight 's piece of work . A moment later a highballing Orinco truck cuts between THE CAMERA and JUD .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, IN THE LIVING ROOM  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's on the phone , smiling and happy .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You want to talk to the birthday girl?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>That'd be real fine.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hi. daddy?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( sings . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Happy birthday to you/Happy birthday to you/Happy birthday, dear Ellie/Happy birthday to you!</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That was awful, daddy.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah, I know. how are things out there in Chicagoland?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Fine. except when Mom was airing Gage's diaper rash, he walked away and got into Grampa's study and pooped in Grampa's favorite chair.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( grinning broadly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Way to go, Gage!</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I said that's too bad. What did you get for presents from Gramma and Grampa?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Lots of stuff! I got two dresses. and a Chatty Cathy doll.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN LIVING ROOM, WITH ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's dressed for bed , in fuzzy pink pajamas . Her Chatty Cathy is crooked in one arm . In her lap is a Garfield transistor radio .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>and a Garfield radio! How's Church, dad? Does he miss me?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED LIVING ROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The smile fades off his face . It 's replaced with a look of combined guilt and unhappiness . He 's looking at his hands , which are still dark with the dirt from CHURCH 'S grave .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well. I guess he's just fine, Ellie. I have n't seen him this evening, but -</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GOLDMAN LIVING ROOM, WITH ELLIE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL , holding GAGE , sits on the arm of ELLIE 'S chair .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Well, make sure you put him down cellar before you go to bed so he ca n't run out in the road and get greased. And kiss him goodnight for me.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yuck! Kiss your own cat!</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Want to talk to Gage?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Before he can answer , she puts the phone in GAGE 'S hand . ELLIE and RACHEL watch , amused , as GAGE gobbles into it . Perhaps RACHEL encourages him to say a few words .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED LVING ROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>From the telephone comes the sound of GAGE talking and chortling . LOUIS is not listening . His eyes - and his mind - are far away .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS is raking leaves on the side lawn , near the tree with the tire swing . After a moment or two of this he props the rake against the tree and starts toward the garage . He goes in .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE GARAGE, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's dim in here . LOUIS is crossing to the door which communicates to the kitchen . As he passes the station wagon , he hears a cat HISS . He turns .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  CHURCH, ECU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's on top of the car , but at this point we probably do n't notice ; THE CAMERA is so close that CHURCH looks like he 's coming right down our throats . He 's hissing angrily .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He recoils and stumbles backward with a cry . He hits a tool - rack on the wall and a lot of them fall down with a LOUD JANGLING NOISE .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  ON TOP OF THE STATION WAGON, WITH CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He jumps down , frightened by the noise , and the CAMERA TRACKS as he goes flying out the garage door into the sunlight .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He gets slowly to his feet again . He 's getting over his fright but we can see he 's totally freaked out by what gave him that fright . He goes to the garage door and looks out .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( calls . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Church?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE SIDE YARD, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Grass and fallen leaves . No sign of CHURCH .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS'S STUNNED FACE, CU</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's spooning cat - food into a dish . He goes to the door - there should be a total of three doors in the kitchen : one to the living room , one to the shed/garage , and one which leads directly outside . LOUIS uses this latter door now .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE KITCHEN STOOP, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He puts the dish of food down and sits beside it .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Food, Church. food!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Miaow .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE SIDE OF THE HOUSE, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHURCH comes slinking out of the bushes and comes slowly toward THE CAMERA . He stops , looking mistrustful .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Come on, Church! Chow down!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He crosses to the stoop and begins eating the food .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( to himself . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Christ. I do n't believe this.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He picks CHURCH up . CHURCH miaows again - he wants the food .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( wincing . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>God, you stink, Church.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CHURCH is looking at the food , trying to get out of LOUIS 'S arms .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>In a second.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He tilts the cat 's head back so he can get a look at CHURCH 'S neck .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  CHURCH'S NECK, CU (LOUIS'S POV)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There 's some sort of mark here - a clear remnant of the crash . A line of white fur , or perhaps a dark red scar where no fur at all grows .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND CHURCH, ON THE STOOP</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS sees something else as he lets the cat 's neck go . He tweezes something out of CHURCH 'S whiskers .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS'S HAND, ECU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's a shred of green plastic .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Chewed his way out. Jesus Baldheaded Christ, he ch -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CHURCH suddenly claws at his face .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Ow!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He claps his hand to his face . CHURCH leaps for the food . LOUIS slowly takes his hand away . There are claw marks on his cheek , welling blood . He looks at the cat .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD CRANDALL'S GARDEN, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The garden is a plot of about half an acre . JUD comes trundling slowly along a row , pushing a wheelbarrow . There are several pumpkins in it . JUD is wearing old khaki gardening pants and a Ramones sweatshirt . He 's wearing his headphones and we can hear the Romantics doing `` What I Like About You . '' JUD is singing along and bopping a little - as much as his arthritis will allow , if you can dig it . He sees a real big pumpkin , stops , and bends over to get it . He takes out his pocket - knife and slits the pumpkin - vine . He gets the pumpkin in his arms and stands up . He turns . and LOUIS is right there -LRB- kind of a cheap jump , but always fun -RRB- , looking totally stunned . JUD , startled , drops the pumpkin . LOUIS reaches out and slides the phones off JUD 'S ears .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What did we do?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CRANDALL KITCHEN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS is sitting at the kitchen table . JUD is at the fridge . JUD comes back with a couple of long - necked bottles of beer and opens them .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I most generally do n't start before noon, but this looks like an exception.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What did we do, Jud?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Why, saved a little girl from being unhappy. that's all. Drink up, Louis!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS drinks about half the beer .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I tried to tell myself I buried him alive. You know - Edgar Allan Poe meets Felix the Cat. But.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Would n't wash?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>No. I'm a doctor. I know death when I see it, and Church was dead. He smells horrible and he uses his claws, but he's alive. and I feel like I'm going crazy. It was that place, was n't it?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ayuh. It was the rag - man told me about the place - Stanley Bouchard. Us kids just called him Stanny B. He was half Micmac himself.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS drains his beer .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Can I have another one?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I guess it would n't hurt.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He gets up and goes to the fridge .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD, AT THE FRIDGE</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>The Micmacs used to bury their dead up there long before the whites came.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He returns to the table with the beer .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>They buried their dead and for a long time their dead stayed buried. Then something happened. Half the tribe died in a season. The rest moved on. They said a Wendigo had soured the ground.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Wendigo?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Spirit of the north country. Not a good spirit. Wendigos are great liars and tricksters, according to the stories. And if one touches you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD pauses , perhaps a flustered , and gathers his thoughts .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Maybe it really was a Wendigo - I ai n't the one to say it was n't - or maybe it was just some disease. Whatever the reason, those that were left moved on. But they left that place. the way it is now.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD shrugs , and drinks .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AS A BOY, CU/SEPIA TONE  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The time here is about 1910 . JUD is wearing short pants . He 's crying , not in any big - deal histrionic way , but as if he means to keep doing it for a long time . I mean he looks really sad .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I loved my dog a lot, Louis. When Spot died, I thought I was gon na die.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD is sitting on the front stoop . It 's the same house JUD lives in now , but the porch has n't been added yet , and the road is dirt rather than tar . Along this road comes a horse - drawn wagon - STANNY B. 'S wagon . The wagon 's full of junk , rags , bottles . stuff to sell and swap . Strung across the top are bells , and we can hear their CHIMING SOUND . but faint , like bells heard in a dream . STANNY B. is old and drunk . Dust spumes up behind the wagon as he draws up to the CRANDALL house and stops . He gets down , almost falls , takes a bottle out of his back pocket , drinks , and approaches JUD . We can see him speaking .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S KITCHEN, WITH JUD AND LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>You and this old Indian rag - man -</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Stanny B. did for me what I did for you last night, Louis. Only I was n't alone when Spot came back.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CRANDALL BACK YARD/SEPIA TONE  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>JUD 'S MOTHER is back to THE CAMERA , hanging sheets on the line . The sheets billow . And suddenly , pushing out from behind them , quite near her , is a small mongrel dog . SPOT . He 's covered with graveyard dirt . His eyes are red and rolling . He splashes the sheets with the muck of his passage .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My mother was with me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She sees who it is - what it is - and backs away , screaming , horrified .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  SPOT, CLOSER/SEPIA</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>He'd got caught in bobwire that infected. You could still see the marks on him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>And so we can , around his neck and along the side of his head . These marks are the counterpart of the marks we 've already seen on CHURCH . SOUND of JUD 'S MOM SCREAMING . Like the bells , these are screams heard in a dream .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE BACK STOOP OF THE CRANDALL HOUSE/SEPIA</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The BOY JUD comes running out , dressed in a night - shirt .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD'S MOM/SEPIA (JUD'S POV)</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's cringing against the fence at the rear of the yard . SPOT stands in front of her , swaying from side to side , as if doped .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD'S MOM</character>
    <parenthetical>( dim ; far . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Get your dog, Jud! He stinks of the ground you buried him in! Come here and get your dog!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She is in utter terror .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE BOY JUD/SEPIA</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Horrified . ashamed .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD'S MOM/SEPIA</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD'S MOM</character>
    <parenthetical>( terror . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>COME AND GET YOUR DOG!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD AND LOUIS, IN JUD'S KITCHEN</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>How did your mother take it, Jud? How did she take it when your dog came back from the dead?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD 'S face is a complication . He 's lying to LOUIS , certainly - but is he also lying to himself ? Yes , I think so .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Well, she was a little upset at first, and that's why I thought you ought to hold your peace when you talked to your people last night. you did, did n't you, Louis?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Why, then, things should be fine.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>A little upset is all she was? Because I'll tell you, Jud, my brains feel a little like a nuclear reactor on the edge of a meltdown.</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>She got used to the idea. Spot lived another four years. He died peacefully in the night that second time, and I buried him in the Pet Sematary. where his bones still lie.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ROAD BETWEEN THE TWO HOUSES, WITH LOUIS AND JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We see them crossing .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You still have n't told me why you did it.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD AND LOUIS, ON THE CREED FRONT LAWN</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>A man does n't always know why he does things, Louis. I think I did it because your daughter ai n't ready for her favorite pet to die.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Ellie's a little scared of death. And the main reason Ellie's that way is because your wife is a lot scared of death. Now you just go ahead and tell me I'm wrong.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But LOUIS 'S reaction tells him he 's not wrong - in fact , JUD has hit the nail right on the head .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  BATHTUB FIXTURES, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS 'S hands come into the frame and turn the spigots .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He starts to undress , still looking troubled . We should notice that the door behind him is firmly shut . The bathroom has no windows .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHTUB SPIGOTS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The hot water is steaming . LOUIS 'S hands enter the frame and turn off the faucets . SOUND of LOUIS climbing in .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS IN THE TUB</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A big sigh and an expression of exquisite pleasure . He relaxes in the hot water . After a few moments he puts a wet washcloth over his face .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  BY THE KITCHEN SINK, WITH RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Do n't shilly - shally, Louis. Give the little girl her promise.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN TABLE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>GAGE is in his high chair . ELLIE is at her place , crying . In RACHEL 'S place sits VICTOR PASCOW , bloody and wrecked . LOUIS sits in his place . On the platter of bacon and scrambled eggs is CHURCH 'S mangled body .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>The door must not be opened. The barrier must not be crossed.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>You do n't understand -</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHTUB, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The washrag is slipping , but it still covers his face .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( mutters . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>- I'm a doctor.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED KITCHEN TABLE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In attendance : PASCOW , LOUIS , ELLIE , GAGE in his high chair . Lying in the middle of the table , clotted with dirt and blood , eyes staring , neck a gory mess of infected wounds , is SPOT . He 's also dotted with clots of scrambled egg and bits of bacon .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>Sometimes the dead do more than speak. Remember, doc.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL, AT THE KITCHEN SINK</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( with great force . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Do n't shilly - shally, Louis. Promise me. Promise me. Promise me.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHTUB, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The washcloth has slipped enough so we can see his eyes are closed - he 's dozing .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Promise.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED KITCHEN TABLE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>To LOUIS , ELLIE , PASCOW , GAGE , and the corpse of SPOT enters JUD , his eyes shocked and staring .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( to LOUIS . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You do it for all the best reasons, but that ai n't why. You do it because it gets hold of you. you do it because you have to.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, IN THE BATHTUB, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The washrag has worked its way down to his mouth by now . His doze is deepening ; he 's started to snore a little . SOUND : A splash . Something has been dropped into the bath . LOUIS opens his eyes . Looks puzzled . Looks down . Eyes widen in shock .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHWATER, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A very large and very mangled dead rat floats in the bath , actually brushing against LOUIS 'S chest . Blood has begun to stain the water .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Turns his head , preparatory to leaping out .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE TOILET LID, WITH CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Its mouth yawns open . It hisses , showing bloodstained teeth .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHROOM</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS leaps from the tub . Grabs a towel and begins to rub himself frantically . He 's grossed out . The cat tries to arch against him and he hits it . CHURCH falls to the floor , hissing . LOUIS looks at the closed door .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>How the hell did you get in?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He may not know that , but he knows how it 's going to get out . He opens the door to the upstairs hall . If CHURCH does n't go at once , LOUIS helps it with his foot . Then he looks down at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BATHTUB WITH BRER RAT, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Staring at the rat . Over this : THE SOUND OF JET ENGINES .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  A DELTA 727</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Its landing gear unfolds preparatory to touching down at Bangor International Airport .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  A DEPLANING AREA  DAY</stage_direction>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, OUTSIDE THE SECURITY POINT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's looking anxiously for his people . In one hand he 's got half a dozen roses . His face lights up .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE DEPLANING AREA, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Here comes LOUIS 'S family . ELLIE is a little ahead . RACHEL is pushing GAGE in his stroller . ELLIE sees LOUIS and lights up .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Daddy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She runs for him .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUST OUTSIDE THE SECURITY POINT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ELLIE comes belting up to LOUIS , weaving among the deplanees like a slalom skier . She leaps into his arms . LOUIS swings her cheerfully .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Hi, sugar!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She smacks him noisily . He smacks her back just as noisily .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Daddy, is Church all right?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS 'S face changes . All at once he 's watchful .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. I guess so. He was sleeping on the front porch when I left.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Cause I had a bad dream about him. I dreamed he got hit by a car and you and Mr. Crandall buried him in the Pet Sematary.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( trying to smile . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>That was a silly dream, was n't it?</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Is he really all right?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Because you promised.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I know.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL reaches them . She 's pretty tired . Hair hanging in her face , good travelling clothes now looking a bit wrinkled and a bit stale .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Want to take your son, doc?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS does . GAGE is ecstatic . LOUIS kisses RACHEL deeply .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED KITCHEN, NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHURCH at the door , waiting to be let out . ELLIE does the honors . CHURCH oils out into the shed/garage . ELLIE closes the door . She looks distressed . She crosses the kitchen again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED LIVING ROOM, NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RACHEL , in a flannel nightgown , is watching TV . LOUIS is reading a medical tome and making notes . GAGE , zipped into a warm blanket suit , is sacking on the couch .</scene_description>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( entering . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Can cats have shampoos?</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Yes - you have to take them to someone who grooms animals, though. I think it's pretty expensive.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <parenthetical>( still upset . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I do n't care. I'll save up my allowance and pay for it. Church smells bad.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>I've noticed it, too. I'll cough up the money, Ellen.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>I hate that smell.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He looks both grim and sad - a man discovering that what you pay for you own , and what you own always comes home to you .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes - I hate it, too.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BLACK . And on it , a fourth title card : MISSY DANDRIDGE . SOUND : A pen scratching over paper .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  A STUDY DESK, CU</stage_direction>

Can not face this Pain . Sorry . '' The hand puts the pen down . It tears the paper in two , leaving just the half with the message .</scene_description>

    <stage_direction>INT.  THE NOOSE, CU</stage_direction>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE DANDRIDGE HOUSE, NIGHT</stage_direction>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CELLAR, WITH MISSY DANDRIDGE</stage_direction>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  IN FRONT OF THE GRACE METHODIST CHURCH  DAY</stage_direction>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS AND ELLIE, ON THE CHURCH STEPS</stage_direction>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>They're all turning on their lights! Daddy, why are they all turning on their lights in the middle of the day?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>JUD , dressed in a rusty old black suit and a black tie , comes out and stands with them . He looks haggard and old .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>They do it to honor the dead, Ellen.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Is that right, dad?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. To honor the dead.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CHURCH PARKING AREA</stage_direction>

  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LUDLOW CEMETARY  DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>-LSB- NOTE : In the book LOUIS finds it difficult to enter at night because of a high iron fence .     <character>MINISTER</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>May the Lord bless you and keep you ; may the Lord make his face to shine upon you, and comfort you, and lift you up, and give you peace. Amen.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, ELLIE, JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>As the mourners begin to break up , these three start back toward LOUIS 'S car .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Rachel not feeling well?</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Well. a touch of the flu.</dialogue>
    <character>ELLIE</character>
    <dialogue>She's in bed. She was throwing up. Ever since Mrs. Rogers called and said Missy -</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>That's enough, Ellen.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They 've reached the CREED station wagon .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Out of the mouths of babes, Louis.</dialogue>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>This babe has said enough.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He opens the front passenger door .</scene_description>

    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Ellie -</dialogue>

    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( v - o continues . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Bill was bitter - his son had been in the thick of it two years and then got shot in the leg - a clean flesh - wound. He was supposed to be coming home safe and sound. Instead, he come home in a box after all.</dialogue>

    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <parenthetical>( bitter . )</parenthetical>

    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( v.o. continues . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She knew it was an abomination. George Anderson, the town postmaster, was there. and Alan Purinton. Hannibal Benson. and me. I was there.</dialogue>

    <scene_description>It 's a ramshackle old farm which looks remarkably like the estate of that gentleman farmer Jordy Verrill . An old Ford pulls into the driveway , and the four men get out . SOUND BLEEDS IN : Most of all the SOUND OF THE CRICKETS . They go to the door , and JUD is wordlessly elected as the prime honcho . He knocks . No answer . Again . No answer . SOUND : Crazy laughter .</scene_description>
    <character>BILL BATERMAN</character>

  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LITTLE GOD SWAMP, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Nothing there .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>See? Just imagination. Just -</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We can barely see them because they are thick in mist , but he is standing on a couple of low , marshy tussocks . Suddenly a thick tentacle slimes its way out of the standing water and slithers around his ankle .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, LOOKING DOWN</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Nothing. there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns around and begins to walk again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The tentacle falls away .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, IN LITTLE GOD SWAMP</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MYRIAD SOUNDS , none of them pleasant - laughter , gobbling howls , screams . Sounds like the swamp has been invaded by a pack of escaped lunatics . LOUIS continues on regardless .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  WOODS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS comes into the frame . He 's obviously tiring now , but he keeps moving along . SOUND : Approaching footsteps . Big ones . Thudding ones . Something is coming which sounds approximately the size of a Tyrannosaurus Rex . And it just keeps getting louder and louder and louder . LOUIS looks plenty scared . SOUND : A falling tree .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  WOODS, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Those SOUNDS keep getting closer and closer . Another tree falls - we see this one . And now we see a SHAPE - just a SHAPE .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's scared almost to death . His face turns up . up . up .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE WOODS--AND THE SHAPE, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is vaguely manlike : perhaps sixty feet tall , perhaps eighty . We do n't see it very well , nor do we have to - I 'm not even sure it 's flesh and blood . But there is a clear suggestion of a head . Now it turns and looks down . looks at LOUIS CREED . We see great yellow eyes the size of lighthouse lamps . It makes a huge GRUNTING SOUND . and then walks on .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The SOUND OF FOOTFALLS is slowly diminishing .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It was the Wendigo. Dear God, I think the Wendigo just passed within sixty feet of me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slowly he begins to walk again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS, A NEW ANGLE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In the extreme f.g. is a tree which has just fallen - it is no small tree , either , but a great big old fir . LOUIS approaches it . Stops . Looks at the tree . Looks down at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE FOREST FLOOR, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Here is a gigantic animal track - if it was full of water , LOUIS could swim in it . It looks like no animal track we 've ever seen before . Three big claws at the end of it .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Looks up again . His face is set and hard .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>It does n't matter. Come on, Gage.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts to walk again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE MICMAC BURYING GROUND</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND : The wind , lonesome and keening . THE CAMERA MOVES SLOWLY toward the slope , dreaming its way over those rocky cairns . most of them burst apart . SOUND : Tortured breathing . Panting . LOUIS toils his way into view , carrying his bundle . He reaches the top . He makes his way slowly into the burying ground . He stumbles over a rock . Falls down . Slowly gathers his things together and gets up again . He goes a little further and then stops and looks at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  A BROKEN CAIRN AND THE GRAVE BENEATH, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We can also see the shredded remains of a green garbage bag .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He slowly kneels down . He puts the canvas tarp to one side and slowly takes the pick and shovel from the duffle bag . By now he is clearly a man approaching total exhaustion .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  A COUNTRY ROAD, WITH AN ARIES K</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It tracks past THE CAMERA .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE ARIES K WITH RACHEL AND PASCOW</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Both of them look tense . RACHEL is bolt upright behind the wheel . Suddenly , BANG ! as one of the tires blow .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ARIES K</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It goes skidding and slueing across the road , the rear tire half off the rim . IT climbs the curb and hits a tree .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She lurches forward , but she 's wearing her seat - belt - good girl ! She unbuckles it and gets out .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She looks at the car , which now has quite a bit more wrong with it than just a scratch up the side . RACHEL slumps , near tears . LOUIS is n't the only one who 's been through a lot tonight .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Now what?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PASCOW comes from around the tree as RACHEL walks to the road , looking for cars , or something . He looks urgent and upset .</scene_description>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>It's trying to stop you. Do you hear me? It's trying to stop you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL looks around uncertainly . a little afraid . As she scans the scene she looks at - and through - PASCOW .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Is anyone there?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>After a moment of silence she turns back to the road . Lights appear and brighten as a car approaches . RACHEL steps to the shoulder and after a moment she sticks out her thumb , surely for the first time in her life . The car sweeps by her without slowing .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  GAGE'S CAIRN, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS 'S hands enter the shot and put a few more rocks on it . THE CAMERA PULLS BACK and we see him surveying his work . Beside him is the canvas tarp , now open and empty . Absently , LOUIS stuffs the tarp into the duffle bag -LRB- where his tools have also been replaced -RRB- and stands up with a wince . One hand goes to his lower back . He looks down at the cairn .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Come back to me, Gage. Come back to us.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He turns away toward the stairs .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL, ON ROUTE 9</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She 's walking down the shoulder with her high heels in one hand . Lights . An approaching car . She turns , thumb out . The car blasts by .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shouts . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>MAY THE SEWERS OF RANGOON BACK UP IN YOUR BEDROOM, ASSHOLE!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She starts walking again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE FIELD BESIDE LOUIS'S HOUSE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS is moving down the path . As he passes the tire swing he pushes it , setting it in motion .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE GARAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOUIS slings the duffle bag wearily to one side and goes into the kitchen . CHURCH is under the table but LOUIS Does n't see him .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE UPSTAIRS HALL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SOUND of LOUIS slowly plodding up the stairs . He comes into view , dirty and exhausted , his hair hanging in his face . He walks down the hall toward the master bedroom .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BEDROOM</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The clock on the bedtable reads 2:17 A.M. LOUIS falls face - first on the immaculate bedspread and lies still . In this shot we should note the closet door is standing open .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE MICMAC BURYING GROUND, FEATURING GAGE'S CAIRN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA MOVES IN SLOWLY . Holds . Nothing for a beat . Then : A small white hand slams up through the rocks , hopefully scaring the living shit out of us . CAMERA MOVES CLOSER as the hand begins to feel around . It takes one of the rocks and pushes it aside . Another . Another . Another . The SOUNDS are not encouraging . It is GRUNTING and GROWLING . There is nothing human here . Rocks begin to tumble as GAGE starts to come out of his grave .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED BEDROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Fast asleep on the coverlet in his dirty jeans and black sweater .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>My babe is still takin ' a hike . But here comes another vehicle .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE DEADFALL IN THE PET SEMATARY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA MOVES IN on that snarling face . SOUNDS : GAGE coming . Dead dry breath . Low snarling noises . Now we see small feet in dirty black shoes walking down the deadfall .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Suddenly , as the lights appear , she does a Claudette Colbert , pulling her skirt up and exhibiting a very lovely leg . Lights - it 's an Orinco truck , naturally - spotlight her . The truck stops .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL AND THE TRUCK</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The driver leans over and opens the door .</scene_description>
    <character>DRIVER</character>
    <dialogue>Hop in, baby.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She does .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED KITCHEN, WITH CHURCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's under the kitchen table , green eyes gleaming . I think he loves dead , hates living . SOUND : The doorlatch . CHURCH MIAOWS .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, A NEW (LOW) ANGLE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>GAGE 'S shoes grit slowly across the linoleum , leaving dirty tracks . CHURCH turns to watch GAGE 'S passage , and then follows .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BEDROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CAMERA HOLDS ON LOUIS as those gritting footsteps approach . Then we pan to the closet . On the floor is LOUIS 'S little black bag . We hold on this as the footfalls near . A small white hand enters the frame and pulls the doctor - bag out of the closet . Now another hand enters the frame and opens the bag . The hands search around inside and bring out a scalpel . They hold it up . The GAGE - THING makes a contented SOUND .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE ORINCO TRUCK, ON ROUTE 9  NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It sweeps past THE CAMERA</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CAB, WITH RACHEL AND DRIVER</stage_direction>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Ca n't you go any faster?</dialogue>
    <character>TRUCKER</character>
    <dialogue>Lady, I got nine points on my license right now.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>I understand. It's just that -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She looks at him , pleading . The TRUCKER speeds up .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you. If you only understood how important this is -</dialogue>
    <character>TRUCKER</character>
    <dialogue>That's all right, babe. Only if we get stopped, next time I'll be the one hitchin' and you can give me a ride.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD, ON HIS PORCH</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>More deeply asleep than ever . Suddenly , from inside , comes the sound of Quiet Riot singing/screaming `` Bang Your Head . '' It 's the stereo , and boy , is it cranked . JUD straightens up so suddenly he almost falls off his chair . His hands go first to his earphones - his first thought on waking is that it 's coming from there - and then he hurries inside . CAMERA PANS DOWN to small muddy tracks on the porch floor .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE LIVING ROOM, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He hurries in , turns on the light , and rushes across to his stereo system , which is state - of - the - art digital - it looks like a flying saucer among the more traditional furnishings of the room . He shuts it off and looks around , frowning . SOUND : Todd Rundgren , singing `` Bang on the Drum All Day '' at the top of his voice . JUD 'S head snaps toward the SOUND .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  A SONY RADIO, CU</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE CAMERA PULLS BACK as JUD hurries across the kitchen to the counter , where the radio is . He turns it off , looking around , more bewildered than ever .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( sharply . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Who's here?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He walks toward the door which gives on the hall .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE HALL, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's dimly lit by light - spill from the living room and kitchen .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Come on, stop playing games!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Molly Hatchet , `` Flirtin ' with Disaster , '' being played top end , from upstairs . JUD hurries up . Let me suggest that there is a certain psychology at work here - for the moment he 's more concerned about waking the neighborhood with all this high - decible rock and roll than with the prowler . and he would certainly know who - or what - that prowler was , if he had time to think .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S BEDROOM</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He enters and turns on the light . We see a portable phonograph with the record , turning . JUD rushes over and turns it off . He looks around , and we see by his face that he knows .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Gage?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Are you the one playing games?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He goes to the window and looks out at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE, WITH THE STATION WAGON, JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE BEDROOM, WITH JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He turns slowly and walks toward the bed .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>Gage? Come on out.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He reaches in his pocket and brings out a pocket - knife . He unfolds the blade .</scene_description>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <dialogue>I want to show you something.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SOUND : Miaow !</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE DOORWAY, WITH CHURCH, JUD'S POV</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD, BY THE BED</stage_direction>
    <character>JUD</character>
    <parenthetical>( to the cat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How did you -?!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A small hand holding a scalpel shoots out from beneath the skirt of the coverlet and slashes JUD 'S calf ,</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He screams with pain and staggers backward .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD'S FEET</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The other hand shoots out . GAGE grabs one of JUD 'S ankles and pulls .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>With a startled yell , he falls .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  JUD AND GAGE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>This one 's got ta be pretty rough . George will know what to do . We finally see GAGE , but it should be clear to us that it 's not really GAGE at all . Some daemonic presence is riding inside the mouldering , disfigured shell of GAGE . There is a struggle . JUD is repeatedly slashed with the scalpel . Perhaps he gets GAGE a time or two with the pocketknife . GAGE screams and gibbers - nothing intelligible here ; only sounds . JUD expires . GAGE sits on top of him . and then bites into his throat .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ROUTE 9, BETWEEN THE CRANDALL AND CREED HOUSES</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Headlights . RACHEL 'S truck has arrived . It pulls up . RACHEL opens the passenger door , which is on JUD 'S side .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  ANGLE ON THE CAB</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>We can see PASCOW sitting in the passenger seat where RACHEL just was .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you so much.</dialogue>
    <character>TRUCKER</character>
    <dialogue>I did n't get a ticket, so you're welcome, lady.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( And , more seriously . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Whatever your problems are, I hope they work out.</dialogue>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>It's the end of the line for me, too - I'm not allowed any further.</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to the trucker . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'm sure things will be fine.</dialogue>
    <character>PASCOW</character>
    <dialogue>I'm not.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She closes the door and steps down . The truck starts off with a HISS OF RELEASED AIRBRAKES . As it pulls past her , RACHEL starts across the road , when :</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( soft voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She stops , startled . Her face wears a `` did I hear that ? '' expression . She looks back toward JUD 'S house .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( soft voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL walks halfway up JUD 'S paved walk and looks at :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  JUD'S HOUSE, RACHEL'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The one place in the whole world we do not want RACHEL to go .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  RACHEL</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She goes . Up the steps to the porch . All through this she 's been travelling with two bags : her handbag and a light tote with her initials on it . Now she sets the tote down on the top step and opens the porch door . She looks very uncertain . This is the wee hours of the morning , and someone else 's house . But . that voice .</scene_description>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy, I need you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RACHEL looks stunned - rocked . She steps onto the porch .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Who -</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The door to the house swings open . After a moment CHURCH comes into the doorway and sits down .</scene_description>
    <character>CHURCH</character>
    <dialogue>Miaow!</dialogue>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Church!</dialogue>
    <character>GAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mummy, I need you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She crosses to the open door .</scene_description>
    <character>RACHEL</character>
    <dialogue>Gage? Gage?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>No answer . RACHEL steps in .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT.  THE CREED HOUSE  MORNING</stage_direction>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE CREED BEDROOM, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He 's restless , having a very bad dream , from the look . He rolls back and forth . Closer and closer to the edge . Finally , with a wild yell , he goes over onto the floor .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, ON THE FLOOR</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He comes awake . Sits up . Ouch ! He 's aches from top to bottom and side to side . but his back is worst . His hands go to it .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Jesus!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He starts to get up very slowly , and this his eyes fix on :</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  GAGE'S TRACKS ON THE BEDROOM FLOOR, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>They enter the house , go to the closet , then leave again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Gage -?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He scrambles for the closet , his aches and pains forgotten . He stares in wildly .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE DOCTOR-BAG</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It 's open .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He pulls the doctor - bag out . His original hope is now tempered with the first signs of fear . He begins to go through the doctor - bag . Suddenly he brings out a case and opens it . The case is empty , but the indented shape is clear . There was a scalpel in this case . but not anymore .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Oh my God.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( Pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gage!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE HALL, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Gage!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LOUIS stands there , tensely listening , for a moment or two , but there 's only silence . He rushes down the hallway and opens the door to GAGE 'S room .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  GAGE'S ROOM, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Empty .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  LOUIS, ON THE STAIRS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>He goes downstairs , yelling GAGE 'S name .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Nothing . The phone RINGS . LOUIS almost jumps out of his skin reaching for it .</scene_description>
    <character>LOUIS</character>
    <dialogue>Hello!</dialogue>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( voice . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Hello, Louis - it's Irwin. I just wanted to be sure Rachel got back all right.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As IRWIN says this , LOUIS 'S eyes fix upon something .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE FLOOR, WITH TWO SETS OF GAGE-TRACKS, LOUIS'S POV</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One set comes in from the shed - garage and heads for the parlor and upstairs . The other comes out of the parlor and crosses to the kitchen door giving directly on the outside .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT.  THE KITCHEN, WITH LOUIS</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In his eyes we suddenly see that he understands everything . or almost everything .</scene_description>
    <character>IRWIN</character>
