    "summary":"The Creed family—Louis, Rachel, and their children Ellie and Gage—move from Chicago to rural Ludlow, Maine, after Louis is offered a job as a physician with the University of Maine. They befriend their elderly neighbor Jud Crandall, who takes them to an isolated pet cemetery (misspelled "sematary") in the forest behind the Creeds' new home. On his first day at work, Louis encounters Victor Pascow, a jogger who has been mortally injured after being hit by a truck. He warns Louis about the pet cemetery before he dies, calling Louis by name despite the fact they have not previously met. That night, Pascow comes to Louis as a ghost and leads him to the Pet Sematary, warning him not to cross the barrier because the ground beyond is "sour". Louis awakens, assuming it was a dream, but notices his feet are covered in dirt. During Thanksgiving while the family is gone, Ellie's cat, Church, is run down on the highway. Realizing that Ellie will be devastated, Jud takes Louis beyond the cemetery and deep into the woods, where they reach an ancient Miꞌkmaq burial ground. Jud instructs Louis to bury the cat and warns him not to tell anyone else about what they have done. The next day a reanimated Church returns to the house, a shell of what he was before; he stinks, moves sluggishly, and is vicious towards Louis. Jud explains that as a boy he himself revived his beloved pet dog in the Miꞌkmaq ground and that although the cat might be different, it will save Ellie the grief of losing her favorite pet. Sometime later, Gage is killed by a truck along the same highway. The family is devastated, and Jud anticipates that Louis is considering burying his son in the Miꞌkmaq ground, although Louis denies it. Jud believes that introducing Louis to the ritual ground aroused the malevolent forces present there, which caused Gage's death. He tells him the story of a local named Bill Baterman who buried his son Timmy in the Miꞌkmaq ground after he was killed in World War II. Timmy returned as a malevolent zombie, terrifying the townsfolk. A group of men including Jud tried destroying Timmy by lighting the Baterman house on fire, only for Bill to perish with his son. Jud insists that the burial ground is evil and Louis must never try to bury his son there. After the funeral, Rachel and Ellie leave for Chicago while Louis remains home. Despite Pascow and Jud's warnings, Louis exhumes his son's body and buries him at the ritual site. In Chicago, Pascow appears to Ellie in a dream and warns her that Louis is about to do something terrible. Rachel is unnerved by her daughter's dream but is only able to reach Jud when she calls, who tells her Louis is not home. She decides to return to Maine, much to Jud's alarm. That night, Gage returns home and steals a scalpel from his father's bag. He taunts Jud before slashing his Achilles tendon and his mouth horizontally through the lips, before biting his throat, killing him. Rachel returns home and is lured into Jud's house by the voice and specter of her dead sister Zelda, only to discover that she is actually seeing Gage, holding a scalpel. In shock and disbelief, Rachel reaches down to hug her son and he kills her. Waking up from his sleep, Louis notices Gage's muddy footprints in the house and discovers that his scalpel is missing. Receiving a phone call from Gage that he has "played" with Jud and Mommy, he fills three syringes with morphine and heads to Jud's house. Encountering Church, he kills the cat with an injection before entering the house. Gage taunts him further and Louis is startled by Rachel's falling corpse hanged from the attic before he is attacked by his son. After a brief battle, Louis kills Gage with the morphine injection. He then lights the house on fire, leaving it to burn as he carries Rachel's body from the fire. Pascow appears and warns Louis not to "make it worse" but grief-stricken Louis believes that because Rachel was not dead as long as Gage was, burying her "will work this time". Pascow cries out in frustration and vanishes as Louis passes through him. That night, Rachel returns to Louis and the couple embrace. Rachel takes a large knife from the counter as Louis screams."

    <scene_description>It 's very late . It 's quiet . Just the sounds of The City LINDA SANTANA CRAIG , an attractive Hispanic woman in her thirties , waits at the ELEVATED STATION for the F train . Linda looks great . She 's dressed festively but tastefully . Next to her is her eleven year old DAUGHTER , ALICIA . She is twirling about the platform , still jazzed from the birthday party they attended in The City . Alicia wears a black dress with a pink cardigan and has a pink handbag . We notice a CHARM BRACELET with four - leaf clovers on her right wrist . The mother and daughter wait alone at one end of the station platform . TWO TEENAGE BOYS wait at the other end . They speak soft , SLURRED SPANISH to each other . Linda gives the boys a glance and evaluates . She watches them as Alicia spits a wad of gum into her mom 's open hand . The Boys approach . Linda tenses . At the last second the boys make a hard left turn and disappear down the stairwell . It 's quiet again . Linda relaxes , smiles at her daughter . The F TRAIN is rounding the final bend into the station . Their focus is on this train . It 's getting closer , louder . And so they do n't see , do n't hear the Boys coming back up the stairwell behind them . Not until the boys have the mother and daughter boxed in and the one who can hardly grow a mustache is showing them his gun . Linda puts her arm around her daughter . Alicia looks terrified . The train roars INTO THE STATION as Linda quickly hands over her purse , her watch . She hands over her engagement ring and her wedding band . One of the boys yanks Alicia 's little purse away from her . The other boy fumbles the wedding band . The ring CLANGS to the ground and rolls to a stop a few feet away . We hear MEN 'S VOICES echoing up the stairwell . Now the Boys are boxed in . And starting to panic . - THE TRAIN DOORS SLIDE OPEN - . The Boys see their way out and step into the last empty rail car , leaving the mother and daughter alone on the platform . Through the window on the train , Linda stares at the boy holding her daughter 's purse , her face hardening into a MASK OF CONTEMPT . The boy clocks it . Who does she think she is ? - THE TRAIN DOORS BEGIN TO CLOSE - When a HAND WITH TATTOOED KNUCKLES reaches out and stops the car doors from closing . A forearm and gun extend out of that last subway car . There 's a muzzle flash . a distant POP . a cloud of smoke . a mist of blood . and Linda 's body collapses on itself . Alicia 's face , shock , terror and blood .</scene_description>

    "summary":"In New York City in 1991, Alyssa "Ally" Craig is waiting with her mother for the subway, when they are mugged by two young men, who shoot her mother after boarding the train. Ten years later, Ally is a student at New York University (NYU), and lives with her father, Neil, a New York Police Department detective. Tyler Hawkins audits classes at NYU and works at the university bookstore. He has a strained relationship with his workaholic businessman father, Charles, because his older brother, Michael, died by suicide years before. Charles ignores his youngest child, Caroline, of whom Tyler is protective. One night, with his roommate, Aidan, Tyler gets involved in somebody else's fight, and is arrested by Neil. Aidan calls Charles to bail Tyler out, but he does not stick around to have a conversation with his father. Aidan sees Neil dropping Ally off, realizing that she is his daughter. He approaches Tyler with the idea to get back at the detective by persuading him to sleep with and dump Ally. Tyler and Ally go to dinner, kiss at the end of the night, and continue seeing one another. While at Tyler's apartment, Aidan convinces the pair to go to a party, after which Ally is very drunk, and ends up throwing up. She passes out before Tyler can get her to tell him Neil's phone number. The following day, she and her father argue. Neil slaps her, and Ally flees back to Tyler's apartment. Caroline, a budding artist, is featured in an art show, and Tyler asks his father to attend the show. When he fails to show up, Tyler confronts him in a board room filled with people, which causes his father's frustration to boil over. Neil's partner recognizes Tyler with Ally on a train, so Neil breaks into Tyler's apartment, and confronts him. Tyler provokes Neil by confessing to Aidan's plan and his initial reason for meeting Ally, which forces Tyler to confess to Ally. She leaves and returns home. Aidan visits Ally at her father's home to explain that he is to blame, and Tyler is genuinely in love with her. Caroline is bullied by classmates at a birthday party where they cut a chunk of her hair off. Ally and Aidan visit Tyler's mother's apartment, where Caroline is sobbing. Tyler accompanies his sister back to school, and when her classmates tease her for her new haircut, Tyler turns violent, and ends up in jail. Charles is impressed that Tyler stood up for his sister, and they connect. Charles asks Tyler to meet with the lawyers at his office. Tyler spends the night with Ally, and they reveal they love each other after making love. Charles takes Caroline to school. He calls Tyler to let him know this, and explains that he will be late. Tyler is happy that his father is spending time with Caroline. He tells Charles that he will wait in his office. He looks on Charles's computer, featuring a slideshow of pictures with Tyler, Michael, and Caroline when they were younger. After Charles drops Caroline off at school, she sits in her classroom, where the teacher writes the date on the blackboard as September 11, 2001. Tyler looks out the window of his father's office, which is revealed to be located on the 101st floor of the North Tower of the World Trade Center. Once the terrorist attacks begin, the rest of the family, Aidan and Ally, look at the towers before the camera pans over the rubble, showing Tyler's diary. In a voice-over of his diary, Tyler reveals to Michael that he loves him, and he forgives him for killing himself. Tyler is buried next to Michael. Some time later, Caroline and Charles seem to have a healthy father-daughter relationship. Aidan, who has since gotten a tattoo of Tyler's name on his arm, is working hard in school, and Ally gets on the subway at the same spot where her mother was killed."

    "summary":"Julianne Potter (Julia Roberts), a 27-year-old New York City restaurant critic, receives a call from her lifelong friend Michael O'Neal (Dermot Mulroney). In college, the two made an agreement that if neither of them were married by the time they turned 28, they would marry each other. Three weeks before her 28th birthday, Michael tells her that in four days, he will marry Kimmy Wallace (Cameron Diaz), a 20-year-old University of Chicago student from a wealthy family, and the daughter of the owner of the Chicago White Sox. Julianne is disappointed that Michael will marry someone whom she perceives as being so wrong for him, and someone he has known for such a short time. She realizes that she is in love with Michael, and heads to Chicago, intent on sabotaging his wedding. Soon after arriving she meets Kimmy, who asks her to be the maid of honor. This sets off a subplot in which Julianne must pretend to be the dutiful maid of honor while secretly scheming ways to prevent the wedding from happening. When trying on dresses, Michael walks in on Julianne in her underwear as he tells her that she looks great, leaving her to think that she still has a chance to get him back. She also engages in petty sabotage—for example, taking Kimmy and Michael to a karaoke bar after discovering that Kimmy is a terrible singer. When these tactics fail, Julianne enlists the aid of her gay friend, George (Rupert Everett) to help her break Michael and Kimmy up. George flies to Chicago to meet Julianne and persuades her to do the obvious: tell Michael that she is in love with him. While at a tailor shop, George convinces Julianne to tell Michael her true feelings before it’s too late. While she finally has the chance to tell him, she gets nervous and quickly tells him that she is engaged to George to get him jealous. Speechless, Michael is shocked about seeing Julianne with someone other than him. Since Julianne didn’t tell the truth, George tries to get back at her by embarrassing her. On the taxi ride to the church, he snuggles up to Julianne to make her uncomfortable in front of Michael. At a big family lunch with all of Kimmy's family in attendance, he also decides to embarrass Julianne by telling everyone an exaggerated tale of how they met, and sings “I Say a Little Prayer” as the whole restaurant joins in. After George leaves to catch his flight back home, Julianne tells Michael the truth about her and George not being together, and Michael admits to being jealous, thinking they were really engaged. Since it will be their last opportunity to spend time together before his new life as a married man, Michael gets Julianne to go on a boat ride with him. He expresses some skepticism about marrying Kimmy, explaining that he and Kimmy don't share a special song like he and Julianne do. Michael discreetly gives Julianne the invitation to tell him she's in love with him, but she lets the opportunity pass. Michael starts singing their song, “The Way You Look Tonight” in her ear as he grabs Julianne and holds her while they dance one last time. As the wedding date is approaching, Julianne becomes more desperate to win Michael. She uses Kimmy’s father's email account to forge a fake message to Michael's boss, and chooses to save it for later instead of deleting it — that way it will give Kimmy the opportunity to continue on with school and cause Michael to want to leave Kimmy if he can’t have his dream job. Realizing Kimmy’s father had sent out all of his emails, including the fake one Julianne wrote, she forces Michael to go back to his job so she can get the letter before he finds it. Since the place was closed, Julianne and Michael make their way back to the hotel. Unfortunately, Michael already received the letter and becomes upset, calling off the wedding and leaving Julianne alone as he goes for a walk. The next morning, the day of the wedding, Julianne tries to sabotage the situation further; as Michael and Kimmy are not speaking to each other, they communicate through Julianne, not realizing she is trying to manipulate them into breaking up for good. In spite of this, Michael and Kimmy decide they do love each other and want to get married after all. Feeling vulnerable, Julianne then takes a walk with Michael, during which she finally confesses her love to him. She asks him to marry her, and passionately kisses him. Kimmy witnesses this, and runs off, but Michael chases her while Julianne chases Michael. As Julianne is chasing after Michael in a truck, she frantically calls George explaining the situation, and George makes it clear to her that Kimmy is the one Michael loves because he is chasing after her and not Julianne. Julianne finds Michael at Chicago Union Station, where he is looking for Kimmy, and confesses all to him. Despite his anger at her deception, Michael forgives Julianne, and they split up to look for Kimmy. Julianne then tracks down Kimmy in the bathroom of Comiskey Park (Kimmy's family has a private viewing box at the stadium). Kimmy, rightly furious with Julianne, confronts her, while the other women watch, immediately siding with Kimmy and are disgusted with Julianne's dirty tactics. Julianne, however, apologizes and explains to Kimmy that she kissed Michael unexpectedly, but he didn't kiss her back because he was in love with Kimmy. Julianne declares that Kimmy has won, and that she accepts Michael's decision. Kimmy and Julianne reconcile with each other while the witnesses applaud. After the wedding, at the reception, Julianne gives a speech as Kimmys maid of honor and  says that Michael and Kimmy can use Julianne and Michael's special song until they find one of their own, essentially acting like a true best friend. Julianne wishes them well, and she and Michael share their goodbyes, both of them finally moving on with their lives. Later, Julianne is surprised by George showing up at the wedding reception. The movie ends with the two of them happily sharing a dance together."

North of the city was the Curtain Theatre , home to England 's most famous actor , Richard Burbage . Across the river was the competition , built by Philip Henslowe , a business with a cash flow problem . The Rose . Gradually a building is revealed , The Rose Theatre , three - tiered , open to the elements and empty . On the floor , roughly printed , a poster - torn , soiled , out of date . It says : SEPT. 7TH & 8TH AT NOON . MR. EDWARD ALLEYN AND THE ADMIRAL 'S MEN AT THE ROSE THEATRE , BANKSIDE THE LAMENTABLE TRAGEDIE OF THE MONEYLENDER REVENG 'D OVER THIS the screams of a man under torture . The screams are coming from the curtained stage .</scene_description>
    <character>VOICE</character>
    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You Mongrel! Why do you howl When it is I who am bitten?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The theatre owner , PHILLIP HENSLOWE , is the man screaming . HENSLOWE 'S boots are on fire . He is pinioned in a chair , with his feet stuck out over the hot colas of a fire burning in a brazier . He is being held in that position by LAMBERT , who is a thug employed by FENNYMAN , who is the owner of the VOICE . The fourth man , FREES , is FENNYMAN 'S bookkeeper .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>What am I, Mr. Lambert?</dialogue>
    <character>LAMBERT</character>
    <dialogue>Bitten, Mr. Fennyman.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>How badly bitten, Mr. Frees?</dialogue>
    <character>FREES</character>
    <dialogue>Twelve pounds, one shilling and four pence, Mr. Fennyman, including interest.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Aaagh! I can pay you!</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>When?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Two weeks, three at the most, Aaaagh! For pity's sake.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Take his feet out. Where will you get</dialogue>
    <character>FREES</character>
    <parenthetical>( the mathematical genius with a notebook . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sixteen pounds, five shillings and nine pence</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>including interest in three weeks?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>I have a wonderful new play!</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Put his feet in.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>It's a comedy.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Cut his nose off.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>A new comedy. By Will Shakespeare!</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>And his ears.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>And a share. We will be partners, Mr. Fennyman!</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( hesitating . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Partners!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>It's a crowd - tickler - mistaken identities, a shipwreck, a pirate king, a bit with a dog, and love triumphant.</dialogue>
    <character>LAMBERT</character>
    <dialogue>I think I've seen it. I did n't like it.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>This time it is by Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>What's the title?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo and Ethel the Pirate's Daughter.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Good title.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FENNYMAN snaps his fingers at FREES and LAMBERT . LAMBERT unties HENSLOWE , FREES starts writing a contract .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A play takes time. Find actors... rehearsals... let's say open in three weeks. That's - what - five hundred groundlings at tuppence each, in addition four hundred groundlings tuppence each, in addition four hundred backsides at three pence - a penny extra for a cushion, call it two hundred cushions, say two performance for safety how much is that Mr. Frees?</dialogue>
    <character>FREES</character>
    <dialogue>Twenty pounds to the penny, Mr. Fennyman.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Correct!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>But I have to pay the actors and the authors.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>A share of the profits.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>There's never any</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Of course not!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( impressed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mr. Fennyman, I think you may have hit on something.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FENNYMAN slaps a contract down on the table next to n ink - pot and quill .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Sign here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE takes the quill and signs .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Romeo and Ethel The Pirate's Daughter... Almost finished?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Without doubt he is completing it at this very moment.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WILL'S ROOM. DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A small cramped space in the eaves of a building . A cluttered shelf containing various objects , wedged between crumpled pieces of paper . Among those we have time to observe : a skull , a mug that says A PRESENT FROM STRATFORD - UPON - AVON . At infrequent intervals further pieces of crumpled paper are tossed towards the shelf . The man who is throwing them , WILL SHAKESPEARE , is bent over a table , writing studiously with a quill . Now we see what he is writing : Will is practising his signature , over and over again . `` Will Shagsbeard ... W Shakspur ... William Shasper ... '' Each time he is dissatisfied , and each time he crumples , and tosses it away . Suddenly WILL becomes impatient . He jumps up and goes to the loft area in the rafters , where he sleeps , and starts to pull on his boots . At this point the door opens and HENSLOWE walks in . He is out of breath and his feet hurt .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Will! Where is my play? Tell me you have it nearly done! Tell me you have it started.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( desperately . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You have begun?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( struggling with his boots . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Doubt that the stars are fire, doubt that the sun doth move</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>No, no, we have n't the time. Talk prose. Where is my play?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( tapping his forehead and heading out the door . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It is all locked safe in here</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>God be praised!</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( then doubt . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Locked?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>As soon as I have found my muse</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. STREET. OUTSIDE WILL'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL lives in a crowded area of the city . Hawkers are crying their wares , tract - sellers , delivery boys , and merchants go about their business . HENSLOWE catches up with WILL as he strides purposefully along .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( catching up . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Who is she this time?!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>She is always Aphrodite.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Aphrodite Baggot who does it behind the Dog and Trumpet?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Henslowe, you have no soul so how can you understand the emptiness that seeks a soulmate?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I am a dead man and buggered to boot. My theatre is close by the plague these twelve weeks, my company is playing the inn - yards of England, while Burbage and the Chamberlain's Men are invited to court and receive ten pounds to play your piece, written for my theatre, by my writer, at my risk when you were green and grateful -</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>What piece? Richard Crookback?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>No - it's comedy they want, Will! Comedy! Like Romeo and Ethel?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Who wrote that?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Nobody! You are writing it for me! I gave you three pounds a month since.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Half what you owed me. I am still due for One Gentleman of Verona.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. ANOTHER STREET. DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE 'S hardly paused in his appeal .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Will! What is money to you and me? I, your patron, you my wordwright! When the plague lifts Burbage will have a new Christopher Marlowe for the Curtain and I have nothing for the Rose.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL stops .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Henslowe, will you lend me fifty pounds?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( staggered . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Fifty pounds? What for?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Burbage offers me a partnership in the Chamberlain's Men. For fifty pounds my hired player days are over.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Cut out my heart! Throw my liver to the dogs!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( answering for him . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No, then.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL turns down a side street .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. MARKETPLACE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE and WILL are crossing a crowded marketplace where a Puritan preacher , MAKEPEACE , is haranguing anyone who will listen .</scene_description>
    <character>MAKEPEACE</character>
    <dialogue>and the Lord shall smite them! Yea, harken to me. The theatres are handmaidens of the devil! Under the name of the Curtain, the players breed lewdness in your wives, rebellion in your servants, idleness in your apprentices and wickedness in your children! And the Rose smells thusly rank by any name! I say a plague on both their houses!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As he passes WILL gratefully makes a mental note .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DR. MOTH'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL turns into a narrow street and walks toward a doorway .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Where are you going?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>To my weekly confession.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As HENSLOWE arrives the door closes in his face . A sign identifies the place as the premises of Dr. MOTH , apothecary , alchemist , astrologer , seer , interpreter of dreams , and priest of psyche . HENSLOWE looks puzzled .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DR. MOTH'S HOUSE. DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A stuffed alligator hangs from the ceiling , pills , potions , amulets and charms , star charts and mystic paraphernalia festoon the place . Testimonials and framed degrees hang on the walls . WILL lying on a couch , on his back . His eyes are closed DR. MOTH sits by the couch , listening to WILL and occasionally making a note on a pad he holds on his knee . What we have here is nothing less than the false dawn of analysis . The session is being timed by an hourglass .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Words, words, words... once, I had the gift... I could make love out of words as a potter makes cups out of clay love that overthrows empires, love that binds two hearts together come hellfire and brimstones... for sixpence a line, I could cause a riot in a nunnery... but now</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>And yet you tell me you lie with women?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL seems unwiling to respond . DR. MOTH refers to his notes .</scene_description>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Black Sue, Fat Phoebe, Rosaline, Burbage's seamstress ; Aphrodite, who does it behind the Dog and</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( interrupting . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Aye, now and again, but what of it? I have lost my gift.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>I am here to help you. Tell me in your own words.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I have lost my gift.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( not finding this easy . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's as if my quill is broken. As if the organ of the imagination has dried up. As if the proud tower of my genius has collapsed.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>Interesting.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Nothing comes.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>Most interesting.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>It is like trying to a pick a lock with a wet herring.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <parenthetical>( shrewdly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Tell me, are you lately humbled in the act of love?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL turns towards him . How did he know that ?</scene_description>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How long has it been?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>A goodly length in times past, but lately</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>No, no. You have a wife, children</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The sand runs through the hourglass .</scene_description>
    <character>LATER</character>
    <dialogue>Not much sand left.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I was a lad of eighteen. Anne Hathaway was a woman, half as old again.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>A woman of property?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shrugs . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She had a cottage. One day, she was three months gone with child, so</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>And your relations?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>On my mother's side the Ardens</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>No, your marriage bed.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Four years and a hundred miles away in Stratford. A cold bed too, since the twins were born. Banishment was a blessing.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>So now you are free to love</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>yet can not love nor write it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>DR. MOTH reaches for a glass snake bracelet .</scene_description>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>Here is a bangle found in Psyche's temple on Olympus cheap at four pence. Write your name on a paper and feed it in the snake.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL looks at the snake bangle in wonder .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Will it restore my gift?</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>The woman who wears the snake will dream of you, and your gift will return. Words will flow like a river. I will see you in a week.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He holds out his hand . WILL drops a sovereign into it , and takes the bracelet .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DR. MOTH'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL comes out . HENSLOWE is waiting , standing in a horse trough to ease his feet . WILL walks straight past him , and HENSLOWE follows .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Now where? Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>To the Palace at Whitehall.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BACKSTAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WHITEHALL means nothing yet . We are behind closed curtains on a stage busy with preparations for the imminent performance of Two Gentlemen of Verona . This is not a theatre but a banqueting hall , as we will see . RICHARD BURBAGE is to play `` PROTEUS . '' A BOY PLAYER will play `` SILVIA , '' and last minute improvements to his makeup etc. are being applied by BURBAGE 'S mistress ROSALINE . `` LAUNCE , '' one of the clowns , is the famous comedian WILL KEMPE . `` LAUNCE 'S '' dog , CRAB is in KEMPE 'S charge and is not helping much . There is no set . A helpful placard reading VERONA - AN OPEN PLACE , is ready to hand . MUSICIANS can be heard tuning their instruments . From the other side of the curtain there is an expectant bubbub . KEMPE leads the dog into the wings and rummages in a box of proops . He finds a skull . He has one foot on the box , his elbow on his knee , he looks at the skull ... in other words he reminds us of Hamlet . We see this from the POV of WILL , who is just entering through a door backstage .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( approaching . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Prithee, Mr. Kempe, break a leg. You too, good Crab.</dialogue>
    <character>KEMPE</character>
    <dialogue>Crab is nervous. He has never played the Palace. When will you write me a tragedy, Will? I could do it.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>No, they would laugh at Seneca if you played it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL 'S attention has been caught by ROSALINE , BURBAGE 'S mistress . ROSALINE is big breasted , dark - eyed , dark - haired , sexual .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to ROSALINE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My sleeve wants for a button, Mistress Rosaline, where were my seamstress's eyes?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BURBAGE kisses her mouth and slaps her behind . He comes over to greet WILL .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>There is no dog in the first scene, Will Kempe, thank you. How goes it Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I am still owed money for this play, Burbage.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Not from me. I only stole it. When are you coming over to the Chamberlain's Men?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>When I have fifty pounds.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ROSALINE brings over the last elements of BURBAGE 'S costume and helps him into them .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Are you writing?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( nods somewhat defensively . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A comedy. All but done, a pirate comedy, wonderful.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>What is the chief part?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo. Wit, swordsman, lover.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>The title?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>I will play him. Bring it tomorrow.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>It's for Henslowe. He paid me.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>How much?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Ten pounds.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>You're a liar.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BURBAGE digs under his costume for his purse , which is on a waistband , over his corset .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I swear it. He wants Romeo for Ned and the Admiral's Men.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Ned is wrong for it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL turns to see HENSLOWE approaching .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <parenthetical>( to WILL . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Here is two sovereigns - I'll give you two more when you show me the pages.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Done.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( arriving . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Burbage, I will see you hanged for a pickpocket.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>The Queen has commanded, she loves a comedy and the Master of the Revels favours us.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>And what favour does Mr. Tilney receive from you?</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Ask him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Master of the Revels -LRB- TILNEY -RRB- comes through the curtain officiously .</scene_description>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>She comes!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He disappears back through the curtains . The hubbub falls silent , rather dramatically , and all the busy PLAYERS know what that means : they all crowd to the curtain and find places to peep through .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. FRONT OF HOUSE/STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE POV OF THE PLAYERS . The arrival of QUEEN ELIZABETH , aged sixty , coming to take her place in the audience at front centre . The hill is crowded with lords and ladies , bowing ELIZABETH to her seat , which is raised high on a pedestal , affording the QUEEN an uninterrupted view of the play , and the audience an uninterrupted view of the QUEEN . Trumpets sound . Close on a small piece of paper : a quill is writing `` W. Shakespeare . '' WILL rolls the paper up carefully and slips it into the mouth of the snake bangle . The curtain draws back and CONDELL as `` VALENTINE '' and BURBAGE as `` PROTEUS '' begin the play .</scene_description>
    <character>CONDELL AS VALENTINE</character>
    <dialogue>`` Cease to persuade, my loving Proteus ; Home - keeping youth have ever homely wits...''</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. THE WINGS/BACKSTAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>With BURBAGES 'S presence accounted for on stage , ROSALINE curls an arm around WILL 'S neck . They kiss hungrily . After a moment , WILL pulls back .</scene_description>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>When will you write me a sonnet, Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I have lost my gift.</dialogue>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>You left it in my bed. Come to look for it again.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Are you to be my muse, ROSALINE?</dialogue>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>Burbage has my keeping but you have my heart.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL takes the snake bracelet and slips it onto her arm . ROSALINE looks at it , then at WILL . Then they kiss again , but WILL is distracted by the sound of coughing from the auditorium .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>You see? The consumptives plot against me. `` Will Shakespeare has a play, let us go and cough through it.''</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>`` VALENTINE '' is on stage with `` PROTEUS . '' CONDELL AS VALENTINE `` To be in love , where scorn is bought with groans : Coy looks with heart sore sighs ; One fading moment 's mirth With twenty watchful , weary , tedious nights ... '' As the scene continues , WILL appears at the back of the hall and finds himself next to HENSLOWE .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I feel a scene coming on.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Is it about a pirate's daughter?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BACK OF THE BANQUETING HALL/STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Laughter . It is later , and KEMPE is now on stage with his dog . The audience is roaring .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>You see? Comedy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>QUEEN ELIZABETH 'S idiosyncratic laugh rises above the others .</scene_description>
    <character>QUEEN</character>
    <dialogue>Well played, Master Crab, I commend you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She throws a sweetheart on the stage and the dog wolfs it down . Everyone applauds .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Love and a bit with a dog, that's what they like.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now we meet VIOLA . VIOLA DE LESSEPS is twenty - five and beautiful , and she is laughing with great natural enjoyment . She sits slightly apart from her small family group - her parents , SIR ROBERT DE LESSEPS and LADY MARGARET DE LESSEPS . Part of the group but seated behind as befits her lower status is VIOLA 'S NURSE . Elsewhere is LORD WESSEX , our villain . WESSEX is in his forties , dark cruel , self - important . He has noticed VIOLA . The nurse notices him .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. FRONT OF HOUSE/STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LATER . `` VALENTINE '' is on stage alone . He is speaking the speech rather more coarsely than the version we hear later .</scene_description>
    <character>CONDELL AS VALENTINE</character>
    <dialogue>`` What light is light if Silvia be not seen? What joy is joy, if Silvia be not by? Unless it be to think that she is by And feed upon the shadow of perfection...''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now we see that VIOLA knows the speech by heart , and is silently mouthing it with the actor .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>There's a lady knows your play by heart.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But when he turns to WILL he finds that WILL has gone .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WILL'S ROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL comes into his room , goes straight to his table in the window , and arranges pen , ink , and paper . Now he has his ritual : he spins round once in a circle , rubs his hands together and spits on the floor . Then he sits down , picks up his pen , and stares in front of him . PAUSE . Then he begins to write .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The NURSE is undressing her , though VIOLA tries intermittently to push her away . She is still bright with excitement .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Did you like Proteus or Valentine best? Proteus for speaking, Valentine for looks.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>I liked the dog, for laughs.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>But Silvia I did not care for much. His fingers were red from fighting and he spoke like a schoolboy at lessons. Stage love will never be true love while the law of the land has our heroines played by pipsqueak boys in petticoats! Oh, when can we see another?</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>When the Queen commands it.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>But at the playhouse. Nurse?</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Be still.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now the NURSE is cleaning VIOLA 'S ears , one by one , of course . She has an ear - cleaning implement for this . VIOLA submits .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Playhouses are not for well - born ladies.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>I am not so well - born.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Well - monied is the same as well - born and well - married is more so. Lord Wessex was looking at you tonight.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>All the men at court are without poetry. If they look at me they see my father's fortune. I will have poetry in my life. And adventure. And love. Love above all.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Like Valentine and Silvia?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>No. not the artful postures of love, but love that over - throws life. Unbiddable, ungovernable, like a riot in the heart, and nothing to be done, come ruin or rapture. Love like there has never been in a play.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I will have love or I will end my days as a.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>As a nurse.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( kissing her . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But I would be Valentine and Silvia too. Good Nurse, God save you and good night. I would stay asleep my whole life if I could dream myself into a company of players.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>VIOLA goes over to the window .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The NURSE thrusts a twig to her face .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Clean your teeth while you dream, then.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Automatically , VIOLA takes the twig and begins brushing her teeth , all the while looking downriver towards the Rose . The NURSE attends her with a beaker of water , and a bowl .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Now spit</dialogue>
    <scene_description>VIOLA gazes longingly towards the Rose ... And , there and then , she makes a plan .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. SQUARE IN FRONT OF THE ROSE THEATRE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE is making his way from the theatre to the market place when FENNYMAN and LAMBERT appear at either shoulder and propel him back the way he came . FREES follows behind .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>This time we take your boots off!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>What have I done, Mr. Fennyman?</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>The theatres are all closed by the plague!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, that.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>by order of the Master of the Revels!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Fennyman, let me explain about the theatre business.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( they stop . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>The natural condition is one of insurmountable obstacles on the road to imminent disaster. Believe me, to be close by the plague is a bagatelle in the ups and downs of owning a theatre.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>So what do we do?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Nothing. Strangely enough, it all turns out well.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>How?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't know. It's a mystery.</dialogue>
    <character>LAMBERT</character>
    <parenthetical>( dumbly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Should I kill him, Mr. Fennyman?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>At this point din is heard in the background . a messenger , ringing a bell , is running though the street .</scene_description>
    <character>MESSENGER</character>
    <dialogue>The theatres are reopened. By order of the Master of the Revels, the theatres are reopened</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FENNYMAN is intrigued .</scene_description>
    <character>FREES</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Fennyman! Mr. Tilney has opened the playhouses.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Yes I heard.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE plays his temporary advantage modestly , shrugging himself free of LAMBERT 'S grip .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to LAMBERT . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>If you would n't mind</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE continues on his way . FENNYMAN watches HENSLOWE , curious .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Where is the play?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, it's coming, it's coming.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WILL'S ROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is . WILL is writing furiously . A burnt - down candle is still alight , although it is day outside the window . He has been writing all night . He has written about ten pages . Pleased with himself and excited , he gathers them up and leaves the room like a man with a mission .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. WILL'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Leaving the house , pages in hand , WILL nearly knocks down HENSLOWE who has come to see him .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Will! The theatres are</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Before he can finish , WILL brandishes the pages in his hand .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo and Rosaline. Scene One! God, I'm good!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Rosaline? You mean Ethel.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL has gone .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. BURBAGE'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>BURBAGE lives in another part of the city . WILL bangs through the door without ceremony .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shouting . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Richard!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BURBAGE'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL enters and calls out .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Burbage?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BURBAGE'S BEDROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL charges into the bedroom . ROSALINE is in bed . The Master of the Revels is pulling up his breeches . WILL is shattered .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Tilney</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The unsuccessful snake bracelet glints at him from ROSALINE 'S arm .</scene_description>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>Like you, I found him not at home!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>So this is the favour you find in the Chamberlain's Men.</dialogue>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>Will!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to ROSALINE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I would have made you immortal.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( turning to go . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Tell Burbage he has lost a new play by Will Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>What does Burbage care of that? He is readying the Curtain for Kit Marlowe.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>You have opened the playhouses?</dialogue>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>I have, Master Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>But the plague</dialogue>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <parenthetical>( sighs . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes, I know. But he was always hanging around the house.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A bell can be heard ringing outside .</scene_description>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to WILL , leaving . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Will... you're the only one, Will! - in my heart.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. STREET. OUTSIDE BURBAGE'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL emerges looking distraught . A burning brazier stands by the wall . WILL thrusts the pages into the coals . He watches for a moment as the pages catch fire .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. TAVERN. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL walks in to find the place in an uproar of celebration . A handsome young serving man -LRB- NOL -RRB- is bumping through with a tray of tankards .</scene_description>
    <character>NOL</character>
    <parenthetical>( excitedly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Mr. Henslowe!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, I heard. The theatres are open. But where is my playwright?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE finds a seat , and takes a tankard off NOL 'S tray .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Chalk it up, Nol. I'm hungry, too.</dialogue>
    <character>NOL</character>
    <dialogue>The special today is a pig's foot marinated in juniper - berry vinegar, served with a buckwheat pancake which has been</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They are interrupted by WILL who joins them . He looks distracted .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Will! Have you finished?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Yes. Nearly.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( he taps his forehead . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's all locked safe in here. We need Ralph for the Pirate King. Good morning, Master Nol. You will have a nice little part.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>NOL shouts for you , takes off his apron and flings it behind the bar . HENSLOWE jumps up and embraces WILL . The entire staff and half the customers are now crowding around , actors the lot of them . HENSLOWE bangs the table to shut them all up .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Ned Alleyn and the Admiral's Men are out on tour. I need actors. Those here who are unknown will have a chance to be known.</dialogue>
    <character>ACTOR</character>
    <dialogue>What about the money, Mr. Henslowe?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>It wo n't cost you a penny! Auditions in half - an - hour!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The din of excited chatter returns . He sweeps grandly to the tavern door ... where he meets RALPH BASHFORD , a big , burly , middle - aged actor .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ralph Bashford! I'd have a part for you but, alas, I hear you are a drunkard's drunkard.</dialogue>
    <character>RALPH</character>
    <dialogue>Never when I'm working.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. TAVERN. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL has remained behind , aghast now at his predicament . He goes to the bar .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Give me to drink mandragora.</dialogue>
    <character>BARMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Straight up, Will?</dialogue>
    <character>VOICE</character>
    <dialogue>Give my friend a beaker of your best brandy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL turns towards a figure further down the bar . It 's CHRISTOPHER MARLOWE .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Kit</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>How goes it, Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Wonderful, wonderful.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Burbage says you have a play.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I have. And chinks to show for it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>His drink arrives . WILL places a sovereign on the bar .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I insist - and a beaker for Mr. Marlowe. The BARMAN does the business.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I hear you have a new play for the Curtain.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Not new - my Doctor Faustus.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I love your early work. `` Was this the face that launched a thousand ships and burnt the topless towers of Ilium?''</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>I have a new one nearly done, and better. The Massacre at Paris.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Good title.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>And yours?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo and Ethel the Pirate's Daughter.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( beat , sighs despondently . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes, I know.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>What is the story?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Well, there's a pirate.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( confesses . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>In truth, I have not written a word.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo is... Italian. Always in and out of love.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, that's good. Until he meets</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Ethel.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Do you think?</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>The daughter of his enemy.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( thoughtfully . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>The daughter of his enemy.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>His best friend is killed in a duel by Ethel's brother or something. His name is Mercutio.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Mercutio... good name.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>NOL hurries back to WILL 'S side .</scene_description>
    <character>NOL</character>
    <dialogue>Will - they're waiting for you!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I'm coming.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He drains his glass .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Good luck with yours, Kit.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>I thought your play was for Burbage.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>This is a different one.</dialogue>
    <character>MARLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( trying to work it out . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A different one you have n't written?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL makes a helpless gesture and hurries after NOL .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. GALLERY/STAGE/AUDITORIUM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE and WILL are sitting in the gallery , listening to a YOUNG ACTOR auditioning .</scene_description>
    <character>YOUNG ACTOR</character>
    <dialogue>... Was this the face that launched a thousand ships, And burnt the topless towers of Ilium? Sweet Helen, make me immortal with a kiss!''</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE and WILL look a bit deflated . The YOUNG ACTOR leaves and is replaced by a SECOND ACTOR .</scene_description>
    <character>SECOND ACTOR</character>
    <dialogue>I would like to give you something from Faustus by Christopher Marlowe.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>How refreshing.</dialogue>
    <character>SECOND ACTOR</character>
    <dialogue>`` Was this the face that launched a thousand ships, And burnt the topless towers of Ilium?''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE and WILL let him continue a bit further , but exchange despairing looks . A succession of would - be actors offer their version of Marlowe 's lines , each as inappropriate as the other . Among them is a small URCHIN .</scene_description>
    <character>URCHIN</character>
    <dialogue>... the topless towers of Ilium? Sweet Helen, make me immortal with a -?''</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( bellows . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thank you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The URCHIN leaves , glowering furiously , and is replaced by a beanpole of a man -LRB- WASBASH -RRB- . WABASH has a bad stutter .</scene_description>
    <character>WABASH</character>
    <dialogue>`` W - w - w - w - was th - th - this th - th - the f - f - f - face...''</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( unexpectedly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Very good, Mr. Wabash. Excellent. Report to the property master.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL looks at HENSLOWE in outrage .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <parenthetical>( apologetically . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My tailor. Wants to be an actor. I have a few debts here and there. Well, that seems to be everybody. Did you see a Romeo?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I did not.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I to my work, you to yours. When can I see pages?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Tomorrow</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE leaves him .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <parenthetical>( a prayer . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>please God.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL sits brooding alone for a moment . Then he realizes he is being addressed from the stage . ANOTHER ACTOR .</scene_description>
    <character>ACTOR</character>
    <dialogue>May I begin, sir?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL looks at the stage and sees a handsome young man , with a hat shadowing his eyes .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Your name?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <dialogue>Thomas Kent. I would like to do a speech by a writer who commands the heart of every player.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL can hardly manage a nod .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>`` What light is light, if Silvia be not seen, What joy is joy, if Silvia be not by? Unless it be to think that she is by And feed upon the shadow of perfection.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>It does not take four lines of `` VALENTINE 'S '' speech to confirm for us , if confirmation be needed , that THOMAS is VIOLA . For WILL , amazement at hearing his own words soon gives away to something else . He is captivated . He has found his `` ROMEO '' .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . ) ''</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>... except I be by Silvia in the night, There is no music in the nightingale. Unless I look on Silvia in the day, There is no day for me to look upon.''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL interrupts `` him . ''</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Take off your hat.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <dialogue>My hat?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Where did you learn how to do that?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <dialogue>I.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Wait there.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <dialogue>Are you Mr. Shakespeare?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Let me see you. Take off your hat.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THOMAS begins to panic . WILL jumps down to ground level . THOMAS runs offstage , to WILL 'S bewilderment . WILL hurries after him . We go with WILL as he crosses the stage , then backstage , then into the</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. RETIRING ROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RETIRING ROOM which is crowded with actors and HENSLOWE 'S lieutenant , property manager , copier , and general factotum who is a new character , PETER .</scene_description>
    <character>ACTOR</character>
    <dialogue>What are we playing?</dialogue>
    <character>NOL</character>
    <dialogue>Where are the pages?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL enters into the middle of this .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shouts . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Where's the boy?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>NOBODY knows what he is talking about . WABASH , the stutterer , grabs Will 's hand and shakes it excitedly .</scene_description>
    <character>WABASH</character>
    <dialogue>B - b - b - b - break a l - l - l - leg!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The street door is swinging shut . WILL sees it . He fights his way through the men to get to the door .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE ROSE THEATRE. BANKSIDE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL emerges from the theatre into a street throbbing with nefarious life . Whores , cutpurses , hawkers , urchins , tract - sellers , riffraff of all kinds in an area of stews -LRB- lowdown pubs -RRB- , brothels and slums . It is some time before WILL spots THOMAS , way ahead of him in the crowded street . The chase is taking them to the riverbank .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE RIVER. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>When WILL gets to the riverbank he sees that THOMAS is in a smallish boat being rowed upriver and in midstream . The river is quite busy , and among the boats there are a number of waiting `` taxis . '' WILL jumps into the nearest one and shouts at the `` Taxi Driver '' BOATMAN .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Follow that boat!</dialogue>
    <character>BOATMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Right you are, governor!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL sits in the stern of the boat and the BOATMAN sits facing him , rowing lustily .</scene_description>
    <character>BOATMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I know your face. Are you an actor?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( oh God , here we go again . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes.</dialogue>
    <character>BOATMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, I've seen you in something. That one about a king.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Really?</dialogue>
    <character>BOATMAN</character>
    <dialogue>I had the Christopher Marlowe in my boat once.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE RIVER. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LATER . The BOATMAN is puffing . WILL is looking ahead to where THOMAS 'S boat has reached a jetty on the farther shore , a private jetty attached to a rich house on the north bank . WILL sees THOMAS jump out of his boat and run toward the house .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Do you know that house?</dialogue>
    <character>BOATMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Sir Robert De Lesseps.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL runs towards the house .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THOMAS rushes up the back stairs , removing his hat . Her hair tumbles down about her shoulders , so we will call her VIOLA again .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Her mother LADY DE LESSEPS , is talking to the NURSE . LADY DE LESSEPS Where is she ? Our guests are upon us , Lord Wessex too , bargaining for a bride . My husband will have it settled tonight . Behind her , the door opens revealing VIOLA as THOMAS to the NURSES view , but only for a moment . The door closes again as LADY DE LESSEPS turns .</scene_description>
    <character>LADY DE LESSEPS</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Tomorrow he drags me off to the country and it will be three weeks gone before we return from our estates.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A different door communicating to the next room , opens and VIOLA comes in after a lightning dress change into a robe . She curtseys to her mother .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>God save you, mother.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to NURSE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Ho water, nurse.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The NURSE looks at her , round - eyed .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. KITCHEN. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>From a cauldron on the stove , hot water is poured into two pails , by the a KITCHEN BOY under the NURSE 'S command .</scene_description>
    <character>SCULLERY MAID</character>
    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thomas Kent, sir? No sir.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>The actor</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Who asks for him?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL has come to the kitchen door with a letter .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>William Shakespeare, actor, poet, and playwright of the Rose.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The NURSE sends the SCULLERY MAID back to work .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Master Kent is... my nephew.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( giving her the letter . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I will wait.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Much god may it do you.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BATHROOM. EVENING.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>VIOLA in her bath , reads WILL 'S letter . The NURSE is adding hot water to the tub .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( delighted . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>He sees himself in me! Romeo Montague, a young man of Verona.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <parenthetical>( unimpressed . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Verona again.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( devouring the letter . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A comedy of quarreling families reconciled in the discovery of Romeo to be the very same Capulet cousin stolen from the cradle and fostered to manhood by his Montague mother that was robbed of her own child by the Pirate King!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL waits hopefully . The kitchen door opens and a SERVANT flings a bucket of dirty water in the general direction of the gutter . WILL hops nimbly aside and escapes a soaking .</scene_description>
    <character>SERVANT</character>
    <dialogue>Be off!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The NURSE is helping VIOLA into her party dress .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Your mother, and your father</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( gaily . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>From tomorrow, away in the country for three weeks! Is Master Shakespeare not handsome?</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>He looks well enough for a mountebank.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, Nurse! He would give Thomas Kent the life of Viola De Lesseps's dreaming.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <parenthetical>( firmly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My lady, this play will end badly. I will tell.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( twice as firmly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You will not tell. As you love me and as I love you, you will bind my breast and buy me a boy's wig!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL spots a gaggle of MUSICIANS approaching , carrying instruments . WILL recognizes them .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Master Plum! What business here?</dialogue>
    <character>MUSICIAN</character>
    <dialogue>A five shilling business, Will. We play for the dancing.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The sound of hooves gives hardly any warning as a GALLOPING HORSEMAN thunders through the MUSICIANS who have to leap out of the way . It is WESSEX arriving at the house , with his usual good manners . Will watches WESSEX skid to a halt and enter the house .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. BANQUETING ROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL has got in with the MUSICIANS . Competently enough he strums along with them on the bandstand . Two dozen guests are enough to crowd the space for dancing . WILL glances around , looking for THOMAS KENT . He stops a passing SERVANT , helping himself to a snack off the man 's tray .</scene_description>
    <character>SERVANT</character>
    <dialogue>Musicians do n't eat, Sir Robert's orders.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I seek Master Thomas Kent.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>It means nothing to the SERVANT who moves on . ANGLE ON WESSEX and SIR ROBERT .</scene_description>
    <character>SIR ROBERT</character>
    <dialogue>She is a beauty, my lord, as would take a king to church for a dowry of a nutmeg.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>My plantations in Virginia are not mortgaged for a nutmeg. I have an ancient name that will bring you preferment when your grandson is a Wessex. Is she fertile?</dialogue>
    <character>SIR ROBERT</character>
    <dialogue>She will breed. If she do not, send her back.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>Is she obedient?</dialogue>
    <character>SIR ROBERT</character>
    <dialogue>As any mule in Christendom. But if you are the man to rider her, their are rubies in the saddlebag.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>I like her.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ANGLE on WILL - watching the dancing . Then he sees VIOLA in the crowd . He turns to blood . Love at first sight , no doubt about it . VIOLA has not seen him . She is doing a daughter 's duty among her parents ' friends . The guests form up to begin a changing - partners dance -LRB- the very same one you get in every ROMEO and JULIET -RRB- .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to Musician . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>By all the stars in heaven, who is she?</dialogue>
    <character>MUSICIAN</character>
    <dialogue>Viola de Lesseps. Dream on, Will.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL leaves the bandstand and is moving trancelike to keep her in view between the dancers and onlookers . VIOLA moves through patterns of the dance until ... as night follows day , she finds WILL opposite her . He has insinuated himself into the dance . VIOLA gasps .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Master Shakespeare</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL reacts , surprised by her reaction . The dance separates them . VIOLA finds herself opposite WESSEX .</scene_description>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>My lady Viola.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>My lord.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>I have spoken with your father.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>So my lord? I speak with him every day.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WESSEX scowls . The dance separates them . VIOLA finds herself opposite WILL again . WILL stares at her entranced .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Good sir...?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL has lost his tongue .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I heard you are a poet.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL nods in his trance and she smiles at him .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But a poet of no words?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL tries to speak but the silver tongue wo n't work . He is dumb with adoration . Suddenly WESSEX takes him affably by the elbow and leads him into an alcove .</scene_description>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <parenthetical>( smiling evilly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>`` Poet?''</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( coming round form the anaesthetic and not noticing the danger . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I was a poet till now, but I have seen beauty that puts my poems at one with the talking ravens at the Tower.</dialogue>
