    "summary":"In 1593 London, William Shakespeare is a sometime player in the Lord Chamberlain's Men and playwright for Philip Henslowe, owner of The Rose Theatre. Suffering from writer's block with a new comedy, Romeo and Ethel, the Pirate's Daughter, Shakespeare attempts to seduce Rosaline, mistress of Richard Burbage, owner of the rival Curtain Theatre, and to convince Burbage to buy the play from Henslowe. Shakespeare receives advice from rival playwright Christopher Marlowe, but is despondent to learn Rosaline is sleeping with Master of the Revels Edmund Tilney. The desperate Henslowe, in debt to ruthless moneylender Fennyman, begins auditions anyway. Viola de Lesseps, daughter of a wealthy merchant, who has seen Shakespeare's plays at court, disguises herself as a man named Thomas Kent to audition. "He" gains Shakespeare's interest with a speech from Two Gentlemen of Verona, but runs away when Shakespeare questions her. He pursues Kent to Viola's house and leaves a note with her nurse, asking Kent to begin rehearsals at the Rose. Shakespeare sneaks into a ball at the house, where Viola's parents arrange her betrothal to impoverished aristocrat Lord Wessex. Dancing with Viola, Shakespeare is struck speechless and ejected by Wessex, who threatens to kill him, leading Shakespeare to say that he is Christopher Marlowe. He finds Viola on her balcony, where they confess their mutual attraction before he is discovered by her nurse and flees. Inspired by Viola, Shakespeare quickly transforms the play into what will become Romeo and Juliet. Rehearsals begin, with "Thomas Kent" as Romeo, the leading tragedian Ned Alleyn as Mercutio, and the stagestruck Fennyman in a small role. Shakespeare discovers Viola's true identity, and they begin a secret affair. Viola is summoned to court to receive approval for her proposed marriage to Wessex. Shakespeare accompanies her, disguised as her female cousin, and persuades Wessex to wager £50 that a play can capture the true nature of love, the amount Shakespeare requires to buy a share in the Chamberlain's Men. Queen Elizabeth I declares that she will judge the matter. Burbage learns Shakespeare has seduced Rosaline and cheated him out of payment for the play, and starts a brawl at the Rose with his company. The Rose players repel Burbage and his men and celebrate at the pub, where a drunken Henslowe lets slip to Viola that Shakespeare is married, albeit separated from his wife. News arrives that Marlowe has been murdered, and a guilt-ridden Shakespeare assumes Wessex had Marlowe killed, believing him to be Viola's lover. Viola believes Shakespeare has been murdered but he appears at her church, terrifying Wessex who believes he is a ghost. Viola confesses her love for Shakespeare, but both recognize she cannot escape her duty to marry Wessex. John Webster, an unpleasant boy who hangs around the theatre, spies on Shakespeare and Viola making love and informs Tilney, who closes the Rose for breaking the ban on women actors. Viola's identity is exposed, leaving them without a stage or lead actor, until Burbage offers his theatre and the heartbroken Shakespeare takes the role of Romeo. Following her wedding, Viola learns the play will be performed that day, and runs away to the Curtain. She overhears that the boy playing Juliet cannot perform, his voice having broken, and Henslowe asks her to replace him. She plays Juliet to Shakespeare's Romeo to an enthralled audience. Tilney arrives to arrest everyone for indecency due to Viola's presence, but the Queen reveals herself in attendance and restrains him, instead asserting that Kent's resemblance to a woman is “remarkable”. Powerless to end a lawful marriage, she orders Kent to "fetch" Viola to sail with Wessex to the Colony of Virginia.     <scene_description>The hand grabs Mike around the ankle! Mike turns, raising his gun. Too late. A DEAD UNIFORMED POLICEMAN, the skin on half its face STRIPPED DOWN TO BONE, RIPS A HOLE IN HIS LEG with its teeth! Mike SCREAMS, staggers into a wall, and drops to a seated position on the floor. Riley and Charlie spin around at the sound of his cry. Cholo, closest to Mike, pulls his crossbow and fires an arrow through the Zombie's head.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Fuckin' rookies.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo tucks away the crossbow, grabs a box of Cohibas off a counter, and runs outside with Foxy. Riley goes to Mike.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(Kneeling) It's alright, son. You're gonna be alright.</dialogue>
    <character>MIKE</character>
    <dialogue>No. I'm dead. You get bit by one f those things and you become what they are.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley wraps a strong arm around Mike and lifts him. Mike quickly plants the barrel of his .45 under his chin and... BLOWS HIS OWN BRAINS OUT! Riley, stunned, lets the corpse slide to the floor. He looks into the rookie's open eyes, devastated.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. MAIN STREET - UNIONTOWN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE WHITE MOVING VAN, THE T-BIRD, AND THE JEEP roll out of town in a convoy. Trailing them, THREE SADISTIC GUERILLAS on MOTORCYCLES ROAR past, firing... ...a HAIL OF BULLETS at A DEAD FAMILY on the sidewalk. The MOTHER FALLS. Not shot. It has been GRABBED and SHOVED down to the ground by... ...BIG DADDY! Who GRABS the little GIRL next, thrusting her roughly behind the protection of a wrecked car. The FATHER is last. Big Daddy grabs it from behind, by its hair, just as... ...ROUNDS from an UZI DRILL A DOTTED-LINE across the Father's neck. Big Daddy is unhurt, but spattered with BLOOD. Not red, greenish-black. The blood of the dead. here's a RIPPING SOUND as the Father's NECK is PULLED APART by the weight of its limp body. The body DROPS to the street. The HEAD remains suspended in Big Daddy's hand. His face contorts. His mouth opens and closes, trying to utter sounds. Big Daddy drops the head, looking down at its befuddled eyes with sympathy. After a moment, the sympathy is joined by rage. Big Daddy lifts his right foot and brings it STOMPING DOWN on the disembodied head, CRUSHING ITS SKULL. The convoy ROARS off, leaving a cloud of exhaust. Big Daddy sees Harry's downed motorcycle lying in the street. The butt of an AUTOMATIC RIFLE protrudes from a saddlebag. Big Daddy goes over. Pulls out the rifle. Tests the weight of it in his hand. Curls his finger in through the guard and pulls the trigger. BLAM! A bullet ricochets off a brick wall. Big Daddy is startled at first. Then, he relaxes, realizing the rifle's power. With surprising dexterity, he slings the weapon's strap over his head and across his chest, patting the strap as if comforted by it. Turning, he looks toward... ...THE DISTANT GLOW OF A SKYSCRAPER that can be seen ON THE HORIZON. That's the direction the convoy is headed. That's where the bad men came from. That's where he wants to go. REVERSE ANGLE: With the city in the distance, Big Daddy starts walking. NUMBER NINE falls into step beside him. Soon there are MORE. None of them knows where they are going. Or why. All that seems to matter is that they have a leader.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - PRE-DAWN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>DEAD RECKONING, emitting tendrils of HOT STEAM from twenty steel nostrils, stands parked in a corner of a fenced-in outdoor yard. (We don't see how big the yard is. Yet.) A SEARCHLIGHT sweeps the darkness as GUERILLAS unload the supplies they took from Uniontown and carry them toward... ...a set of RUSTY STEEL DOORS, above which is a FADED SIGN that reads "SUBWAY (TO CITY)". In the bustle of activity, HARRY, the biker who was attacked in town, perspires as he helps unload. He looks ill. RILEY walks past, handing out bottles of beer to the men.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Harry. Beer?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Harry doesn't answer.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Harry?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Harry SPINS! GROWLS! LUNGES at Riley like a beast! Riley has no time to reach for his gun. The Harry-Thing is strangling him. SMASHING the neck of a beer bottle on the snout of Dead Reckoning, Riley JAMS THE JAGGED GLASS into the Harry-Thing's forehead. Its body drops to the ground.</scene_description>
    <character>PRETTY BOY</character>
    <dialogue>Got knocked off his bike in town. Must have been bit.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley looks down at the body with a mixture anger and regret.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SUBWAY TUNNEL - DAWN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A mile-long subway tunnel extends into BLACKNESS. A wide PLATFORM runs the length of the tracks, at the head of which A DERELICT TRAIN is parked. A CARGO CARRIER pulls out, driving along the platform, its flatbed piled with supplies, while ANOTHER CARRIER is being loaded with boxes of food, pharmaceuticals, ammunition, and... TWO BODY BAGS.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Shit happens, Riley.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(Blaming himself) Only if you let it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The cargo carrier that was first to pull out drives into the tunnel. CEILING LIGHTS spaced far apart STUTTER on and off. Two guerillas, ANCHOR and MOUSE, who looks like a mouse, ride on the open flatbed with the cargo. The tunnel is filled with looming steel shapes that cast menacing shadows. Mouse shifts nervously. Suddenly... ...PLINK! SOMETHING WET FALLS ON HIS FACE! He JUMPS. Recovers. Wipes his cheek with his sleeve.</scene_description>
    <character>MOUSE</character>
    <dialogue>I hate going under the fuckin' river.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He takes out a joint. Lights up. The match FLARES. SPLAT! Mouse and the match are soaked by WATER dripping from above.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE CITY - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RIVERS flank a TRIANGLE OF LAND where A CITY glows in the sunrise. Once proud and prosperous, its buildings now seem like tombstones. SEVEN BARRICADED BRIDGES span the rivers.</scene_description>
    <character>ANNOUNCER (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Protected on three sides by mighty rivers, the city stands as a monument</dialogue>
    <dialogue>to man's ingenuity. At the center of it all is Fiddler's Green.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SUBWAY TUNNEL - DAWN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A TV MONITOR broadcasts views of A KITCHEN, A PLUSH LIVING ROOM, A DEN with a VIDEO FIREPLACE.</scene_description>
    <character>ANNOUNCER (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Luxury living in the grand old style. Dine at one of three restaurants. Look for that perfect gift in our fabulous shopping mall.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>he monitor shows a huge ATRIUM with shops and restaurants.</scene_description>
    <character>GUERILLA (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>They make it sound nice.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>It is nice.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Holding his case of Dom Perignon and his box of Cohibas, CHOLO looks with FOXY at a monitor mounted to a white-tiled subway station wall. Down the tunnel behind them, the other GUERILLAS unload supplies from CARGO CARRIERS parked on the platform. A sign reads, "GOLDEN TRIANGLE/FIDDLER'S GREEN". M f E W</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(Approaching) Cholo.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Foxy moves away, leaving Riley and Cholo alone.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Two people dead. That kid, Mike. He should be here with us right now.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I didn't kill him. He got bit and he killed himself. Same thing I woulda done. And you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley lunges at Cholo, takes hold of his shirt, and SLAMS him against the wall.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>The fuck are you turning into, man?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>e take money to do nasty shit. Shit that nobody else is dumb enough to do. We go in knowing the risks. The kid did too. His number came up, that's all.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>We take the risk to bring in things people need. Not to make a few extra bucks selling liquor. You used to know that.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Everybody makes their own way. everybody makes their own fucking way!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo shrugs out of Riley's grasp. Behind them, the guerillas continue to unload cargo.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>y daddy...he picked fruit, penny- a-piece. He never went for anything, so he never had anything. I'm gonna have a place, Riley. My own place! And now I got enough money to buy my way in.</dialogue>
    <character>ANNOUNCER (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Isn't it time? Isn't it your time? For Fiddler's Green.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo looks up at the TV monitor. Riley follows his gaze, seeing well-dressed PEOPLE sipping cocktails in a club room.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You're dreaming, Cholo. They'd never let me in. They'll never let you in. We're the wrong kind.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The image on the TV MONITOR changes to an overhead view of the city and its rivers. Animation draws a RED LINE along the base of the "golden triangle", a zone known as "THE THROAT".</scene_description>
    <character>ANNOUNCER (O.S.</character>
    <dialogue>Bask in the security of a city protected not only by its natural boundaries, but by hand-picked members of its own private militia.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE CITY - "THE THROAT" - DAWN</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In live action, not on the monitor, WEARY TROOPS, sloppily uniformed, guard four rows of electrified, barbed-wire FENCING. DEAD THINGS cluster by the DOZENS outside the barricades. CORPSES hang all along the stretch, suspended on the barbs.</scene_description>
    <character>MILITARY WOMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Stench! Ten o-clock!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A WALKER lumbers in and touches the fencing. SPARKS FLY! The Thing's flesh is literally COOKED! BOILS develop, POPPING OPEN, emitting SMOKE. Still the Thing remains animated.</scene_description>
    <character>MILITARY MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Take its fuckin' face off.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>UDDA-BUDDA-BUDDA! The Military Woman FIRES. The Thing is decimated. Its body hangs, welded to the SPARKING barbs.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. FIDDLER'S GREEN CENTRAL MALL - MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO approaches a CHECKPOINT manned by TWO SECURITY GUARDS. Setting down the champagne and Cohibas, he unstraps his weapons and hands them over.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>DeMora. Supply unit</dialogue>
    <character>SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>What's in them boxes?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Essential supplies. For the man upstairs.</dialogue>
    <dialogue>l</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Guard takes Cholo's weapons and returns a claim check. CHOLO collects his boxes and steps onto an escalator that carries him up into an ENORMOUS ATRIUM. The "mall" we saw on TV. SUNLIGHT splashes through glass walls onto box-planted trees. Caged birds CHIRP seemingly in tune with the Chopin that lilts over a sound system. SHOPPERS, expensively over- dressed, stroll past stores. OTHER RESIDENTS lunch at "outdoor" cafes. Cholo pulls out a kerchief and wipes the smudges off his face, trying to make himself presentable.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. "GOLDEN TRIANGLE" - MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>FIDDLER'S GREEN, a heavily protected HIGH-RISE in the center of the city, dominates the skyline. It's where the Fat Cats live, protected from urban decay. The building is surrounded by unoccupied high-rises that define "the golden triangle", a clean section in the center of the city. No ugliness in view. RILEY and CHARLIE cross a manicured plaza to a CHECKPOINT manned by TWO SECURITY GUARDS. Riley hands over his ID.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Quittin' time, Deke.</dialogue>
    <character>SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>(Holding up the ID) You're gonna need this.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(Walking on) Nope. When I said quittin' time, I meant quittin'</dialogue>
    <dialogue>time.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. "GHETTO" - MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY and CHARLIE walk down a street into the city's "ghetto" zone, which is lined with taverns, gambling clubs, strip joints, like a boom town from Alaskan gold-rush days. BUYERS and SELLERS lurk in the shadows, copulating, dealing drugs. Riley is welcomed by nearly everyone he passes, greeting them in return with a smile and a nod, handing some bills to a FATHER with a YOUNG SON, patting an OLD MAN on the back.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Wanna get a drink, Riley? Just look at me, you can tell I could use a drink.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Later. Gotta see a man about a car.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Charlie follows Riley, who strides into... ...an alley, surprised to find a cadre of rough-looking REVOLUTIONARIES, led by MULLIGAN, a defiant man who stands on a soapbox. A small audience is gathered in front of him. He takes a swig from a bottle of whiskey.</scene_description>
    <character>MULLIGAN</character>
    <dialogue>(Irish accent) How long are you gonna let him push you around? If</dialogue>
    <dialogue>there was enough of us...if you all would join up with us...we could pull him down off his throne!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Some of the people in the audience nervously shift their eyes to the FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE ten blocks away.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You can't fix a place like this, Mulligan. You just have to get out</dialogue>
    <dialogue>of it.</dialogue>
    <character>MULLIGAN</character>
    <dialogue>We've got the firepower, Riley. If you and your friends would come in with us, we'd be unstoppable.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Mulligan holds out his bottle to Riley, who passes it to Charlie, who takes a swig.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Everyone's stoppable.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>We hear the sound of a boy coughing. Mulligan's son BRIAN stands behind him, looking feverish.</scene_description>
    <character>MULLIGAN</character>
    <dialogue>You alright, son?</dialogue>
    <character>BRIAN</character>
    <dialogue>I'm fine, dad.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>As Riley starts past, he stops, pulls something from his pocket, and presses it into Mulligan's palm.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Antibiotics. For your boy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Mulligan looks down with gratitude at a bottle his hand. When he looks up again, Riley is gone.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. GARAGE - MORNING</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Turning a corner, RILEY and CHARLIE stop in front of a rundown GARAGE with a tarp hanging down instead of a door. Riley pulls it aside and looks in. A HOBO lies asleep on a grease-stained floor, curled under some old newspapers.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Where's the car?</dialogue>
    <character>HOBO</character>
    <dialogue>(Waking) What car?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>My new car. I paid for it. I was</dialogue>
    <dialogue>here yesterday. There were two guys getting it ready for me.</dialogue>
    <character>HOBO</character>
    <dialogue>There was nobody here this morning.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Sonofabitch!</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What happened, Riley. Didja get fucked?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley stands there, grim-faced.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(A whisper) Come on.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PENTHOUSE CORRIDOR - FIDDLER'S GREEN - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ING! An elevator door opens. CHOLO, carrying the champagne and Cohibas, steps out, walks to "PENTHOUSE NUMBER ONE", and rings the bell. An instant after he pushes the button... ...the door is JERKED OPEN by TYLER KNIPP, 50-something, an African American man in a white butler's jacket. Frightened, he's wielding a SCISSORS, poised to strike.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>(Lowering the scissors) Oh, Mister DeMora. Mister Kaufman ain't home and there's some shit goin' down. No lie. I heard...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A SCREAM RINGS OUT down the corridor!</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>I heard that!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ANOTHER SCREAM.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, man. Mister K. sure gonna be upset about this.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo drops his boxes and moves down the corridor.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>I called Security. They should be here...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo reaches the door to PENTHOUSE NUMBER TWO. It's locked. ANOTHER SCREAM from inside. He FLINGS himself at the door. The LATCH SPLINTERS out of the frame. The door BURSTS open...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PENTHOUSE NUMBER-TWO - FIDDLER'S GREEN - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>...and CHOLO enters a dark foyer. The only light comes from another room somewhere inside. A soft, rhythmic SQUEAK, like a child's swing moving back and forth, ECHOES through the apartment. It's an eerie, incongruous sound. On guard, eyes straining, Cholo moves inside. The squeak gets louder, the light brighter as he turns a corner and sees... ...a MIDDLE-AGED MAN, HANGING DEAD from a HOMEMADE NOOSE suspended from a light fixture in the kitchen! THE BODY SWAYS slowly, the harsh glare making the man's face even whiter than it is. A toppled chair lies on the floor at his feet. Cholo stands transfixed for an instant. And in that instant... ...HE IS GRABBED FROM BEHIND! He whirls, ready to kill, but finds only a MIDDLE-AGED WOMAN, 60-something, wearing a tailored suit and expensive jewelry, her perfectness blemished only by her hysteria.</scene_description>
    <character>WOMAN</character>
    <dialogue>My Johnny, he killed himself, he killed himself. My Johnny! My Johnny!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo shakes her, hard.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Keep it together, lady.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Behind them, in the kitchen, unseen, a dazed YOUNG MAN, walks up to the hanging corpse. He rights the toppled chair and steps on it, lifting a paring to knife cut through the noose.</scene_description>
    <character>YOUNG MAN</character>
    <dialogue>(Softly, to himself) Dad. Oh, Dad.</dialogue>
    <character>WOMAN</character>
    <dialogue>(To Cholo) Se-Security. Are you Security?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No, I...</dialogue>
    <character>WOMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Then, for God's sake, who ARE YOU?!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She resumes her SCREAMING. In the kitchen, the Young Man is slicing through the rope when his DEAD FATHER'S EYES POP OPEN! The Young Man is too busy with the rope to notice. THE HANGED MAN'S EYES BLINK. Once. Twice. Three times. Its body TWITCHES. And then... ...the Hanged Man turns, making a move on the Young Man. The motion increases the strain on the light fixture, which pulls away, SPARKING, from the ceiling and CRASHES TO THE FLOOR, along with the Hanged Man and his son. The entire apartment is PLUNGED INTO DARKNESS. The woman stops her screaming. Almost as soon as she does, a SNARL can be heard from the kitchen, followed by another SCREAM, this one coming from the Young Man. Cholo rushes to a nearby fireplace and grabs a POKER and a MATCHLIGHT, which looks like a pistol, but shoots FIRE from its tip. He approaches the kitchen, using the FLAME to light his way. In the FLICKERING GLOW, he sees... ...the Young Man lying on the floor. CHUNKS have been bitten out of his neck and wrist. The body is CONVULSING in the last moments of life. THE HANGED MAN IS NOWHERE TO BE SEEN. Cholo stands over the Young Man and stabs him in the head with the poker, jabbing the point all the way through. The woman SCREAMS again from the kitchen doorway.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Shut up! I gotta hear. Where'd he go? Where'd the other guy go?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Silence. Cholo pulls the poker out of the Young Man's head. SHUFFLING sounds. He follows them to the other end of the kitchen, probing the darkness with his matchlight. The sounds are LOUDER here. Cholo lifts the poker, ready to strike. Just as he does... ...the back door of the apartment BURSTS OPEN and a SECURITY GUARD lunges into the kitchen, rifle in hand.</scene_description>
    <character>SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>(To Cholo) Drop it!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo drops the poker and holds up his hands.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Hey, no problem.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>TWO MORE SECURITY GUARDS come through the apartment's front door and rush into the kitchen.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No problem, no problem! But there is a problem. There's a dead guy</dialogue>
    <dialogue>walkin' around in here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE HANGED MAN appears without warning, attacking one of the guards who just entered, BITING OFF half his left CHEEK, including the EYE. Before his partner can raise his gun, THE WOMAN GRABS IT FROM HIM! Aims at the Hanged Man. YOU SELFISH BASTARD! YOU LEFT ME ALONE HERE! She fumbles with the weapon, not knowing how to make it work. The bitten security guard starts to lose all strength in his legs. The Dead Thing holds him up, as if waltzing with him, BITING HIM again and again. Cholo takes the gun from the woman and shoots the Hanged Man.</scene_description>
    <character>BITTEN SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>I need help. I need help!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo kills the bitten security guard, too.</scene_description>
    <character>SURVIVING SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>You...FUCK!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo turns the gun on the surviving security guard.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>You wanna talk about this? I did what I had to do. I only did what I had to do!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. "THE ARENA" - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY and CHARLIE step into the CELLAR of an old BROWNSTONE. Dirt floor. Stone walls. The place is filled with smoke and BUZZING with FLIES. As Riley and Charley turn their guns over to TWO BIG BRUISERS inside, a TOUT named ROACH sidles over.</scene_description>
    <character>TOUT</character>
    <dialogue>(Eyeing the weapons) Supply run last night, uh? Bet you have some money in your pocket. I can show you how to turn that money into more money.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Roach. Where's Chihuahua?</dialogue>
    <character>TOUT</character>
    <dialogue>Maybe I can find him for you. Come on in.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley is already in. He has pushed past the Tout and is striding into a fog where GAMBLERS are rushing to place bets with heavily-armed BOOKIES. We're reminded of a cock-fighting joint in a Pancho Villa movie.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Lot of action tonight.</dialogue>
    <character>TOUT</character>
    <dialogue>Gotta new kind of game.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley strides toward a cluster of BETTORS. A very tall man stands among them, wearing a Texas Stetson that sticks up high above all other heads, its peacock feathers poking even higher out of a snake-skin hat band. Riley grabs him and spins him around. he man's feet are off the ground. Way off the ground. Far from tall, he's a little person, who has been standing on a platform, wearing a purple satin pimp-suit. He's a Latino, who looks like a Chihuahua. And that's his name. CHIHUAHUA.</scene_description>
    <character>CHIHUAHUA</character>
    <dialogue>Put me down! Put me down!</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>What happened to my fucking car?</dialogue>
    <character>CHIHUAHUA</character>
    <dialogue>What? They're fixing it up.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I went over to the garage. Your guys aren't there. The car's not there. My dinero's not there.</dialogue>
    <character>CHIHUAHUA</character>
    <dialogue>Hey, this is not me. I did not do this to you. I am your friend. Put me down. Come on. I find out what went wrong.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Just get me the car, or they'll carry you out of here inside that fucking hat.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BACKSTAGE - "THE ARENA" - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In a dark CATACOMB, DEAD MEN are chained to the walls. WHAM! A POLE shoots out. A NOOSE on the end encircles the neck of a captive Dead Man and is cinched tight. TWO MEN hold the pole while A THIRD sprays RED PAINT on the Thing's face. ANOTHER DEAD THING is dragged in and sprayed with BLACK PAINT.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BACK OFFICE - "THE ARENA" - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Cursing in Spanish, CHIHUAHUA pulls a GLOCK out of a filing cabinet and jams a magazine up its butt.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. CENTER RING - "THE ARENA" - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY and CHARLIE drift into a large room that's packed with BETTORS hooting and hollering like football fans. They're all jammed onto tiered wooden viewing stands arranged around an IRON-MESH STRUCTURE that looks like a lion-tamer's cage. Gates open. THE PAINTED WALKERS are thrust inside the cage. Their nooses are released. The gates are locked behind them. EAD RED, alarmed by the color of DEAD BLACK'S face, reaches out and gently touches the paint. Its fingers come away with blackened tips. lack follows suit, staining its fingers red. Black licks its hand, spitting when it identifies not blood, but something distasteful. BOOKIES drift among the spectators, taking bets with fists full of cash.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What are they betting on, Riley?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Red or Black. Who's gonna win the fight.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What fight? Stenches don't fight.</dialogue>
    <character>TOUT (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>They do when there's food.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The TOUT sidles over.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>What's on the menu today? Cat or dog?</dialogue>
    <character>TOUT</character>
    <dialogue>I told you. Today it's something new.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CLANG! Another gate opens in the cage. A hush falls as everyone awaits what will come. Including the Dead Men, who gaze with anticipation at the opening. What comes is... ..A WOMAN! Alive, badly bruised, her dress in tatters. Despite tarnish, she still looks sexy. Last night she was a hooker known as SLACK. Now she's meat in a lion cage.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Jesus fucking Christ.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The gate SLAMS shut. The Dead Things walk toward the woman. Riley rushes off. Charlie follows. lack backs up, hits the wall of the cage and, terrified, starts to circle its iron perimeter. The Dead Men flank her. Black is the first to touch her. The crowd HOWLS. lack's terror turns to determination. She punches Black three times in the face. The Thing recoils as she glides out of its grasp. RILEY and CHARLIE reach the BRUISERS who took their weapons.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Give us our guns.</dialogue>
    <character>BRUISER</character>
    <dialogue>(Handing over the weapons) You leavin'?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley cocks his M-16.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>In a little while.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>In the ring, BLACK reaches for SLACK again. With one lightning-fast move, she kicks it in the chest, sending it flying into Red's arms. Red shoves Black aside. Black makes another try for the woman. Red grabs its rival. This time Black hangs on to Red's shirt. The two twirl around in a staggering lampoon of a wrestling match. Slack rushes to the side of the cage and starts to climb. She's agile. Strong. But she almost falls as the cage SHAKES with the force of... ...Red SLAMMING Black against the mesh. On their way back through the arena, RILEY and CHARLEY push through the crowd, trying to reach the center ring. A GOON steps in front of them.</scene_description>
    <character>GOON</character>
    <dialogue>No guns in here!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley gives him a rifle butt in the face and moves on. lack continues to climb the cage, almost out of reach, but Black grabs one of her ankles, pulling her down and slamming her to the ground. Black hunkers, drooling, over Slack. As it is about to bite, RAT-A-TAT! A short burst from Riley's M-16 shatters Black's collarbone. Cheekbone. Skull. The Thing drops. Red lunges for Slack. Riley kills it with another short BURST. he crowd PANICS, stampeding toward the exit. Suddenly MORE BULLETS FLY, this time from a GLOCK, FIRED by... ...CHIHUAHUA, who, in a rage, is pushing through the LEGS of the fleeing crowd. He makes it to a clear spot and draws a steady bead on a target...Charlie. Chihuahua pulls his trigger. Riley beats him by an instant, FIRING the M-16. Just as Chihuahua's gun GOES OFF...a LINE of BULLET HOLES PERFORATES the little man's belly. The round from his Glock misses Charlie completely. Riley runs to the cage, where Slack stands, trembling, just on the other side of the bars.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You okay?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She nods gratefully. Chihuahua is still on his feet. And now he is really pissed. Not because of the holes in his gut, but because...</scene_description>
    <character>CHIHUAHUA</character>
    <dialogue>My suit! You fucked up my new suit!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley turns to Chihuahua, but doesn't have time to lift the M-16 before...BLAM! The little man FIRES at him. Slack delivers a powerful KICK into the flexible fencing, sending Riley sprawling to the ground and saving him from... ...Chihuahua's round, which misses Riley...but HITS SLACK! Spun around by the impact, she falls face down. Chihuahua continues to FIRE. Riley Marine-crawls as bullets PUNCH around him, SPARKING off the cage. Chihuahua keeps coming, keeps FIRING, until... ...A SINGLE SHOT from Charlie's .45 shatters his skull. He drops like a broken pinata. Riley looks up, seeing TWO OTHER MEN with guns. Chihuahua's GOONS. For a moment it seems as if a major shooting match is going to break out. But before it does...</scene_description>
    <character>POLICEMAN (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Hold it!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>..FOUR POLICEMEN burst in. The Goons lower their weapons. Riley runs back to the cage, BLASTS the lock on the nearest gate, and rushes inside. Slack's body is lying on the floor. He suspects she's dead. When her BODY MOVES, he suspects worse. He plants the barrel of his M-16 against her temple.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>I'm alright, I'M ALRIGHT!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slack uses her left arm to push herself up to a sitting position. Her right arm is BLEEDING, up near the shoulder.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Fucker got my right arm. I'm a lefty.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They look into each other's eyes.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Seen you around.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Seen you around.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A POLICEMAN steps over.</scene_description>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>The hell happened here?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Somebody shot the little fat man.</dialogue>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah, I see that. You're under arrest.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BOARD ROOM - FIDDLER'S GREEN - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A UNIFORMED GUARD leaves CHOLO in a PRISTINE WHITE conference room with glass walls overlooking the rotting CITY far below. Cholo sets the case of champagne and the box of Cohibas on a conference table. A SMAN stands in SILHOUETTE at the windows.</scene_description>
    <character>SILHOUETTED MAN</character>
    <dialogue>How was Uniontown?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Dead.</dialogue>
    <character>SILHOUETTED MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Death intrudes on us even in the Green, I'm afraid. I heard about what happened with my neighbors.</dialogue>
    <dialogue>I'm grateful for your help.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>brought you back some presents.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo opens the case of champagne. He pulls a bottle out, untwists the wire, and uses his strong thumbs to pop the cork. FOAM runs.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>You probably want a glass, don't you? Sure, a high-toned man likes to drink out of a glass.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo grabs a highball glass from a cupboard, pours champagne into it, and brings it, overflowing, to the Silhouetted Man.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I got something else, too.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo tears open the box of Cohibas. He picks up two cigars, bites off the tips, puts one in his mouth, then, walking back to the Silhouetted Man, puts the other in his mouth, lighting them both with a wooden match that he strikes on his jeans. F</scene_description>
    <character>SILHOUETTED MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No, thank you! Twenty grand. That's what I got comin' for last night. I never bothered to pick it up.</dialogue>
    <character>SILHOUETTED MAN</character>
    <dialogue>You didn't?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Nope. I left it in the bank. Your bank. With all my other dough. From all those other nights. I got enough now to buy me a place.</dialogue>
    <character>SILHOUETTED MAN</character>
    <dialogue>You mean here? In the Green?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Silhouetted Man steps away from the window. Expensively dressed, in his early 60s, he is PAUL KAUFMAN. He sets down the highball glass Cholo gave him, gets out a proper champagne flute, and fills it from the bottle, smiling politely at Cholo.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>I'm sorry, Mister DeMora, but there's a very long waiting list.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>How long?</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>This is an extremely desirable location. Space is limited.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>You mean restricted.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Well, I do have a board of directors, a membership committee that has to approve...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A wave of incomparable sadness sweeps over Cholo's face.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I guess it takes more than money to become a "member".</dialogue>
    <scene_description>( Y</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Take my advice. Withdraw your funds from the bank and spend them somewhere else.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>(Quietly) Don't do this to me. Don't do this to me.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>I'm sorry, but...</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No, no, no. Three years! Three years I been cleaning up after you, taking out your garbage, and you tell me I'm not good enough? You're the one who's no good. You are no fucking good. And you are gonna let me in. You know why? Because I know what goes on around here. How many of your fucking "members" know what's in that garbage I take out for you?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo lunges at Kaufman, grabs him by the collar. OU'LL LET ME IN OR I'LL... Cholo feels the barrel of a .45 against his waist. Kaufman, who has drawn the pistol from his jacket, is still smiling.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Maybe we should talk about this when you're less excited.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman presses a button under the table. THREE SECURITY GUARDS rush in, GRAB Cholo, and drag him away. Kaufman stops one of the guards at the door.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Softly) I won't be needing this man any more.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. STAIRWELL - FIDDLER'S GREEN - DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HE SECURITY GUARDS lead CHOLO down the stairs. Cholo WHIRLS like a Ninja. He SLUGS one guard, kicks another in the groin, the third in the face, and escapes through a fire door.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT. JAIL - AFTERNOON</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY RIPS off part of his shirt-sleeve and starts to bandage the wound on SLACK'S arm. They are in a jail cell that has brick walls and a small barred window facing a dark alley. CHARLIE, stripped of all his guns, stares outside longingly.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(To Slack) Why you? In that arena. Why did the little fat man throw you in with those things?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>It wasn't the little man. It was the big man. The man upstairs. He's got his fingers in everything down here. If you can drink it, shoot it up, fuck it, or gamble on it, it belongs to him. He's just seein' that we get a few cheap kicks so we don't go thinkin' too hard about why he's eating steak and the rest of us are lucky to get the bones.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Same question. Why you?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>They found out I was working with Mulligan and his people. Tired of eatin' off Cbones.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What can you do? Every place is the same.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Places with people. I'm gonna find me a place where there ain't no people. North. Canada.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Wherever you're going, take me with you.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>He won't. Riley likes to be alone. He might take me. Cuzz havin' me around is pretty much the same as bein' alone. (Glancing at Riley) can make myself useful. And I an shoot.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>I can shoot. And I can be pretty</dialogue>
    <dialogue>fucking useful. I had training. I was gonna join the Army. Up the Green. Till somebody figured I'd be a better hooker than a soldier.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I don't need to hear your story. Everybody's got a story, and I'm tired of hearin' them all!</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>What's your story, Riley?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>They look at each other, clearly attracted.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I said everybody has a story. That was wrong. I don't have one. Daddy was a preacher. Mama kept the house. School. Engineering. Nothing bad ever happened to me...(turning away)...till everything changed.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Everything changed for all of us. Whether we had a story or not.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A SOUND outside the window. Charlie glances through the bars.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Hey...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley and Slack look out the window. FOUR SECURITY MEN are chasing MULLIGAN into the alley outside. They drive him like an animal against a wall, club him, and drag him away.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Mulligan.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RILEY instinctively reaches through the window's bars, but there's nothing he can do. It's a helpless feeling.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>What are they gonna do? Kill him?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Not right away. First, they'll try to get what they can out of him. About people like me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley puts his hand on her back. g t</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BEDROOM - AFTERNOON</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In a ratty bedroom, FOXY is wakened out of a snore by CHOLO.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>We're taking the truck out. Get he guys.</dialogue>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>Riley?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No, not him. Just the regular guys. Know what I mean?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CRANE DOWN FROM A FADED SIGN, TONY'S AUTOMANIA, high above what was once a car dealership, but is now a fenced-in DEPOT full of VEHICLES. A huge WHITE FACE with black cartoon eyes POPS into view, attached to a TEN-FOOT-TALL BODY emblazoned TONY BALONEY. It's one of those vinyl ADVERTISING DUMMIES that does the hula as air pumps through it. Tony's arms wave wildly, like a giant zombie, comic yet oddly unnerving as... BLAM! BLAM! Bullets hit it in the face and neck. GUS, a young soldier, and his partner BARRETT, are shooting outside the SALES OFFICE of the car-lot-turned-depot. A sign is printed on the window. "BEST DEALS IN TOWN AND THAT'S NO BALONEY!"</scene_description>
    <character>BARRETT</character>
    <dialogue>(Handing Gus a five) You win. You got him in the brain.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SUBWAY TUNNEL - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SCREECH! CHOLO pulls a CARGO CARRIER to a stop along the platform of the tunnel. FOXY, PRETTY BOY, MOUSE, ANCHOR, and SCAR, the youngest of the team, leap off the flatbed.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The steel doors under the "SUBWAY" sign open and CHOLO strides out with his TEAM. A DEPOT GUARD steps forward as the doors close and lock automatically behind them.</scene_description>
    <character>DEPOT GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>What's up, Cholo?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>(Flashing an official-looking paper) Takin' the truck out.</dialogue>
    <character>DEPOT GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>You just got back in this morning.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Nobody gets a day off these days.</dialogue>
    <character>DEPOT GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>(Taking Cholo's paper) Hey, wait a minute this is from yesterday.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>(Keeping his cool) Oh, I must have given you the wrong one. Here...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo reaches down, but not into his pocket. For his gun. Just before he draws it...SHOTS ring out.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>What's that?</dialogue>
    <character>DEPOT GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>Relax. Just target practice.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - TONY'S AUTOMANIA SALES OFFICE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>Double or nothing?</dialogue>
    <character>BARRETT</character>
    <dialogue>Sure.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>GUS aims his rifle at the jerking head of TONY BALONEY. As he is about to fire, there's a SOUND at his back.</scene_description>
    <character>GUS</character>
    <dialogue>Quit scratching around back there. You're tryin' ta fuck up my aim.</dialogue>
    <character>BARRETT</character>
    <dialogue>I'm just standin' here. I'm not doin' nothing.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The SOUND comes again. From the woods that adjoin the lot. Barrett grabs the handles of a KLIEG LIGHT mounted on a pivot and swings it so that it ILLUMINATES the tree-line. here's nothing there. Nothing but BRANCHES being slapped by erratic gusts of wind. Barrett pivots the Klieg light back to its original position, jumping out of his skin when the bright white beam reveals... A DEAD THING within arm's length. Barrett FIRES! The dead thing DROPS OUT OF FRAME, REPLACED BY ANOTHER. BLAM! Barrett SHOOTS again. This creature collapses. It is also replaced by another, which is also shot, as... BLAM! The top of Barrett's head is taken off by a rifle shot. The rifle was fired by BIG DADDY. The barrel is still smoking. In the darkness behind him stands NUMBER NINE. Behind Number Nine are the SHUFFLING SHADOWS of many more dead things. GUS SCREAMS.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>What's that? Screaming practice?</dialogue>
    <character>GUNNER (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Stenches! Jesus! They're all over the place!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE DEPOT GUARD turns and runs toward his men. CHOLO'S TEAM unstraps weapons and gets ready for battle.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>(Stopping them) Ain't our fight. Stenches are making it easy for us.</dialogue>
    <dialogue>Let's grab the truck.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HOLO and his team sprint across the lot to DEAD RECKONING. A GUNNER at a machine-gun battery opens fire on the WALKERS. Many of the rounds SPARK off the wire fencing.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO and his TEAM scramble into the vehicle.</scene_description>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>Should we send up some `sky flowers'?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No. Those things want to get in here...let `em in.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE WALKING DEAD march through MACHINE GUN FIRE behind their "leader". BIG DADDY. He is the first to reach the fence surrounding the lot. Pushing against the wire, he is soon joined by NUMBER NINE. Then OTHERS. The FENCE COLLAPSES. The Dead Things SWARM into the depot. VROOOM! DEAD RECKONING pulls out. Rumbling over the section of fencing the zombies pushed down, it drives into the night. SOLDIERS abandon their stations and scatter, shooting wildly. NUMBER NINE knocks one of them cold with its baseball bat. The soldier falls, losing his M-16. BIG DADDY grabs the bat and throws it aside. Picking up the soldier's M-16, he presses the weapon into Number Nine's hands, even arranging Number Nine's fingers on the trigger. RATATATAT. With the gun aimed at the ground, Number Nine fires a BURST that sends her into a spastic dance. The soldier sits back up. Draws a pistol. Big Daddy grabs the barrel of the still-firing M-16 and guides it along the pavement to... ...the soldier's legs. Bullets march up his groin, belly, chest, and, finally, head. He drops. ANOTHER SOLDIER attacks. This time, Number Nine aims her weapon purposefully and scores a direct hit. OTHER DEAD THINGS SMACK at the steel doors that lead down to the subway. They can't get through. Losing interest, they drift slowly away, until their attention is refocused by... ...a GRUNT from Big Daddy, who is gazing toward the GLOW of the FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE across the river, closer now than before. The city. That's where he wants to be. That's where he's determined to go.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. KAUFMAN PENTHOUSE - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>KAUFMAN RIPS a TURKEY LEG off a cooked bird on a platter in front of him and eats. Across the table sits one of his board members, HARRISON SUTHERLAND. KNIPP enters.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Phone call, sir.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you, Knipp. I'll take it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Knipp brings a radio-phone to the table. Kaufman picks up the receiver and lifts it to his ear.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Yes?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Kaufman?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman tenses, just enough for Sutherland to notice.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Ah. The one that got away.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>You said we should talk when I was less excited. I'm a lot less excited now.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>What do you want, Mister DeMora?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I can't have a place in the Green, fine. I'll go find another place. But you know what I'm gonna need? Money. I want my money out of your bank. And I want the rest of the money out of your bank. And if you don't give it to me, I'm gonna blow you out of your fuckin' ivory tower. I've got Dead Reckoning.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. KAUFMAN PENTHOUSE - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>That's unfortunate.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Put the money on a boat and send it across the river to the South Side. Tenth Street Pier. One man to drive the boat, no more. You've got till midnight. Four hours. I won't be there. Dead Reckoning won't be there. But I'll know if it happens. I'll know if it doesn't happen.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CLICK! CHOLO hangs up.</scene_description>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>Trouble?</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>In a world where the dead are returning to life, the word `trouble' loses much of its meaning. (Beat) He wants money.</dialogue>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>Pay him.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>We don't negotiate with terrorists. There are other options.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. JAIL - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CLANG! A FIDDLER'S GREEN SECURITY GUARD opens a cell door.</scene_description>
    <character>SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>Which one of you is Denbo?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>RILEY, CHARLIE, and SLACK exchange glances. What now?</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. FIDDLER'S GREEN BOARDROOM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>KAUFMAN sips a Scotch. SUTHERLAND is present, with a middle- aged board member named CHANDLER STYLES and CLIFF WOODS, who is young and ambitious. All of them are nervous, pacing. A door opens and RILEY is ushered into the room.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Mister Denbo. Come in. Can I offer you a drink?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I don't drink.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>

    <scene_description>The steel doors to the subway tunnel open. RILEY and his TEAM step out. The depot has been DEVASTATED. FIRES BURNING. FENCES DOWN. Only TONY BALONEY moves, still waving spookily.</scene_description>

    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Stenches have been at this place.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He leads the way into the depot, his M-16 at the ready. Behind him, all eyes peer nervously into the smoke. Everyone speaks in HUSHED tones.</scene_description>
    <character>MANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>When the truck pulled out, it must have knocked the fence down. That's how they got in.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Good thing we're smarter.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Look who's talkin'.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>They're getting smart. I saw it in</dialogue>
    <dialogue>Uniontown, last time out. They're learning how to work together.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Thoughts darken. So does the SMOKE, which billows thicker, virtually blinding the team. SOUNDS come. The MOANING of the WIND. The POPPING of burnt metal and wood.</scene_description>
    <character>TEAHOUSE</character>
    <dialogue>What do they want?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slack looks back as she walks. The zombies have taken down another section of the depot fence, beyond which lies a suburb. Beyond which is the river. Beyond which is the glow of the FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>They want the city.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>The city is us. They're after us. We pissed `em off one too many times.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>O</scene_description>
    <character>MANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>They'll never get across the river.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Thank Heaven.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Gotta love the guy. He still believes in Heaven. Anyone got a radio?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Teahouse pulls a Motorola from his belt. Just as he tosses it to Riley, they hear...GROWLING! the team draws their weapons, standing in a loose circle, their backs to each other, guns searching for a target. Darting eyes peer into the void. MORE NOISES emanate from somewhere. Everywhere. Slowly... ...Charlie unstraps his Remington. Licks his thumb. Wets the sight of the rifle.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(A whisper) Why do you do that?</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>(Whispering back) Catches the light. Right now it's moonlight. Lets me see where I'm aimin'.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BLAM! Charlie FIRES! A single shot into the black smoke.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>The hell you shooting at?</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>That thing.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>DEAD MAN steps out of the smoke! Before anyone can react, it grabs Slack's shoulder from behind! She whirls around. Pulls away. Is about to shoot when she sees AN ENTRY WOUND on the left side of the Thing's forehead.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>ff-center. But I got him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Thing relaxes its grip and drops at Slack's feet.</scene_description>
    <character>ANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>(Hysterical) There's more of `em out there. I can hear `em. THERE'S MORE!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>There are SHUFFLING SOUNDS in the smoke. Manolete backs away. Pillsbury grabs him. Slaps him, hard, across the face.</scene_description>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>If they is more, we gonna need mo guns. Pull `em out n'stann up wid us, like de man you ain't.</dialogue>

    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Even-Steven.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Not! That hurt! I didn't hurt you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Manolete fumbles with colored wires under the dash.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Hurry up.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>(Impatient) Yellow to red!</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Mexico got a million cars. Samoa got five thousand. Every one. Stolen.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE T-BIRD'S ENGINE REVS. I GOT IT! LET'S GET OUT OF HERE! Riley leads the team into the T-Bird. Manolete starts to get out from under the dash. As TEAHOUSE settles into a seat by the door... ...SOMETHING heavy and wet SMACKS his shoulder. It's a FOREARM! It drops onto Teahouse as if thrown at him.</scene_description>
    <character>TEAHOUSE</character>
    <dialogue>God! Oh, GOD, WHAT'S THIS?!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Teahouse HURLS the bloody thing onto the asphalt. Shockingly, the ARM SPRINGS BACK, THUMPING against Teahouse's face! A twist of torn muscle, no thicker than clothesline, is keeping the limb loosely attached to... ...A DEAD THING that has crawled beside the T-Bird. Lifting itself, it BITES a large filet out of Teahouse's arm. CHARLIE SHOOTS it. Manolete climbs up behind the wheel and...VROOOOOM!...pedal to the metal he pulls out of the depot. Slack glances at Teahouse, then, wind in her hair, leans in close to Riley.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(Softly) How long does he have?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I had a brother. Real brother, by birth. Bit. Hung on for six days. Before he turned. I was the one had to shoot him.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>And you said nothin' bad ever happened to you.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>That happened to my brother.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(Into his eyes) But you kept going.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Got to, right?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Yup. Dead is dead. And that ain't you. And that ain't me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slack turns to Teahouse.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry, man. I truly am.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>I recognize that some of you are concerned. We've been threatened by a disgruntled employee. I've sent people out to take care of the problem.     <dialogue>On our way? To where?</dialogue>

    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>You interrupted me. I was just talking about how people can be replaced. You don't want to be replaced, do you?</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>(Nervous) No.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>No, and I don't want to replace you. You have promise. A day may come when you earn yourself some responsibilities. Right now, the responsibilities are mine. All the responsibilities. I keep the people on the streets away from us by giving them their games and vices. It costs me money! But I spend it because the responsibility is mine!     <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, but...</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>No buts.</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>But...</dialogue>

    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Take him out with the rest of the garbage. I won't be needing this man anymore.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>At the conference table, Sutherland sees the light coming in from the outer corridor, better defining the silhouettes as the Security Guard drags Cliff away.</scene_description>

    <dialogue>(To Styles) Pretty soon it's going to be one of us.</dialogue>

    <dialogue>Pull over.</dialogue>

    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I made a deal with your boss. Find Cholo. I'm gonna do it. Keep him from blowing up the Green. I'm gonna do it, I don't want people to get hurt. Bring back Dead Reckoning... Sorry.
