    <stage_direction>INT. DR. MOTH'S HOUSE. DAY</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A stuffed alligator hangs from the ceiling , pills , potions , amulets and charms , star charts and mystic paraphernalia festoon the place . Testimonials and framed degrees hang on the walls . WILL lying on a couch , on his back . His eyes are closed DR. MOTH sits by the couch , listening to WILL and occasionally making a note on a pad he holds on his knee . What we have here is nothing less than the false dawn of analysis . The session is being timed by an hourglass .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Words, words, words... once, I had the gift... I could make love out of words as a potter makes cups out of clay love that overthrows empires, love that binds two hearts together come hellfire and brimstones... for sixpence a line, I could cause a riot in a nunnery... but now</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>And yet you tell me you lie with women?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL seems unwiling to respond . DR. MOTH refers to his notes .</scene_description>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Black Sue, Fat Phoebe, Rosaline, Burbage's seamstress ; Aphrodite, who does it behind the Dog and</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( interrupting . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Aye, now and again, but what of it? I have lost my gift.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>I am here to help you. Tell me in your own words.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I have lost my gift.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( not finding this easy . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>It's as if my quill is broken. As if the organ of the imagination has dried up. As if the proud tower of my genius has collapsed.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>Interesting.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Nothing comes.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>Most interesting.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>It is like trying to a pick a lock with a wet herring.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <parenthetical>( shrewdly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Tell me, are you lately humbled in the act of love?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL turns towards him . How did he know that ?</scene_description>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How long has it been?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>A goodly length in times past, but lately</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>No, no. You have a wife, children</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The sand runs through the hourglass .</scene_description>
    <character>LATER</character>
    <dialogue>Not much sand left.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I was a lad of eighteen. Anne Hathaway was a woman, half as old again.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>A woman of property?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shrugs . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>She had a cottage. One day, she was three months gone with child, so</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>And your relations?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>On my mother's side the Ardens</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>No, your marriage bed.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Four years and a hundred miles away in Stratford. A cold bed too, since the twins were born. Banishment was a blessing.</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>So now you are free to love</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>yet can not love nor write it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>DR. MOTH reaches for a glass snake bracelet .</scene_description>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>Here is a bangle found in Psyche's temple on Olympus cheap at four pence. Write your name on a paper and feed it in the snake.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL looks at the snake bangle in wonder .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Will it restore my gift?</dialogue>
    <character>DR. MOTH</character>
    <dialogue>The woman who wears the snake will dream of you, and your gift will return. Words will flow like a river. I will see you in a week.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He holds out his hand . WILL drops a sovereign into it , and takes the bracelet .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DR. MOTH'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL comes out . HENSLOWE is waiting , standing in a horse trough to ease his feet . WILL walks straight past him , and HENSLOWE follows .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Now where? Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>To the Palace at Whitehall.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BACKSTAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WHITEHALL means nothing yet . We are behind closed curtains on a stage busy with preparations for the imminent performance of Two Gentlemen of Verona . This is not a theatre but a banqueting hall , as we will see . RICHARD BURBAGE is to play `` PROTEUS . '' A BOY PLAYER will play `` SILVIA , '' and last minute improvements to his makeup etc. are being applied by BURBAGE 'S mistress ROSALINE . `` LAUNCE , '' one of the clowns , is the famous comedian WILL KEMPE . `` LAUNCE 'S '' dog , CRAB is in KEMPE 'S charge and is not helping much . There is no set . A helpful placard reading VERONA - AN OPEN PLACE , is ready to hand . MUSICIANS can be heard tuning their instruments . From the other side of the curtain there is an expectant bubbub . KEMPE leads the dog into the wings and rummages in a box of proops . He finds a skull . He has one foot on the box , his elbow on his knee , he looks at the skull ... in other words he reminds us of Hamlet . We see this from the POV of WILL , who is just entering through a door backstage .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( approaching . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Prithee, Mr. Kempe, break a leg. You too, good Crab.</dialogue>
    <character>KEMPE</character>
    <dialogue>Crab is nervous. He has never played the Palace. When will you write me a tragedy, Will? I could do it.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>No, they would laugh at Seneca if you played it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL 'S attention has been caught by ROSALINE , BURBAGE 'S mistress . ROSALINE is big breasted , dark - eyed , dark - haired , sexual .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to ROSALINE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My sleeve wants for a button, Mistress Rosaline, where were my seamstress's eyes?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BURBAGE kisses her mouth and slaps her behind . He comes over to greet WILL .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>There is no dog in the first scene, Will Kempe, thank you. How goes it Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I am still owed money for this play, Burbage.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Not from me. I only stole it. When are you coming over to the Chamberlain's Men?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>When I have fifty pounds.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ROSALINE brings over the last elements of BURBAGE 'S costume and helps him into them .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Are you writing?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( nods somewhat defensively . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>A comedy. All but done, a pirate comedy, wonderful.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>What is the chief part?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo. Wit, swordsman, lover.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>The title?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>I will play him. Bring it tomorrow.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>It's for Henslowe. He paid me.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>How much?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Ten pounds.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>You're a liar.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BURBAGE digs under his costume for his purse , which is on a waistband , over his corset .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I swear it. He wants Romeo for Ned and the Admiral's Men.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Ned is wrong for it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL turns to see HENSLOWE approaching .</scene_description>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <parenthetical>( to WILL . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Here is two sovereigns - I'll give you two more when you show me the pages.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Done.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( arriving . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Burbage, I will see you hanged for a pickpocket.</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>The Queen has commanded, she loves a comedy and the Master of the Revels favours us.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>And what favour does Mr. Tilney receive from you?</dialogue>
    <character>BURBAGE</character>
    <dialogue>Ask him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Master of the Revels -LRB- TILNEY -RRB- comes through the curtain officiously .</scene_description>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>She comes!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He disappears back through the curtains . The hubbub falls silent , rather dramatically , and all the busy PLAYERS know what that means : they all crowd to the curtain and find places to peep through .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. FRONT OF HOUSE/STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE POV OF THE PLAYERS . The arrival of QUEEN ELIZABETH , aged sixty , coming to take her place in the audience at front centre . The hill is crowded with lords and ladies , bowing ELIZABETH to her seat , which is raised high on a pedestal , affording the QUEEN an uninterrupted view of the play , and the audience an uninterrupted view of the QUEEN . Trumpets sound . Close on a small piece of paper : a quill is writing `` W. Shakespeare . '' WILL rolls the paper up carefully and slips it into the mouth of the snake bangle . The curtain draws back and CONDELL as `` VALENTINE '' and BURBAGE as `` PROTEUS '' begin the play .</scene_description>
    <character>CONDELL AS VALENTINE</character>
    <dialogue>`` Cease to persuade, my loving Proteus ; Home - keeping youth have ever homely wits...''</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. THE WINGS/BACKSTAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>With BURBAGES 'S presence accounted for on stage , ROSALINE curls an arm around WILL 'S neck . They kiss hungrily . After a moment , WILL pulls back .</scene_description>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>When will you write me a sonnet, Will?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I have lost my gift.</dialogue>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>You left it in my bed. Come to look for it again.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Are you to be my muse, ROSALINE?</dialogue>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>Burbage has my keeping but you have my heart.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL takes the snake bracelet and slips it onto her arm . ROSALINE looks at it , then at WILL . Then they kiss again , but WILL is distracted by the sound of coughing from the auditorium .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>You see? The consumptives plot against me. `` Will Shakespeare has a play, let us go and cough through it.''</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>`` VALENTINE '' is on stage with `` PROTEUS . '' CONDELL AS VALENTINE `` To be in love , where scorn is bought with groans : Coy looks with heart sore sighs ; One fading moment 's mirth With twenty watchful , weary , tedious nights ... '' As the scene continues , WILL appears at the back of the hall and finds himself next to HENSLOWE .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I feel a scene coming on.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Is it about a pirate's daughter?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BACK OF THE BANQUETING HALL/STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Laughter . It is later , and KEMPE is now on stage with his dog . The audience is roaring .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>You see? Comedy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>QUEEN ELIZABETH 'S idiosyncratic laugh rises above the others .</scene_description>
    <character>QUEEN</character>
    <dialogue>Well played, Master Crab, I commend you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She throws a sweetheart on the stage and the dog wolfs it down . Everyone applauds .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Love and a bit with a dog, that's what they like.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now we meet VIOLA . VIOLA DE LESSEPS is twenty - five and beautiful , and she is laughing with great natural enjoyment . She sits slightly apart from her small family group - her parents , SIR ROBERT DE LESSEPS and LADY MARGARET DE LESSEPS . Part of the group but seated behind as befits her lower status is VIOLA 'S NURSE . Elsewhere is LORD WESSEX , our villain . WESSEX is in his forties , dark cruel , self - important . He has noticed VIOLA . The nurse notices him .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WHITEHALL PALACE. BANQUETING HALL. FRONT OF HOUSE/STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LATER . `` VALENTINE '' is on stage alone . He is speaking the speech rather more coarsely than the version we hear later .</scene_description>
    <character>CONDELL AS VALENTINE</character>
    <dialogue>`` What light is light if Silvia be not seen? What joy is joy, if Silvia be not by? Unless it be to think that she is by And feed upon the shadow of perfection...''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now we see that VIOLA knows the speech by heart , and is silently mouthing it with the actor .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>There's a lady knows your play by heart.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But when he turns to WILL he finds that WILL has gone .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WILL'S ROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL comes into his room , goes straight to his table in the window , and arranges pen , ink , and paper . Now he has his ritual : he spins round once in a circle , rubs his hands together and spits on the floor . Then he sits down , picks up his pen , and stares in front of him . PAUSE . Then he begins to write .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The NURSE is undressing her , though VIOLA tries intermittently to push her away . She is still bright with excitement .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Did you like Proteus or Valentine best? Proteus for speaking, Valentine for looks.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>I liked the dog, for laughs.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>But Silvia I did not care for much. His fingers were red from fighting and he spoke like a schoolboy at lessons. Stage love will never be true love while the law of the land has our heroines played by pipsqueak boys in petticoats! Oh, when can we see another?</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>When the Queen commands it.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>But at the playhouse. Nurse?</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Be still.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Now the NURSE is cleaning VIOLA 'S ears , one by one , of course . She has an ear - cleaning implement for this . VIOLA submits .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Playhouses are not for well - born ladies.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>I am not so well - born.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Well - monied is the same as well - born and well - married is more so. Lord Wessex was looking at you tonight.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>All the men at court are without poetry. If they look at me they see my father's fortune. I will have poetry in my life. And adventure. And love. Love above all.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Like Valentine and Silvia?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>No. not the artful postures of love, but love that over - throws life. Unbiddable, ungovernable, like a riot in the heart, and nothing to be done, come ruin or rapture. Love like there has never been in a play.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( beat . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I will have love or I will end my days as a.</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>As a nurse.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( kissing her . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But I would be Valentine and Silvia too. Good Nurse, God save you and good night. I would stay asleep my whole life if I could dream myself into a company of players.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>VIOLA goes over to the window .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The NURSE thrusts a twig to her face .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Clean your teeth while you dream, then.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Automatically , VIOLA takes the twig and begins brushing her teeth , all the while looking downriver towards the Rose . The NURSE attends her with a beaker of water , and a bowl .</scene_description>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Now spit</dialogue>
    <scene_description>VIOLA gazes longingly towards the Rose ... And , there and then , she makes a plan .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. SQUARE IN FRONT OF THE ROSE THEATRE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE is making his way from the theatre to the market place when FENNYMAN and LAMBERT appear at either shoulder and propel him back the way he came . FREES follows behind .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>This time we take your boots off!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>What have I done, Mr. Fennyman?</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>The theatres are all closed by the plague!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, that.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>by order of the Master of the Revels!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Fennyman, let me explain about the theatre business.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( they stop . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>The natural condition is one of insurmountable obstacles on the road to imminent disaster. Believe me, to be close by the plague is a bagatelle in the ups and downs of owning a theatre.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>So what do we do?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Nothing. Strangely enough, it all turns out well.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>How?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>I do n't know. It's a mystery.</dialogue>
    <character>LAMBERT</character>
    <parenthetical>( dumbly . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Should I kill him, Mr. Fennyman?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>At this point din is heard in the background . a messenger , ringing a bell , is running though the street .</scene_description>
    <character>MESSENGER</character>
    <dialogue>The theatres are reopened. By order of the Master of the Revels, the theatres are reopened</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FENNYMAN is intrigued .</scene_description>
    <character>FREES</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Fennyman! Mr. Tilney has opened the playhouses.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Yes I heard.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE plays his temporary advantage modestly , shrugging himself free of LAMBERT 'S grip .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to LAMBERT . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>If you would n't mind</dialogue>
    <scene_description>HENSLOWE continues on his way . FENNYMAN watches HENSLOWE , curious .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Where is the play?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, it's coming, it's coming.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WILL'S ROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is . WILL is writing furiously . A burnt - down candle is still alight , although it is day outside the window . He has been writing all night . He has written about ten pages . Pleased with himself and excited , he gathers them up and leaves the room like a man with a mission .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. WILL'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Leaving the house , pages in hand , WILL nearly knocks down HENSLOWE who has come to see him .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Will! The theatres are</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Before he can finish , WILL brandishes the pages in his hand .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo and Rosaline. Scene One! God, I'm good!</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Rosaline? You mean Ethel.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL has gone .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. BURBAGE'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>BURBAGE lives in another part of the city . WILL bangs through the door without ceremony .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shouting . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Richard!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BURBAGE'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL enters and calls out .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Burbage?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BURBAGE'S BEDROOM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL charges into the bedroom . ROSALINE is in bed . The Master of the Revels is pulling up his breeches . WILL is shattered .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Tilney</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The unsuccessful snake bracelet glints at him from ROSALINE 'S arm .</scene_description>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>Like you, I found him not at home!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>So this is the favour you find in the Chamberlain's Men.</dialogue>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <dialogue>Will!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to ROSALINE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I would have made you immortal.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( turning to go . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Tell Burbage he has lost a new play by Will Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>What does Burbage care of that? He is readying the Curtain for Kit Marlowe.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>You have opened the playhouses?</dialogue>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <dialogue>I have, Master Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>But the plague</dialogue>
    <character>TILNEY</character>
    <parenthetical>( sighs . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Yes, I know. But he was always hanging around the house.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A bell can be heard ringing outside .</scene_description>
    <character>ROSALINE</character>
    <parenthetical>( to WILL , leaving . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Will... you're the only one, Will! - in my heart.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. STREET. OUTSIDE BURBAGE'S HOUSE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL emerges looking distraught . A burning brazier stands by the wall . WILL thrusts the pages into the coals . He watches for a moment as the pages catch fire .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. TAVERN. DAY.</stage_direction>

    <parenthetical>( startled . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>How do I offend, my lord?</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>By coveting my property. I can not shed blood in her house but I will cut your throat anon. You have a name?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( gulps . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Christopher Marlowe at your service.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WESSEX shoves him through the nearest door . VIOLA 'S eyes are searching the room for WILL . She finds WESSEX smiling at her . She looks away .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DE LESSEPS' GARDEN/VIOLA'S BALCONY. NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There is a lighted window on the balcony . VIOLA , dressed for bed , and the NURSE pass across the lighted space . WILL is in the garden . He sees her . The light in the room is extinguished . WILL sighs . Then VIOLA comes out onto the balcony in the moonlight . WILL gasps . He watches her . VIOLA sighs dreamily .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo, Romeo. a young man of Verona. A comedy. By William Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL reckons that 's a good enough cue . He comes out of hiding , and approaches the balcony .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( whispers . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My lady!</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( gasps . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Who is there?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Will Shakespeare!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The NURSE calls `` Madam ! '' from inside the room .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Anon, good nurse. Anon.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to WILL . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Master Shakespeare?!</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>The same, alas.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Oh but why `` alas?''</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>A lowly player.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Alas indeed, for I thought you the highest poet of my esteem and a writer of plays that capture my heart.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Oh - I am him too!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The NURSE calls again .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( to NURSE . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Anon, anon!</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to WILL . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I will come again.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She goes inside for a moment .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( to himself . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh, I am fortune's fool, I will be punished for this!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>VIOLA returns . WILL comes forward again .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Oh my lady, my love!</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>If they find you here they will kill you.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>You can bring them with a word.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Oh, not for the world!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The NURSE calls her again : `` Madam ! ''</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Anon, nurse!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But she goes inside . WILL looks around and sees that there is , as ever a convenient tree . He starts to climb up toward the balcony . When his head is nearly level , a soft figure comes once more onto the balcony . WILL pops his head over the parapet and is face to face with the NURSE . The NURSE gives a yell . WILL falls out of the tree .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DE LEESEPSES' HOUSE. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Male voice shout to each other inside the house , candle flames appear in different windows , the garden door is flung open , revealing SIR ROBERT with candelabra in one hand and sword in the other . By this time WILL is on top of the garden wall and he drops safely out of sight . He could have written it better .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. WILL'S ROOM. DAWN.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL is burning the midnight oil - literally and metaphorically . His quill has already covered a dozen sheets . He is inspired .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. STAGE/AUDITORIUM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>It is day one . THE COMPANY is on stage . PETER is passing pages around a bunch of actors . JOHN , JAMES , and NOL are looking through their pages .</scene_description>
    <character>JOHN</character>
    <dialogue>`` Draw if you be men!</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to JAMES . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gregory, remember thy washing blow.''</dialogue>
    <character>NOL</character>
    <dialogue>`` Part, fools, put up your swords.''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL is going around pumping hands and slapping shoulders , flushed with excitement . HENSLOWE is reading his pages , worried . RALPH BASHFORD is next to him .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>It starts well, and then it's all long - faced about some Rosaline. Where's the comedy, Will. Where's the dog?</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to RALPH . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Do you think it is funny?</dialogue>
    <character>RALPH</character>
    <dialogue>I was a Pirate King, now I'm a Nurse. That's funny</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL pulls HENSLOWE aside .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>We are at least six men short, and those we have will be overparted, ranters and stutterers who should be sent back to the stews. My Romeo has let me down. I see disaster.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>We are at least four acts short, Will, if you are looking for disaster.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL as notices a young scruffy thirteen - year - old actor , the URCHIN we met before .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Who are you, master?</dialogue>
    <character>URCHIN</character>
    <dialogue>I am Ethel, sir, the Pirate's daughter.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( furiously . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I'll be damned if you are!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>And he helps the URCHIN off with a kick . The URCHIN glowers with resentment . HENSLOWE finds himself face to face with FENNYMAN .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Is it going well?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Very well.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>But nothing is happening.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, but very well.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( shouts . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gentlemen! Thank you! You are welcome.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Who is that?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Nobody. The author.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>We are about to embark on a great voyage.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>It is customary to make a little speech on the first day. It does no harm and authors like it.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>You want to know what parts you are to receive. All will be settled as we go</dialogue>
    <scene_description>That 's as far as he gets before there is a dramatic interruption - the public entrance door is flung open and SIX MEN make a loud entrance , headed by NED ALLEYN , the actor , who is a handsome piratical figure with a big voice and a big sword .</scene_description>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>Huzzah! The Admiral's Men are returned to the house!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He gets various reactions . HENSLOWE and WILL shout his name joyfully , some of the actors are friends with the new group and behave accordingly , others know they are out of a job . FENNYMAN recovers , or tries to .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Who is this?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ALLEYN slaps him aside with his sword .</scene_description>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <parenthetical>( roars . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Silence, you god! I am Hieronimo! I am Tamburlaine! I am Faustus! I am Barrabas, the Jew of Malta - of yes, Master Will, and I am Henry VI. What is the play, and what is my part?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FENNYMAN is impressed .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>A moment, sir!</dialogue>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <parenthetical>( roars . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Who are you?</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( bleating . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I am the money!</dialogue>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>Then you may remain so long as you remain silent. Pay attention and you will see how genius creates a legend.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <parenthetical>( respectfully . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Thank you, sir.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>We are in desperate want of a Mercutio, Ned, a young nobleman of Verona</dialogue>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>And the title of this piece?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Mercutio</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Is it?</dialogue>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>I will play him!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Half a dozen of the ADMIRAL 'S MEN will be given roles in our play and we meet them and identify them as WILL enthusiastically shakes hands .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Mr. Pope! Mr. Phillips! Welcome, George Bryan! James Armitage!</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( and now greeting SAM GOSSE , the female star of the Admiral 's Men . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Sam! My pretty one! Are you ready to fall in love again?</dialogue>
    <character>SAM</character>
    <parenthetical>( hoarsely . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I am, Master Shakespeare.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( concerned . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>But your voice.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( he thrust a hand between SAM 'S legs . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Have they dropped?</dialogue>
    <character>SAM</character>
    <parenthetical>( a girlie voice now . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No, no, a touch of cold only. We suspect he is lying but WILL has turned away.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Master Henslowe, you have your actors.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He leaves , passing by the humbled FENNYMAN .</scene_description>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>I saw his Tamburlaine, you know. Wonderful.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, I saw it.</dialogue>
    <character>FENNYMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Of course, it was mighty writing. There is no one like Marlowe</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL is used to it . He goes .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. RIVERBANK. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL arrives in a hurry at the wharfside , and looks vainly in the direction of the DE LESSEPSES ' house : no THOMAS .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE ROSE THEATRE. STAGE DOOR. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WILL looks down the alley : - no THOMAS . He turns away . The URCHIN , the short - lived Ethel , is sitting in the alley .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Better fortune, boy.</dialogue>
    <character>URCHIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( shrugs . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I was in a play. They cut my head off in Titus Andronicus. When I write plays, they will be like Titus.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( pleased . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You admire it?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The URCHIN nods grimly .</scene_description>
    <character>URCHIN</character>
    <dialogue>I like it when they cut heads off. And the daughter mutilated with knives.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Oh. What is your name?</dialogue>
    <character>URCHIN.</character>
    <dialogue>says. John Webster. Here, kitty, kitty.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Because a stray cat is nearby . The cat show an interest . The URCHIN passes a white mouse to the cat and watches the result with sober interest .</scene_description>
    <character>URCHIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Plenty of blood. That is the only writing.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL backs away , unnerved by the boy .</scene_description>
    <character>URCHIN</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Wait, you'll see the cat bites his head off.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>I have to get back.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. STAGE/AUDITORIUM. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>On stage . the actors carry their parts . NOL AS BENVOLIO `` See where he comes . So please you step aside ; I 'll know his grievance or be much denied . ''</scene_description>
    <character>MONTAGUE</character>
    <dialogue>`` I would thou wert so happy by thy stay To hear true shrift. Come, madam, let's away.''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Onstage `` MONTAGUE '' and `` LADY MONTAGUE '' make their exit . Offstage , WILL appears next to HENSLOWE .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Cut round him for now.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <parenthetical>( not understanding . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What? Who?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Romeo.</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>The one who came with your letter?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <character>NOL AS BENVOLIO</character>
    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>`` Good morrow, cousin.''</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS ROMEO</character>
    <parenthetical>( O.S . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>`` Is the day so young?''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The voice is THOMAS 'S . WILL turns back to the stage and sees him . Today THOMAS has a wig as well as his small mustache .</scene_description>
    <character>NOL AS BENVOLIO</character>
    <dialogue>`` But new struck nine.''</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS ROMEO</character>
    <dialogue>`` Ay me, sad hours seem long. Was that my father that went hence so fast?''</dialogue>
    <character>NOL AS BENVOLIO</character>
    <dialogue>It was. What sadness lengthens Romeo's hours?''</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS ROMEO</character>
    <dialogue>`` Not having that which, having, makes them short.''</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Good</dialogue>
    <character>NOL AS BENVOLIO</character>
    <dialogue>`` In love?''</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS ROMEO</character>
    <dialogue>`` Out.''</dialogue>
    <character>NOL AS BENVOLIO</character>
    <dialogue>`` Of love?''</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS ROMEO</character>
    <dialogue>`` Out of her favour where I am in love.''</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( interrupting . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>No, no, no... Do n't spend it all at once!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The rehearsal stops .</scene_description>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, sir.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Do you understand me?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <dialogue>No, sir.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>He is speaking about a baggage we never even meet! What will be left in your purse when he meets his Juliet?</dialogue>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>Juliet? You mean Ethel.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( rounding on him . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>God's teeth, am I to suffer this constant stream of interruption?!</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( to THOMAS . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>What will you do in Act Two when he meets the love of his life?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA AS THOMAS</character>
    <parenthetical>( timidly - looking through his few sheets of paper . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I am very sorry, sir, I have not seen Act Two.</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>Of course you have not! I have not written it!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Alone in the auditorium , FENNYMAN looks and listens , fascinated . So this is theatre !</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Go once more!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>NED ALLEYN comes out of the wings , frowning over his manuscript .</scene_description>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>Will... Where is Mercutio?</dialogue>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( tapping his forehead . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Locked safe in here. I leave the scene in your safe keeping, Ned, I have a sonnet to write.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL moves back into the wings where HENSLOWE is looking anxious .</scene_description>
    <character>HENSLOWE</character>
    <dialogue>A sonnet? You mean a play.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL moves on , ignoring him . As he goes , we see that VIOLA is love - struck by him , a riot in the heart .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. STAIRCASE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>VIOLA still dressed as THOMAS , sonnet in hand , runs up the stairs to her room . From the other end of the house WESSEX can be heard ranting .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. HALL. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LORD WESSEX is being kept waiting . The NURSE is bearing the brunt of his impatience .</scene_description>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>Two hours at prayer!</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>Lady Viola is pious, my lord.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>Piety is for Sunday! And two hours at prayer is not piety, it is self - importance!</dialogue>
    <character>NURSE</character>
    <dialogue>It would be better that you return tomorrow, my lord.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>It would be better that you tell her to get off her knees and show some civility to her six - day lord and master.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>VIOLA opens the door . She has changed hurriedly - too hurriedly : the effect of her glorious hair falling to her bare shoulders is spoiled by her mustache . Fortunately , the NURSE spots her before WESSEX does and by coming forward to greet her , the NURSE manages to shield Viola from view , communicate the problem , and announce WESSEX 'S presence , so that by the time the NURSE has passed by VIOLA and let herself out of the room , the moustache has disappeared .</scene_description>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>My lady VIOLA.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Lord Wessex. You have been waiting.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>I am aware of it, but it is beauty's privilege.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>You flatter, my lord.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>No. I have spoken to the Queen.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Her majesty's consent is requisite when a Wessex takes a wife, and once gained, her consent is her command.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Do you intend to marry, my lord?</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>Your father should keep you better informed. He has bought me for you. He returns from his estates to see us married two weeks from Saturday.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( pause . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You are allowed to show your pleasure.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>I do not love you, my lord.</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>How your mind hops about! Your father was a shopkeeper, your children will bear arms, and I will recover my fortune. That is the only matter under discussion today. You will like Virginia.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>Virginia?!</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>Why, yes! My fortune lies in my plantations. The tobacco weed. I need four thousand pounds to fit out a ship and put my investments to work - I fancy tobacco has a future. We will not stay there long, three or four years.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>But why me?</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>It was your eyes. No, your lips.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He kisses her with more passion than ceremony . VIOLA recoils , and slaps him .</scene_description>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Will you defy your father and your Queen?</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <dialogue>The Queen has consented?</dialogue>
    <character>WESSEX</character>
    <dialogue>She wants to inspect you. At Greenwich, come Sunday. Be submissive, modest, grateful and brief.</dialogue>
    <character>VIOLA</character>
    <parenthetical>( forced to submit . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>I will do my duty, my lord.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DE LESSEPSES' HOUSE. VIOLA'S BEDROOM. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>She is writing to WILL . His letter - poem is on her table . We can read part of it . `` Shall I compare thee to a summer 's day ... '' Now we see what VIOLA is writing . INSERT : `` Master Will , poet dearest to my heart , I beseech you , banish me from yours - I am to marry Lord Wessex - a daughter 's duty ... '' She sheds a romantic , unhappy tear .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. STAGE. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SAM is now `` JULIET . '' The play has evidently reached Act I Scene 5 . We are witnessing the meeting of `` ROMEO '' and `` JULIET '' in a simplified version of the changing - partners dance we saw at VIOLA 'S house . NED ALLEYN is in charge .</scene_description>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>Gentlemen upstage, ladies downstage!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The dance goes wrong . it is THOMAS 'S fault .</scene_description>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <parenthetical>( CONT 'D . )</parenthetical>
    <parenthetical>( furious . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>Gentlemen upstage! Ladies downstage! Are you a lady, Mr. Kent?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THOMAS mutters a blushing apology . WILL arrives the bystanders , clutching fresh pages . He gives these to PETER . NED ALLEYN sees him and comes over to start an argument .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <parenthetical>( preempting . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>You did not like the speech?</dialogue>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>The speech is excellent.</dialogue>
    <parenthetical>( he does the first line impressively . )</parenthetical>
    <dialogue>`` Oh, then I see Queen Mab hath been with you!'' Excellent and a good length. But then he disappears for the length of a bible.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WILL points significantly at the pages he has given PETER .</scene_description>
    <character>WILL</character>
    <dialogue>There you have his duel, a skirmish of words and swords such as I never wrote, nor anyone. He dies with such passion and poetry as your ever heard : `` a plague on both your houses!''</dialogue>
    <scene_description>NED nods satisfied and turns back to work . Then he turns back .</scene_description>
    <character>ALLEYN</character>
    <dialogue>He dies?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>But the author has escaped .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. THE ROSE THEATRE. WRITER'S CORNER. DAY.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Up aloft , WILL has a Writer 's Corner where he settle down to work . We see his private superstition : he spins round in a circle , rubs his hands together , and spits on the floor . That done , he picks up his pen .</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. STREET. NIGHT.</stage_direction>
