    <scene_description>Riley lifts Teahouse's Motorola and pushes "Send".</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Riley Denbo. Calling the Green.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. FIDDLER'S GREEN BOARDROOM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>LOSE ON: SUTHERLAND'S alarmed face.</scene_description>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>What?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>A TROOPER, equally alarmed, is reporting.</scene_description>
    <character>TROOPER</character>
    <dialogue>Wiped out! That's what he said! Denbo! He said the depot was wiped out by stenches!</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Thank you. Keep us informed.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY and his TEAM move through DRIFTING SMOKE. VEHICLES are scattered about. They stop at the T-BIRD. There are no keys in the ignition.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Gotta go get the keys, Riley.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley looks across the lot to the CHARRED RUIN of a shack. Tire fires BURN around it. Debris smolders.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Ain't no keys to get. Melted.</dialogue>
    <character>ANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>Screw keys. Hot wire the fucker.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>MANOLETE climbs in and goes to work under the dash.</scene_description>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>He feelin' better since I hit `im.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Suddenly, CHARLIE draws his .45 and FIRES AT SLACK! BLAM! The bullet buzzes just above her ear, blowing a WISP OF HAIR as... ...A DEAD OLD MAN BEHIND HER DROPS, a HOLE in its head.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks, Charlie. That was useful.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The WIND shifts and black SMOKE envelopes them.</scene_description>
    <character>MANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>I can't see!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley pulls out a flashlight and shines it under the dash. The team fans out around the T-Bird. The smoke is so thick they can't make out anything. Including each other. Charlie peers into openings that shift on the breeze. What he doesn't see, what he can't see, is what's behind him... ..a FEMALE WALKER, wearing the soiled and tattered remnants of a bridal gown. The fabric seems to glow in the smoke. The bride shuffles toward CHARLIE. We see it coming. No one else does. Just as it opens its mouth to bite... BLAM! Slack SHOOTS! Her bullet cuts closer than the one Charlie fired, CLIPPING OFF THE TOP OF HIS EAR before DROPPING THE BRIDE.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Even-Steven.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Not! That hurt! I didn't hurt you!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Manolete fumbles with colored wires under the dash.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Hurry up.</dialogue>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>(Impatient) Yellow to red!</dialogue>
    <character>TEAHOUSE</character>
    <dialogue>What the fuck does a Samoan know about hot-wiring cars?</dialogue>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>Five thousand cars. Stole. Every year in Samoa.</dialogue>
    <character>MANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>Fifty thousand in Mexico.</dialogue>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>Mexico got a million cars. Samoa got five thousand. Every one. Stolen.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE T-BIRD'S ENGINE REVS. I GOT IT! LET'S GET OUT OF HERE! Riley leads the team into the T-Bird. Manolete starts to get out from under the dash. As TEAHOUSE settles into a seat by the door... ...SOMETHING heavy and wet SMACKS his shoulder. It's a FOREARM! It drops onto Teahouse as if thrown at him.</scene_description>
    <character>TEAHOUSE</character>
    <dialogue>God! Oh, GOD, WHAT'S THIS?!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Teahouse HURLS the bloody thing onto the asphalt. Shockingly, the ARM SPRINGS BACK, THUMPING against Teahouse's face! A twist of torn muscle, no thicker than clothesline, is keeping the limb loosely attached to... ...A DEAD THING that has crawled beside the T-Bird. Lifting itself, it BITES a large filet out of Teahouse's arm. CHARLIE SHOOTS it. Manolete climbs up behind the wheel and...VROOOOOM!...pedal to the metal he pulls out of the depot. Slack glances at Teahouse, then, wind in her hair, leans in close to Riley.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(Softly) How long does he have?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I had a brother. Real brother, by birth. Bit. Hung on for six days. Before he turned. I was the one had to shoot him.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>And you said nothin' bad ever happened to you.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>That happened to my brother.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(Into his eyes) But you kept going.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Got to, right?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Yup. Dead is dead. And that ain't you. And that ain't me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slack turns to Teahouse.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry, man. I truly am.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She draws her .45, aims at Teahouse, and FIRES.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. FIDDLER'S GREEN BOARDROOM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>KAUFMAN paces with a cigar, passing SUTHERLAND, STYLES, and CLIFF.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>I recognize that some of you are concerned. We've been threatened by a disgruntled employee. I've sent people out to take care of the problem. However, should something go wrong, I want to assure you that measures have been taken. I've established outposts. With food and supplies to support us on our way.</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>On our way? To where?</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Alternate sites have been chosen. Air transport has been arranged. For us and our families. As well as necessary support personnel.</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>What about all the others?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman looks at Cliff, as if expecting him to understand.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>All the others can be replaced. by others.</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>But...</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Cliff, let me talk to you for a moment.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman leads Cliff into... ...an alcove on the far side of the room, shutting two pocket doors made of sandblasted glass. Sutherland and the others can't hear, but can see, Kaufman and Cliff in SILHOUETTE. ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE DOORS: Kaufman leans close to Cliff, smiling, his eyes blinking a bit too rapidly.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>You interrupted me. I was just talking about how people can be replaced. You don't want to be replaced, do you?</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>(Nervous) No.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>No, and I don't want to replace you. You have promise. A day may come when you earn yourself some responsibilities. Right now, the responsibilities are mine. All the responsibilities. It was my ingenuity that took an old world and made it into something new. I put up fences to make it safe. I hired soldiers and paid for their training. I keep the people on the streets away from us by giving them their games and vices. It costs me money! But I spend it because the responsibility is mine! Now do you understand "responsibility"?</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>Yes, but...</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>No buts.</dialogue>
    <character>CLIFF</character>
    <dialogue>But...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman looks disappointed. Taking Cliff by the arm, smiling again, he leads him over to an outer door and opens it. An armed SECURITY GUARD stands in the corridor outside.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Take him out with the rest of the garbage. I won't be needing this man anymore.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>At the conference table, Sutherland sees the light coming in from the outer corridor, better defining the silhouettes as the Security Guard drags Cliff away.</scene_description>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>(To Styles) Pretty soon it's going to be one of us.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. CARNEGIE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In an overgrown suburban street, a LAWN TRACTOR, driven by a GARDENER in work clothes, drives back and forth, back and forth, over a swath of dead grass. The gardener is DEAD too.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO watches the GARDENER through the windshield.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>If I don't have this truck, I'm no different to Kaufman than that poor Mexican bastard out there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CLOSE ON: CHOLO'S WATCH. 11:20.</scene_description>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>He's never gonna pay.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>He knows it's his ass if he doesn't.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Cholo slides open a small window, grabs his crossbow, and SHOOTS the Gardener in the head.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. ALLEY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ANGLE ON: A SOLID WALL OF WOOD. BIG DADDY, NUMBER NINE, and OTHERS OF THE DEAD push against it. The wood holds. Big Daddy turns, surveying his troops. Focusing on the BUTCHER. On the meat cleaver it has in its hand. Big Daddy pounds on the wood, demonstrating. Points at the meat cleaver. Pounds again. The Butcher gets it. Approaches the wall. HACK! The meat cleaver chops into wood, splintering it. REVERSE ANGLE: from the other side of the wall as the wood splinters to reveal BIG DADDY'S EYES staring through at... ...the FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE, looming closer than it was before, though it's still across the river.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. MCKEE'S ROCKS - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CLOSE ON: a small, electronic unit, the size and appearance of a "Game Boy". AN LED SCREEN shows a BLINKING RED DOT moving along a MAP.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Turn left up here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SLACK, driving the T-BIRD now, makes the turn. The car blows through a deserted town, moving fast. Riley notices that Slack is effected by the desolation she sees.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>How long since you been out here?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Never been out. Lived in the city since...it was a regular city.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Pull over.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(Surprised) Huh?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You said you were going to make yourself useful. Right now what I could use is for you to pull over.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>She does. The T-Bird stops along a road bordered by a MARSH thick with tall CAT TAILS. Unexpectedly, Riley stands and points his automatic at PILLSBURY and MANOLETE.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I made a deal with your boss. Find Cholo. I'm gonna do it. Keep him from blowing up the Green. I'm gonna do it, I don't want people to get hurt. Bring back Dead Reckoning... Sorry. That's where I stop. I didn't ask him for much, just guns, ammo, and a car. I've got the guns. I've got the ammo. And if I find Dead Reckoning I'm gonna have the best fucking car that's ever been built, and I'm taking it to Canada. If any of you don't like that idea...</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley reaches down and opens the passenger door. Manolete looks out and sees the CAT TAILS MOVING. THREE WALKERS are slogging through the marsh.</scene_description>
    <character>MANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>Some choice.</dialogue>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>Good choice. I like see Canada.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Pillsbury reaches out and slams the car door closed again.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Charlie, keep these two covered.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Charlie pulls his .45. Riley turns around his seat, glancing down again at the "Game Boy" in his palm. The RED DOT has moved on to ANOTHER MAP.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Take a right onto Route Six.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slack pulls out.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>This is what you were thinking about all along. You got me out here figuring I'm a boy scout, and now you're telling me we're just</dialogue>
    <dialogue>stealing a fucking car?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You have a problem with that?</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>No. I like the way you think.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>I like the way he thinks, too. Just look at me you can tell I like the way he thinks.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Take another right.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>How do you know which way you're going?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley holds up the "Game Boy". It BEEPS SOFTLY as the RED DOT shifts onto another MAP.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I built a homing device into Dead Reckoning. If Cholo's anywhere within fifty miles, we can track him.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. ROAD - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>DEAD RECKONING stops on a long road, at the end of which stands... ...a MILITARY COMPLEX. THE BEAM of a SEARCHLIGHT sweeps back and forth over the buildings, a sign of life.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO checks his watch. 11:29. He speaks into a TRANSMITTER.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Mouse. Anything?</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SHED - 10TH STREET PIER - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MOUSE stands in the shed, holding a transmitter of his own.</scene_description>
    <character>MOUSE</character>
    <dialogue>Not yet. No boat. No money. No nothing.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>PRETTY BOY</character>
    <dialogue>I'm telling you, he's never gonna pay.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>That's why we're here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>CHOLO looks out the window to the searchlight sweeping over the military complex in the distance.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT. IMPALA - COUNTRY ROAD - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SLACK drives as RILEY monitors his "Game Boy".</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Shit. He's going to Ross Park.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>What's there?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Powder magazine. Where they keep the big boomers. Rockets. For Dead Reckoning's cannons.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SHED - 10TH STREET PIER - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MOUSE looks at a GRIMY WINDOW as the SHADOW of a WALKER stops just beyond the glass. Mouse FIRES a BURST shattering the window and dropping the Walker. Silence. Mouse takes a tentative step toward the window. A SCRATCHING SOUND. SOMETHING climbs up onto the sill from outside. Mouse raises his gun, but hesitates when he sees... ...it's a child. A GIRL SCOUT. It died at age nine, still wearing its uniform. Now, it's voracious. It grabs Mouse's gun-hand. The weapon FIRES harmlessly into the floor. Mouse is about to be chomped when... ...a STALAGMITE OF GLASS in the top of the shattered window drops, PIERCING the Girl Scout's head. Mouse runs SCREAMING to the door, where he is grabbed by another DEAD THING. And another. As he is TORN APART, he sees that there are DOZENS MORE.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. RIVER - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CRANE UP TO REVEAL:</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>..AN ARMY OF THE DEAD LINING THE RIVERBANK FOR AS FAR AS THE</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>EYE CAN SEE. CLOSE ON: BIG DADDY. Only the river now flows between he and his goal: FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE, so near and yet so far.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. KAUFMAN PENTHOUSE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>WHAM! The door SLAMS behind KAUFMAN as he enters the foyer. KNIPP emerges from the rear.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Any word from Mister Denbo, sir?</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>No. Pack us up. We might have to be leaving.</dialogue>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>In the helicopters?</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>We'll only need one of them.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PRETTY BOY eases the vehicle up the road to the complex of buildings: ROSS PARK, a sprawling munitions depot. The searchlight continues to sweep across the night, but NO ONE is manning it. It's mounted to an automatic rotator on the roof of the main building.</scene_description>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>Looks like no one's here.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The gates stand wide open. There's no sign of life. CHOLO punches a button. The SIDE HATCH HISSES OPEN.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Foxy. You're elected. Get out there and see what the fuck.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Foxy moves out through the open hatch.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Somebody go out and help.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SCAR grabs his weapons.</scene_description>
    <character>SCAR</character>
    <dialogue>I'll go.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. RIVER - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ONE OF THE DEAD TOPPLES face first into the water, dropping out of sight. ANOTHER FALLS. BIG DADDY looks at the spot where his brothers fell in. He looks for a long time, cocking his head like a puppy trying to understand a high wind. The first Dead Thing slowly rises out of the water. Then the Second. They stand, waist deep, in the shallows. Big Daddy gazes down at the water, a concept dawning. Then, with grim purpose, he steps deliberately off the low wall. Hitting the river, he manages to stay on his feet. Standing, waist deep, with the others, he scoops up water with his one good hand. Sniffs it. Tastes it. He looks up. Sees the CITY LIGHTS REFLECTED ON THE RIVER. He tries to express his thoughts. All that comes from his mouth is a series of inarticulate moans. He's incapable of transmitting his idea. So he does what he's been doing since Uniontown. He leads. He walks toward the city. Out of the shallows. Into deep water. Over his head.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. UNDERWATER - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>There are AUTOMOBILE TIRES, GARBAGE CANS, a rusted ANCHOR, a sunken MOTOR BOAT, HUNDREDS of BEER BOTTLES...AND THOUSANDS OF DEAD THINGS...WALKING...ON THE RIVER BOTTOM...following BIG DADDY through the debris.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. TENEMENT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A knock on a door is answered by A MAN who looks a bit too greasy to be important. SUTHERLAND is outside.</scene_description>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>How much is Kaufman paying you and your men?</dialogue>
    <character>GREASY MAN</character>
    <dialogue>Four hundred a day. Each.</dialogue>
    <character>STYLES</character>
    <dialogue>I'll pay you five thousand a day. Each.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. T-BIRD - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The car speeds down the road with SLACK at the wheel.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. T-BIRD - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY looks at his watch. 11:40.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. ROSS PARK AMMUNITION DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The unmanned SEARCHLIGHT scans the yard, casting intermittent shadows.</scene_description>
    <character>SCAR</character>
    <dialogue>This place is important. The men here wouldn't just walk out.</dialogue>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>Maybe they had no choice.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FOXY and SCAR move toward a large STORAGE BUILDING where a door swings in the night breeze, SLAPPING alarmingly against the wall. Beyond the opening is a BLACK MAW, like a velvet curtain, past which nothing can be seen.</scene_description>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>There could be stenches in there. (Readying his M-16) Got a flashlight?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Scar nervously pulls out a flashlight. As he CLICKS on the BEAM, he loses his grip. The flashlight drops to the ground. Scar reaches for it. His fingers tip it and it spins. The beam WASHES across his shoes. Then Foxy's shoes. Then finds... ...ONE OTHER SHOE. Someone else's. Gasping, Scar grabs the flashlight, shining the beam up onto what should be a leg, but there's nothing left above its bloody shin. PLIP! PLOP! PLIP! Beads of BLOOD hit the floor, dropping from the DARK FIGURE of a SOLDIER who is approaching. Scar aims the flashlight at the figure's face, recognizing...</scene_description>
    <character>SCAR</character>
    <dialogue>Brubaker! You okay? Where's the other guys? What happened here?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Brubaker keeps coming. He has BULLET HOLES in his chest, but they're not what's dripping blood. It's another half-eaten FOOT that he's carrying. BRUBAKER IS DEAD. Foxy shoots him. Foxy and Scar move into a hangar-like space. Pitch black. Except for the mote-filled BEAM from Scar's flashlight, which illuminates a supply of enormous cannon shells, lined up on storage shelves. THE "JOHNSONS". SIX DEAD SOLDIERS are hunkered in the shadows, EATING the REMAINS of OTHER DEAD SOLDIERS. Foxy grimly raises his weapon. As he squeezes the trigger, the sound of the gunfire OVERLAPS into...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ANCHOR and SCAR wrestle TWO "JOHNSONS" into place.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>That's good. That's all we need.</dialogue>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>(Sober) To blow up the Green.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT. T-BIRD - HILLSIDE ROAD - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE T-BIRD rumbles along a road lined with large HOMES, once prized for their panoramic views. RILEY'S "Game Boy" BEEPS. The display shows the RED DOT moving along a MAP.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Cholo's moving out. Looks like he's heading right for us.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley looks outside. Beyond the homes he can see THE CITY.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Shit. Off this hillside...they can shell the Green. Pull in! There!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SLACK pulls into a driveway, stopping the T-Bird in the shadow of one of the houses.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>They'll be coming up this road.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. BANK - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In a walk-in STEEL-WALLED SAFE, KAUFMAN pulls out banded STACKS OF MONEY and stuffs them into TWO PRADA DUFFELS.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. BOAT RAMP - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ONE HEAD RISES out of the river. It's BIG DADDY, rivulets of water running down the creases of his face. Another head rises. And another. NUMBER NINE and the BUTCHER ZOMBIE. More and more heads break the surface. The water FILLS with BODIES emerging from the deep. HUNDREDS OF THEM. The CITY LIGHTS REFLECT off their wet clothes as the ARMY OF THE DEAD clambers up a boat ramp on the city side of the river.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. HILLSIDE HOME DRIVEWAY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY and HIS TEAM wait in the shadows of the driveway they pulled into. They HEAR the distant GROWL of DEAD RECKONING. Looking over a hedge-row, Riley can see HIGH BEAMS advancing.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(To the Others) Y'all stay here.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>You're goin' out there alone? You need our guns.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Dead Reckoning's got steel skin an inch thick. You can't shoot your way in. I'm hopin' I can talk my way in.</dialogue>
    <character>MANOLETE</character>
    <dialogue>He's gonna steal the truck and leave us here.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Riley'd never do that. Just look at him, you can tell he'd never do that.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Keep an eye on the hatches. If I get in, I'll try to leave one open.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley takes off. Charlie looks torn. He wants to go with Riley, but he has to keep PILLSBURY and Manolete covered.</scene_description>
    <character>PILLSBURY</character>
    <dialogue>I like dat man. You go help `im. I take care of dis sissy.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Pillsbury, moving fast for a big woman, POUNDS Manolete's temple with a mighty fist. He drops like a lead weight.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. ROOFTOP - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The door to the roof opens and the GREASY MAN from "downtown" steps out of a fire stair with ANOTHER GREASY MAN. SUTHERLAND remains inside the door.</scene_description>
    <character>GREASY MAN</character>
    <dialogue>I don't know about this. I mean...</dialogue>
    <dialogue>leavin' people behind...</dialogue>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>Kaufman was gonna leave people behind. So we're leaving him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Greasy Men go trotting across the rooftop. As they climb into TWO HELICOPTERS, we realize that they are PILOTS.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. HILLSIDE STREET - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY walks down the road. The GROWLING of the diesels is getting louder, the GLOW from the high-beams brighter. Riley is startled by a NOISE behind him. He whirls around and sees CHARLIE approaching.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Everything's cool back there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley is about to object, when DEAD RECKONING comes rumbling around a corner a hundred yards down the street. Riley checks his watch again. 11:52.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Too late to send me back.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Put on your Sunday smile. Try to look friendly.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>I am friendly. Just look at me you can tell I'm friendly.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In the cab, PRETTY BOY eases off the gas. CHOLO looks out the windshield as the headlights strike...</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Denbo. And his idiot. (Beat) Stop. Gimme the mike.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The vehicle crunches to a stop forty yards away. Pretty Boy hands Cholo a microphone. Cholo speaks into it.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>How'd you get up here, Riley?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>INTERCUT: BETWEEN THE STREET AND DEAD RECKONING'S CAB.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Grabbed the T-Bird.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>What are you doin' up here?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Tracking you. With this.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley holds up his "Game Boy". Cholo looks surprised.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Truck's got a little transmitter in her belly. Sorry I never told you.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>You were always a smart guy, Riley. Much smarter'n me.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You went and took off without inviting us along.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>You weren't around to get invited. Anyway, I figured you wouldn't want in on this.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>We want in on anything you got goin'.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>(To Pretty Boy) Open up.</dialogue>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>What're you, nuts?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Open up!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. HILLSIDE HOME DRIVEWAY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SLACK and PILLSBURY watch from the shadows as a HATCH OPENS.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY and CHARLIE step on board. PRETTY BOY is at the controls. FOXY, ANCHOR, and SCAR stand nearby. Charlie is grinning like a badly scarred Cheshire cat.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>The hell you so happy about?</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Riley told me to smile. So's you'd let us come in.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I'd rather have you in here than out there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>KA-CHUNK! Cholo lifts his crossbow, pressing a loaded arrow up under Riley's chin. BLOOD TRICKLES.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Who's the smart one now?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Charlie is about to react when he feels Foxy's M-16 poking into his back. Cholo looks into Riley's eyes.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Thought you were gonna quit. Here you are still working for the man. Kaufman sent you out here, didn't he? To get the truck back.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Yes.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. HILLSIDE HOME DRIVEWAY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SLACK and PILLSBURY creep forward, freezing as they see RILEY with the crossbow at his neck. Slack aims her K-90 at CHOLO, RUSTLING branches as she moves.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>That man pulls the trigger, he's dead.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO cocks his head outside.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Who else is out there?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Kaufman sent some guys with us. We took care of `em. I know you</dialogue>
    <dialogue>been up to Ross Park. Picked up some Johnsons, huh?</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Yup. Pretty Boy, set the cannons.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>With great WHIRRING SOUNDS, the vehicle's largest guns begin to ROTATE slowly toward the city across the river.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>We're running out of time here. C'mon, Riley. Make yourself useful.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>MANOLETE begins to stir on the ground beside THE T-BIRD.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY keeps cool.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Don't do it, Cholo.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Kaufman's got it coming.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SLACK and PILLSBURY watch THE GUN TURRET continue to turn, the cannon barrels angling toward FIDDLER'S GREEN.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PRETTY BOY lifts a clear cover off a RED FIRING BUTTON.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Hit the tower square, you'll kill a lot of innocent people. Miss and hit the city, you'll kill a lot of our friends. Your beef's with Kaufman, not them.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The turret on the roof GROANS as the cannons rotate.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>He's killed a lot of our friends. Every week we took out the garbage, you and me. Every month I took out Kaufman's garbage. People he wanted off the streets. He turned me into a goon and then he pissed all over me! Foxy, keep `em covered.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The turret stops, cannons aimed directly at the GREEN.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO moves to the RED FIRING BUTTON.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>When the smoke clears, I'm gonna roll in, hit the bank, take the money, and pick up any other fancy shit I can get my hands on.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>There won't be any fancy shit left. And money burns.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Not when you keep it in a safe.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MANOLETE pulls one of the MACHINE GUNS out of its mount on the T-BIRD. Shouldering it, he creeps toward DEAD RECKONING.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>ON THE CONTROL PANEL: A CLOCK CLICKS DOWN TO MIDNIGHT. 4...3...2...1...CHOLO reaches down and pushes the button.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The GUN BARRELS are cold. SILENT.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO punches the button again. Again. Nothing happens. WHAT THE FUCK? CHOLO'S eyes fall to the "Game Boy" in Riley's hand.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>You did something, didn't you? With your FUCKING TOY!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley pushes another button on the "Game Boy". Outside...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>...TWO STEEL LOCKING RINGS swing up to cap the cannons. Just beyond the barrels we see MANOLETE closing in on DEAD RECKONING, raising his machine gun. A DEAD THING advances behind him.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO charges RILEY. Grabs him around the throat.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Fix it!</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Not a chance.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley tosses the "Game Boy" out the open hatch. Cholo reaches out after it.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>MANOLETE has the machine gun aimed at DEAD RECKONING'S open hatch. Where CHOLO is standing. Out of the corner of his eye, RILEY sees Manolete's machine gun barrel flash in the moonlight. MANOLETE FIRES! RATATAT! RILEY PUSHES CHOLO OUT OF THE WAY JUST IN TIME! He drops from the hatch onto the pavement, wounded in the shoulder. The Walker starts to rip Manolete apart. Slack SHOOTS HIM in the head. Then she and PILLSBURY open fire on the Walker, destroying it.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>FOXY, distracted by the mayhem, lets CHARLIE get the drop on him. ANCHOR and SCAR go for their guns. RILEY unslings his M-16 and holds them at bay.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Easy boys.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley looks at the clock on the control panel. 12:01. Charlie follows his gaze.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Geez. We just made it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley CLICKS the transmitter on.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Riley Denbo calling the Green.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. PENTHOUSE CORRIDOR - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>BING! KAUFMAN steps off the elevator, carrying his two Prada bags full of money. A TWO-WAY RADIO in his pocket RINGS.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>(Into radio, urgent) Yes?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>We got Cholo.</dialogue>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>(Sagging with relief) I owe you, Mister Denbo.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I'm glad you feel that way. Because I'm taking your fucking truck.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. KAUFMAN'S PENTHOUSE - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>KAUFMAN rushes in with his bags, dropping them beside other luggage that is already packed.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>(Frightened) Mister Kaufman, sir. I dunno what's happening, sir, but it sounds bad.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The windows are sealed so the NOISE Kaufman hears is MUFFLED, but it is definitely the SOUND OF DISORDER. He goes to a window. Looks down and sees... ...flashes of LIGHT from gunfire. SMOKE rising from an EXPLOSION. PEOPLE running. THE DEAD swarming into the city like ants. A war has begun.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. ROOFTOP - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SUTHERLAND stands at the edge of the roof, looking down at what Kaufman just saw.</scene_description>
    <character>SUTHERLAND</character>
    <dialogue>All this time Kaufman's been</dialogue>
    <dialogue>worried about a revolution on the streets. He never thought it would come from across the river.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Sutherland, STYLES, OTHER BOARD MEMBERS, and their FAMILIES get into the TWO HELICOPTERS.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. KAUFMAN'S PENTHOUSE - FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE SOUND OF RUMBLING. The CEILING VIBRATES, knocking tear- shaped baubles off a CHANDELIER. The SOUND BUILDS in intensity. Then suddenly eases off. Through the window, KAUFMAN sees the things that caused the rumbling... ...TWO HELICOPTERS, SOARING off into the night.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>No. No. They can't leave. Not without me!</dialogue>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>I think they just did, sir.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - HILLSIDE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY jumps out onto the street where CHOLO lies, bleeding from the top of his left shoulder.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I hate you, Riley. There's something about you I've always fucking hated.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(Smiling) Same here.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Riley. Look out there.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley looks where SLACK is pointing. From across the river comes a flickering ORANGE GLOW. Riley moves to a spot where he can see between the houses on the hillside. In the distance, FIRE rises from the city. Cholo sits up, cackling.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I didn't have to blow the fucking place up. Somebody else did for me!</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>(Stunned) The stenches. They got across the river. They got across the fucking river. (To the others) Get him inside.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PILLSBURY steps in and lifts Cholo easily to his feet.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Wait, wait, wait. What are we doin'? Where we goin'?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Back to the city.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Not this horse. You got the T-Bird?</dialogue>
    <dialogue>I'll take that.</dialogue>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>Me, too.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>FOXY jumps out of DEAD RECKONING and stands at Cholo's side. Riley, Slack, and Pillsbury climb aboard. Riley looks down at Cholo and Foxy.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>You guys'd be safer coming with us.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Nah, you'd never let me have any fun.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>T-Bird's down that driveway over there. Guns and ammo inside.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Thanks.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY closes the hatch. Blood trickles from under his chin where Cholo stuck him with the crossbow. SLACK reaches up and pulls off the bandana that holds back her hair, which cascades down. She uses the fabric to clean the blood off Riley's neck. He looks at her, touched by the familiarity of the gesture.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Almost lost you there.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>I don't get lost so easy. (To PRETTY BOY) We gotta get across the water.</dialogue>
    <character>PRETTY BOY</character>
    <dialogue>The bridges into the city are all bricked up.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>PRETTY BOY hits a button. A MAP appears on a MONITOR, showing the "GOLDEN TRIANGLE" bordered by the rivers and the barricaded bridges spanning them.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>We could blast our way through.</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Don't want to. If the stenches got</dialogue>
    <dialogue>in, there's a war going on in the city. We take any of those bridges we'll end up right in the middle of it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley runs his finger along the monitor, outlining the natural and man-made barriers that protect the triangle.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>We've gotta come in above the throat.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>His finger continues down the monitor to "THE THROAT" at the base of the triangle, where the long FENCE runs between the two rivers.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>What was built to keep folks safe is gonna trap them inside. We've gotta give them a way out.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. FIDDLER'S GREEN - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CLOSE ON: KAUFMAN staring out his PENTHOUSE WINDOW, aghast. LICKS OF FIRE reflect on the glass. SOUNDS OF WAR can be heard from far below.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. "GOLDEN TRIANGLE" - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>In the pristine plaza that surrounds the building, WALKERS swarm. CITIZENS run, screaming, including SOLDIERS, driven from their posts, who SHOOT at the Dead Things. CLOSE ON BIG DADDY. Who looks back and forth, as if torn, at the FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE, at the violence in the streets, back at the building, back at the streets. A SOLDIER fires at him! Misses. Big Daddy raises his rifle and blows him away.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. HILLSIDE HOME DRIVEWAY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO and FOXY run up the road to THE T-BIRD. Seeing a WALKER lurking ahead, they duck into the dark cover of the trees.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I got it.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>WFFFFT! Cholo picks off the Walker with his crossbow.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Come on, let's go.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>He slaps a hand on Foxy's back. EXCEPT IT'S NOT FOXY! It's ANOTHER WALKER that has moved between the two men. It grabs the hand that slapped him and BITES it. AHHH...FUCK! Foxy, a few yards away, whirls, aiming his gun at the Walker. Cholo is faster. With no time to reload, in agony, he pulls a FISTFUL OF ARROWS from his quiver and DRIVES THEM THROUGH THE WALKER'S FACE AND SKULL. The Walker falls. So does an ominous silence.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I can't fucking believe it. (A sad chuckle) Nothin' works out. It's like...the world is spinning around and we're just...caught in the wind. Nothin' works out. Some damn thing always comes around the corner and gets you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Foxy aims his rifle Fat Cholo's forehead. Their eyes connect.</scene_description>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>Your choice.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>For a moment, Cholo looks despondent. Then he forces a smile.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>No, don't shoot. (A dark chuckle) always wanted to see how the other half lives.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Foxy lowers his gun.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Take the car and get outa here.</dialogue>
    <character>FOXY</character>
    <dialogue>I'll get outa here. You take the car.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT./EXT. DEAD RECKONING - RIVER ROAD - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>EAD RECKONING drives upriver. THROUGH THE WINDSHIELD: THE CITY can be seen BURNING in the distance.</scene_description>
    <character>PRETTY BOY</character>
    <dialogue>The old J&L'll take us over. Right outside the throat.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>A drawbridge spans the river. Or would span it if it wasn't open, its rusted metal roadbed rising into the sky.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Gotta get it down.</dialogue>
    <character>PRETTY BOY</character>
    <dialogue>The controls are in that booth up there.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. CONTROL BOOTH - J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY'S POV: A CONTROL BOOTH is built into the superstructure of the bridge, about fifteen feet off the ground, on DEAD RECKONING'S side of the river.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY jumps out of DEAD RECKONING. SLACK is right behind him.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Get back in there. What are you doing?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BLAM! She shoots a WALKER that has come out of the night.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Making myself useful.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEPOT - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO jumps out of the T-BIRD and runs to the steel doors, unlocking them with a mag-key.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. SUBWAY TUNNEL - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHOLO walks with determination along the deserted tracks under the river.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY ducks under a caution gate at the entrance to the bridge and starts across the roadway. Behind him... ...SLACK and CHARLIE stand, weapons ready, eyes alert for danger. As Riley runs... ...SOMETHING SKITTERS across the road, chasing him. Not a zombie. Much smaller. A RIVER RAT. Charlie draws his REMINGTON. Wets the sight with his thumb. BLAM! Riley stops running. Looks back to see what's being shot.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>You missed.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Nope. I blew its ass off.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The rat is now half a rat. Its ass has been blown off. Yet IT'S STILL RUNNING!</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Just didn't hit it in the head.</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>(Realizing) Jesus. It's dead.</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>They all are.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>SKREEEEEEEE! ZOMBIE RATS crawl up onto the roadbed. DOZENS. Riley takes off away from them. Slack and Charlie hurry closer, firing, trying to pick the critters off. The rats reach Riley! Nip at his heels. He leaps. Swings onto a girder. Climbs to the control booth. The rats don't follow. Slack heaves a sigh of relief just before... ...SKREEEEEEEE! A second pack of rats scurries toward her! She vaults over a railing, dropping several feet to... ...the riverbank below. But there are rats here too! Charlie fires at them from above. BLAM! BLAM! BLAM! FUR AND BLOOD FLY. But there are too many. He can't shoot them all.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. CONTROL BOOTH - J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY reaches the control booth. Draws his .45, expecting danger within. He steps through the opening... ...but nothing's there. Just a SPIDER WEB that sweeps over his face as he moves toward a RED SWITCH that activates a generator. He flips it. The motor roars to life. He turns toward a giant lever that operates the roadbed. It GROANS from disuse as he pulls it.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RED LIGHTS on the caution gates BLINK, tinting the night. The silence is shattered by a LOUD SIREN that ECHOES across the river. The bridge's roadbed begins to CREAK down slowly.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. RIVERBANK - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THREE DINGHIES lie, upside down, next to the water's edge. SLACK shoves one into the river, climbing onto its upturned bottom. She pushes off. The boat doesn't budge. A tether holds it within inches of the shore. Slack pulls out a jackknife and goes to cut the rope, but... ...rats SNAP at her hands. Slack recoils, but keeps cutting. Finally, the rope frays, enough for the boat to pull free. Slack crouches on top of the upturned hull. No way to steer. No paddles. The current carrying her away.</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Slack!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. CONTROL BOOTH - J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Hearing the scream, RILEY looks out the control booth window and sees... ...SLACK being taken downstream.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY bursts out of the booth, only to be confronted by... ...the BRIDGEKEEPER. Drooling. Dead. It grabs Riley, pushing his head back toward the enormous GEARWORKS of the bridge. Riley struggles. Bests the creature. Spins him around toward the gearworks and... ...SSSNIPPPP! THE BRIDGEKEEPER'S HEAD is scissored off! It drops with a PLUNK into the river below.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. RIVER - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SLACK, adrift on the boat, lies prone at the bow and begins to paddle with her hands. One of which hits something long and slimy. It looks like a snake! But it's not. It's only a moss-covered rope. Slack grabs on. Pulls hand over hand. It seems to take forever for the rope to become taut. A FACE BOBS OUT OF THE WATER! Slack SCREAMS. It's the BRIDGEKEEPER'S HEAD, its eyes blinking as it floats off on the current. The rope is attached to a stanchion on the opposite shore. Slack's muscles strain as she pulls on it until... ...her boat reaches the stanchion and she jumps off, finding herself at the same boat ramp the army of the dead used. The river has carried her into the very part of the city Riley and the team were trying to avoid. SCREAMS rise nearby. She's in the war zone.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THE BRIDGE IS LOWERING SLOWLY. Too slowly. RILEY scrambles up the incline of the roadbed and calls back to CHARLIE.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Bring her over as soon as you can!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Charlie pops back into DEAD RECKONING. Riley climbs to the top of the descending roadbed and... ...LEAPS across the narrowing gulf to the other side. He lands. Falls. Rolls. Gets to his feet and runs toward Slack and the city.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. "GOLDEN TRIANGLE" - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>SLACK runs past hysterical PEOPLE toward the FIDDLER'S GREEN HIGH-RISE. BRIAN, Mulligan's young son, rushes by her in a panic. Slack grabs him.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>Brian!</dialogue>
    <character>BRIAN</character>
    <dialogue>We can't get out! There's no way out!</dialogue>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>There will be. Come with me.</dialogue>
    <character>BRIAN</character>
    <dialogue>Daddy! Daddy's still locked up.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Slack runs off with Brian, past a MANHOLE surrounded by canvas fences, "CAUTION" signs, and flaming OIL POTS. As MAINTENANCE WORKERS scramble out of the manhole... ...DEAD THINGS close in. The Workers, unarmed, pick up the ball-shaped pots and BOWL them at the Walkers. As the "balls" roll, their FIRES SWIRL, making them look like flaming comets. S Some of the pots CRACK OPEN, creating POOLS OF FIRE on the street. One of the "balls" remains whole until it smacks against the feet of a Walker. Then it opens. And the Walker is engulfed in flames. Big Daddy looks at the Walker with sadness. He lifts his rifle again and shoots the flaming creature in the head. Big Daddy walks to the manhole. TOOLS are strewn around it, pickaxes, sledges, chainsaws, and a pneumatic hammer which is lying on the street...RATTATATTAT...still running. Big Daddy looks at the FIDDLER'S GREEN SKYSCRAPER. His goal. Finally in reach. He looks down at the pneumatic hammer, and picks it up by the handle. With the heavy tool vibrating in its hand, Big Daddy walks toward the building. He doesn't get very far before the hammer's electrical cord is pulled out of the extension it's plugged into. The hammer stops running. Big Daddy looks at it. Puzzles over its stillness for a moment. Then...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>..he looks at the building. At its doors, abandoned by guards. Doors that are made of glass.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The barrel of an M-16 is planted against Big Daddy's temple by a MILITIAMAN. UDDA-BUDDA-BUDDA! The Militiaman FLIES BACK. It wasn't he who fired. It was NUMBER NINE, standing nearby with her M-16. The Militiaman lies on the ground, his dead eyes staring at Number NINE in utter surprise. Seeing what has happened, ANOTHER SOLDIER grabs a grenade, pulls the pin, and is about to toss it at Big Daddy when...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>..his HAND IS CUT OFF at the wrist by a meat clever held by THE BUTCHER. The Soldier's hand, still clutching the grenade,</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PLOPS into the street. The Soldier looks down in horror, then collapses on top of his hand. A MUFFLED EXPLOSION makes jelly of his mid-section. Big Daddy continues to walk toward the building, carrying the pneumatic hammer, as OTHER DEAD THINGS collect sledges, pickaxes, lengths of pipe, and follow their leader.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. FIDDLER'S GREEN ATRIUM - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>KAUFMAN and KNIPP, carrying the Prada duffles, rush out of an elevator with FOUR SECURITY GUARDS. Kaufman carries a gun. hey race into the street level of the three-story ATRIUM. Chopin LILTS, caged birds SING. RESIDENTS SCREAM, running crazily in all directions. A bank of GLASS DOORS leading to the street is under assault by WALKERS, ten deep.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>They can't get in. Downstairs.</dialogue>
    <dialogue>The car.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Dead Things POUND at the doors. One Guard runs away. The Other Three follow.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Get back here! GET BACK HERE!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman FIRES THREE ROUNDS at the men! He's not a marksman, but ONE of the GUARDS is WINGED. Whirls around and levels his M-16 at Kaufman. YOU STUPID OLD FUCK! He's about to fire when Knipp steps in front of Kaufman.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>DON'T SHOOT! (Grabbing Kaufman's gun hand) Boss? Don't you shoot, neither. We're all on the same side. Least we're supposed to be.</dialogue>
    <character>SECURITY GUARD</character>
    <dialogue>I'm on my own side now.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The Guard takes off after his comrades.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>Need some help, Mister K.?</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman spins around to see CHOLO walking toward him across the atrium.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Been bit, Mister K. I'm a dead man, so I don't care about nothin' no more. Still care about you, though. I wanna make sure you come to the same end as me.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>LANG! CLANG! CLANG! The Dead Things at the glass doors are POUNDING now with shovels, pickaxes, and lengths of pipe.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>They're going to get you, Mister K. want them to get you.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman raises his gun and aims at Cholo, who aims back with his crossbow.</scene_description>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>Put it down, old man, unless you'd rather die right now.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>BIG DADDY appears outside the doors. Uses his pneumatic hammer to POUND at the safety glass. Kaufman can't take it anymore. He bolts for a stairway door. Cholo shoots. An arrows hits Kaufman in the back of his left calf. Kaufman sprawls, dropping both his bag of money and his gun, which skitters away. Knipp rushes over to help Kaufman.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Just let us go, Mister DeMora. Let us get out of here.</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>(Calmly reloading) You can go, Knipp, but not him.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman shakes Knipp off. His gun is ten feet away. He heads for it. Dragging himself on hands and knees. CRUNCH! The chisel on Big Daddy's pneumatic hammer is the first tool to PENETRATE the doors. The glass doesn't shatter; it COBWEBS into tiny crystals stuck together by a thin plasticine coating. ALARM BELLS SOUND! Puzzled by the sudden transformation of the glass into something that looks different, Big Daddy drops the pneumatic hammer and reaches out. The glass is different. It's soft. Flexible. Big Daddy POKES HIS HAND right through. Kaufman has almost reached his gun. Cholo shoots another arrow. This one hits Kaufman in the shoulder.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>You fucking spic bastard!</dialogue>
    <character>CHOLO</character>
    <dialogue>I think we should talk when you're a little less excited.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman has a will of iron. He keeps going, gritting his teeth against the pain, reaching out for his gun, as... CRUNCH! CRUNCH! CRUNCH! More tools PENETRATE the doors. More HANDS POKE through. Kaufman looks at his worst nightmare...Dead Things ripping their way through the cobwebbed doors, invading his temple. The commotion distracts Cholo just long enough for Kaufman to lift his gun and FIRE nine rounds. Most of the shots miss. TWO hit Cholo, one in the belly, one in the heart. He is slammed against the wall, his glazing eyes staring up into the atrium, the place he so desired. It's the last thing he sees before he keels over, dead. Knipp pulls Kaufman onto his feet. They look up to see... BIG DADDY leading his army into the atrium. Kaufman aims and FIRES. A BULLET HITS BIG DADDY in the upper chest, blowing DEAD FLESH out of his back. The Dead Man feels no pain, but it focuses on Kaufman and starts after him with purpose. Kaufman sees something in Big Daddy's eyes. Something that's not dead. Kaufman fires again. CLICK! He's out of ammo.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Boss. We gotta get outa here!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Knipp pulls Kaufman to a stairway door. They rush inside. The moment they're out of sight, the Walkers forget about them, moving on into the atrium. All except Big Daddy. That rage is still in its face as he lumbers toward the stairway door.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. J&L DRAWBRIDGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>TH-BOOOOM! The roadbed of the drawbridge drops into place. VROOOM! DEAD RECKONING rumbles across the span.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. JAIL - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>KEYS TURN in the locks of cell doors, which SLACK and BRIAN pull open. MULLIGAN and his REVOLUTIONARIES emerge. Mulligan embraces his son and looks gratefully at Slack.</scene_description>
    <character>MULLIGAN</character>
    <dialogue>(To his men) Let's go get our guns, boys.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. NEAR THE "THROAT" - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY runs out of a line of trees. In the distance, he sees... ...the "THROAT", where much of the CITY'S POPULATION is trapped, herded by HUNDREDS OF WALKING DEAD against the layers of electrified fencing that were erected to protect them. There's no escape. People are being TORN apart and EATEN. The fencing SPARKS as bodies touch it and are ELECTROCUTED. Terrible SCREAMS fill the air. Riley hears the distinctive ROAR of DEAD RECKONING'S engines, the CLATTER of its treads. He moves toward the sound as... ..a DEAD THING looms three feet away. Riley lifts his pistol and puts a shell through the thing's skull. Blood flies, taking on the sudden glow of a halo as it is BACKLIT by... ...the glare of DEAD RECKONING'S approaching headlights. The dead thing falls to the road, where... ...it is turned to apple butter by Dead Reckoning's enormous treads. Riley stands right in the vehicle's path.</scene_description>
    <character>PRETTY BOY (O.S. LOUDSPEAKER)</character>
    <dialogue>Get outa the way, Riley!</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THROUGH THE WINDSHIELD: RILEY looms larger and larger as the vehicle closes in. He doesn't move. PRETTY BOY tries to turn the wheel. Too late. RILEY DISAPPEARS!</scene_description>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>(Pure anguish) RILEY!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Three seconds later, Riley's figure comes scrambling across the windshield, climbing up toward...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>...the two fourteen-inch cannons on the vehicle's turrets.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>We gotta blow the fences!</dialogue>
    <character>PRETTY BOY (O.S. LOUDSPEAKER)</character>
    <dialogue>Johnson's are loaded!</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Yeah, but they're capped!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>The barrels of the two fourteen-inchers are still capped. DEAD RECKONING keeps rolling. RILEY climbs out onto one of the cannon barrels. WHAM! A WALKER grabs him by the leg from the road. Riley blasts him with his .45. As OTHER WALKERS approach, he shoots them with one hand, Rusing the other to uncap the cannon.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Number One is clear! I'm going for Number Two!</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE (O.S. LOUDSPEAKER)</character>
    <dialogue>I don't norm'lly need two shots, Riley.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley turns. The road is now filled with WALKERS. Standing ASTRIDE the vehicle, riding it as if it were a living beast, Riley picks some of them of with his .45.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. FIDDLER'S GREEN PARKING GARAGE - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>FOOTSTEPS ECHO as KNIPP, carrying one of the Prada duffles, helps the wounded KAUFMAN across an underground PARKING GARAGE, a dark and spooky place, made more so by the SOUNDS of distant SCREAMING. Kaufman disdainfully SNAPS OFF the shanks of the arrows in his leg and shoulder. The two men reach a stretch LINCOLN. Knipp BEEPS the doors open and they get inside, Knipp behind the wheel, Kaufman in the luxurious back compartment, where he pours himself a scotch from the built-in bar. Knipp starts the engine. The SOUND ECHOES big-time in the concrete tomb.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>(Looking at the fuel gauge) We need gas.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Kaufman moans. Knipp steers the car slowly, carefully through the shadows, pulling in beside a GASOLINE PUMP near the base of a RAMP that leads up to the street. Knipp pushes a button that pops open the gas tank. He shuts the engine off and gets out, taking the keys, which have a Mag-Card attached to them. He slides the Mag-Card into a slot, activating the pump. An LED scrolls "Thank you, Mr. Kaufman". Knipp pulls the nozzle. Freezes when he hears... ...FOOTSTEPS ECHOING. A DARK FIGURE is approaching through the shadows. Knipp drops the nozzle. Ducks into the car. SLAMS the door. WHAM! A SINGLE HAND SMACKS against the driver-side window. A FACE leans in behind the hand. A face full of rage. BIG DADDY'S FACE.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Shoot it! Shoot the damn thing!</dialogue>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>You didn't gimme no gun, sir.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Big Daddy moves to one of the rear windows. He can't see inside. The window is tinted. He returns to the clear windshield, looks back, at an angle, and sees Kaufman in the rear compartment. Big Daddy recognizes him. From upstairs. It's the man who shot him. The Dead Thing looks up. Sees the gasoline pump. His hand drops to the embroidery on its jump-suit..."Texaco". He moves deliberately toward the pump.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>Pull out! PULL OUT!</dialogue>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Sorry, sir. Keys are in the pump.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Big Daddy sees the nozzle on the cement. Picks it up, feeling the familiarity of it. Pulls the trigger. Gasoline squirts. The rage in his face turns to a kind of satisfaction. Using the nozzle as he did the pneumatic hammer, Big Daddy POUNDS on the windshield, three times, before the SAFETY GLASS COBWEBS. He POKES the nozzle through the flexible fabric and pulls the trigger until it locks. Gasoline FLOODS into the car.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>Lord!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>TCHUNG! Big Daddy pulls the driver side door open. As Knipp tries to run, he is GRABBED by Big Daddy.</scene_description>
    <character>KNIPP</character>
    <dialogue>LORD!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Big Daddy looks at the butler. Sniffs him. Then flings him aside. Knipp is not his prey. With a glance at Kaufman, cowering in the back seat, Big Daddy slams the car door and, surprisingly, walks away. Up the ramp toward the street. The nozzle remains stuck in the "fabric" of the windshield. Gasoline continues to flow into the car. Kaufman crawls into the front seat, wincing from his wounds, and KICKS the nozzle out of the window with his good leg, getting soaked with gas in the process. He opens the door. Limps to the pump. Grabs the keys. As he starts back toward the car... ...WHAM! SOMETHING is standing right in front of him. It's one of the WALKING DEAD. It's...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>..CHOLO.</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>Kaufman shakes his head in disbelief.</scene_description>
    <character>KAUFMAN</character>
    <dialogue>N-no, y-you're dead. (Realization dawning) Oh my God. You're dead!</dialogue>
    <scene_description>THE CHOLO THING reaches for Kaufman, vengeance in its eyes. Kaufman breaks for the driver's door. He never makes it. The Cholo Thing grabs him and SLAMS him down across the hood. Leans over him. Opens a drooling mouth. Kaufman whimpers. BRRRUMBLE-UMBLE-UMBLE! The SOUND of a bowling ball. Kaufman looks up. It's not a bowling ball. It's an OIL POT, rolled down the ramp by Big Daddy. Kaufman SCREAMS. The fire ball approaches the gas-soaked Lincoln, the gas-soaked Kaufman, and... ...WHOOOMPH! Kaufman and The Cholo Thing are IMMOLATED. The FIREBALL removes everything from sight, except a few floating HUNDRED DOLLAR BILLS, burning in mid-air. THROUGH LICKS OF FLAME we see...Big Daddy is almost smiling.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. "THE THROAT" - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>DEAD RECKONING approaches the electrified fences from beyond.</scene_description>
    <character>PRETTY BOY (O.S. LOUDSPEAKER)</character>
    <dialogue>Get back! Get back! We're gonna blow the fences! The CROWD screams and starts to clear the area.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHARLIE works a joystick. The cannon turret GRINDS above. He takes aim at an area of the fences that is rapidly emptying of people.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE "THROAT" - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>The fourteen-incher turns toward the fences. RILEY rides it.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Shoot!</dialogue>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Okay, but you best get off the gun.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley leaps down. The instant he's clear... KA-BLOOOOOOOOOOOOOM. The ELECTRIFIED FENCES are BLOWN APART. In the dissipating SMOKE, RILEY is the first one through the opening. Within seconds, CITIZENS start toward it, heading the other way. Riley finds himself running against the tide. Searching. Desperately searching. Behind the surging crowd... ...WALKERS appear, grabbing people. Dropping them to the ground. Eating them. Riley FIRES in all directions. WALKERS DROP around him. He saves a WOMAN with a BABY...a YOUNG COUPLE...a PRIEST. CLICK. He runs out of ammo. WALKERS close in. The situation seems hopeless until...</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>CHARLIE hits a button on the console.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. THE "THROAT" - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PTOOOM! PTOOOM! FIREWORKS "BLOOM" in the sky. HE DEAD THINGS gaze upward, mesmerized. THE HUMANS ESCAPE. RILEY finds himself standing in the midst of FIFTY WALKERS, frozen like statues around him. Other than the intermittent BOOM of the fireworks, SILENCE. Out of which...</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK (O.S.)</character>
    <dialogue>(A whisper) Riley.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley turns. Slack emerges from behind one of the immobile dead things. Riley moves toward her... ...she to him... ...both of them weaving a cautious path between the statues. They reach each other and embrace, surrounded by dead things that don't even know they are there. RATATATATATAT. GUNFIRE EXPLODES around them! HAPLESS DEAD THINGS are MOWED DOWN the way they were back in Uniontown. This time by... ...MULLIGAN and his REVOLUTIONARIES...who slaughter every zombie in the area. BRIAN is shooting, too, raring to go. When it's all over...</scene_description>
    <character>MULLIGAN</character>
    <dialogue>We could still use you, Riley.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley looks out at the city, where there is still scattered distant gunfire. He looks at Brian, standing at Mulligan's side, his innocent face speckled with the blood of the dead. Riley shakes his head.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>It's all yours, Mulligan.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. OUTSIDE THE CITY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>FIREWORKS EXPLODE. A ZOMBIE looks up toward the "blooms". A strong hand grabs the collar of its shirt, pulls its gaze away from the sky, and herds it onward. The hand is BIG DADDY'S. He herds OTHERS along, too. A small group of TWO DOZEN, including NUMBER NINE and the BUTCHER.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>One of the GATTLING GUNS RATCHETS into position, taking aim at BIG DADDY.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>PRETTY BOY sits at the controls, about to push the firing button when... ...RILEY grabs her hand.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>Stop.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>Riley picks up a pair of binoculars and looks through the windshield at BIG DADDY.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. OUTSIDE THE CITY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>THROUGH THE BINOCULARS: BIG DADDY looks at DEAD RECKONING. For an instant, his eyes meet Riley's, as they did in Uniontown.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>RILEY lowers the binoculars.</scene_description>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>All they want is somewhere to go. Same as us.</dialogue>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>EXT. OUTSIDE THE CITY - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <scene_description>BIG DADDY leads his band into the future. DEAD RECKONING rolls into the future, too, but in a different direction.</scene_description>
  </scene>
  <scene>
    <stage_direction>INT. DEAD RECKONING - NIGHT</stage_direction>
    <character>CHARLIE</character>
    <dialogue>Canada. That's where we're goin', ain't it, Riley?</dialogue>
    <character>RILEY</character>
    <dialogue>If no one has any objections.</dialogue>
    <scene_description>ANCHOR, SCAR, and PILLSBURY all shrug. Riley looks at Slack.</scene_description>
    <character>SLACK</character>
    <dialogue>No, we'll take you along with us.</dialogue>
